author: Unknown
title: World of Hurt: Abolitionist Reflections on the Root Causes of Harm
content:
What causes people to harm others? Reactionaries label certain individuals—or, worse, entire demographics—inherently harmful to justify their own efforts to inflict harm via vigilante attacks, policing, and the court system. Others suggest that experiencing harm can lead some to harm others, as suggested by the common catchphrase “Hurt people hurt people.” Here, we examine this popular notion and propose a more useful framework for understanding the root causes of harm.


Today, a ruling class headed by billionaires and aspiring autocrats is making

the celebration of violence

 central to their narratives and policies, openly campaigning against empathy itself. In this context, the question of what causes harm—and how to interrupt it without reinforcing cycles of hurt and oppression—has become increasingly urgent.


World of Hurt


Abolitionists

 who envision a world without

police

 or

prisons

 often face questions about how to address serious forms of interpersonal harm.

Mutual aid

 and resource redistribution may reduce behaviors that arise as a consequence of lack of access to basic needs. But how can we understand those who seem to hurt others out of cruelty or disregard? If we don’t accept the idea that some people are monsters who must be locked up to keep the rest of us safe, how can we make sense of their actions?


Defenders of the criminal legal system frequently cite rape and abuse to justify prisons and imprisonment. In response, abolitionists have devoted considerable energy to developing

alternative approaches

 to addressing sexual violence. Groups such as Generation Five have proposed

principles for responding to child sexual abuse

 through transformative justice frameworks. By focusing on one of the most stigmatized forms of harm, they aim to cut to the root of

carceral thinking

 in order to reimagine safety and justice.


But creative responses beyond the state are not enough. To end sexual violence, we also need to understand its root causes.


Feminist activists coined the term “

rape culture

” to describe how social norms and institutions enable sexual harm. In addition to these structural effects of gender and power, others argue that past experiences of harm shape the behavior of individuals who go on to harm others. One of the most common ways to articulate this principle appears in the phrase “

Hurt people hurt people

.”


Let’s take a closer look to see where this popular saying came from, how it is used, and its implications for an abolitionist understanding of harm.


The Trajectory of a Slogan


From

self-help books

 and

therapist blogs

 to the

writings of abolitionist activists

, “hurt people hurt people” has become an influential account of the psychology of violence. It suggests that some people harm others not because they are pathological monsters, but because they too are victims whose unresolved trauma shapes their hurtful actions.


The precise origins of the phrase are opaque, but it has been in circulation

at least since the 1950s

. It seems to have begun trending in the 1990s in therapeutic and pop psychology circles. A popular 1993 Christian self-help book titled

Hurt People Hurt People

 promised to support readers in healing from painful past relationships “with empathy and biblical insight.” In recent years, this phrase has been repeated by everyone from megachurch pastor Rick Warren to Hollywood actor Andrew Garfield to the stripper con artist character Destiny in the movie

Hustlers

 to

the metal band Mudvayne

. It appears most widely in discourse about therapy, self-help, trauma, and religion.


On the surface, “hurt people hurt people” might seem an odd slogan for radical critics of the

prison industrial complex

. As a maxim of folk wisdom that spans mainstream, religious, feminist, and radical circles, we should consider carefully whether it aligns with our values.


In some ways, it makes sense that abolitionists would find this formulation promising. It humanizes people who cause harm, whereas dehumanizing them paves the way for carceral responses. It attributes the roots of harmful behavior not to inherent depravity, but to contingent circumstances that can be changed. It resonates with the lived experiences of some people who are struggling to heal and to be accountable for hurting others. It seems to offer a hopeful pathway towards a world without sexual violence by intervening in support of those who have been harmed in order to …

author: MissyRedaktion
title: Der neue Medienpass
content:
Wir verbünden uns mit GoodImpact, Krautreporter, Übermedien und Surplus und launchen den Medienpass, mit dem du auf alle digitalen Inhalte von allen fünf Publikationen zugreifen. Das haben wir vor:

Gemeinsam mit GoodImpact, Krautreporter, Übermedien und Surplus launchen wir den neuen Medienpass. Dieser erlaubt dir, unbegrenzt auf alle digitalen Inhalte von allen fünf Publikationen zugreifen.

im Probe-Pass: 90 Tage lang als Jahrespass: 365 Tage lang

Und das für nur 15 Euro im Monat!

Fernab großer Verlage gibt es im deutschsprachigen Raum eine vielfältige, unabhängige Medienlandschaft – mit vielen tollen Inhalten.

Das Problem: Bisher bedeutete jedes neue Angebot auch ein weiteres Abo. Mehrere unabhängige Medien zu lesen und zu unterstützen, geht schnell ins Geld. Auf Dauer wird das schlicht zu teuer und zwingt zur Qual der Wahl. Das Ergebnis: Du verpasst spannenden Content bei anderen – und wir viele Leser*innen!

Das ändern wir jetzt: Mit dem Medienpass kannst du für einen günstigen Preis deinen Horizont erweitern und fünf unabhängige Medien supporten. Denn in Zeiten von Desinformation, KI-Slop und aufgeheizten Diskursen braucht es deren kritische Berichterstattung ganz besonders!

Mit dem Medienpass hast du Zugang zu den Themen, Expertisen und Perspektiven von fünf Medien, die sich für kritische Berichterstattung, verlässliche Fakten und eine starke Demokratie engagieren.

Der Medienpass kostet einmalig 180€ für ein Jahr oder 53€ für 90 Tage – das sind nur 15 € im Monat und über 50% preiswerter als die jeweiligen Einzelabos der fünf Medien kombiniert. (Wenn dir das zu viel ist: Wir freuen uns auch sehr, wenn du ein reguläres Missy Online-Abo für 5€/Monat abschließt.)

Uns kennst du ja schon <3 Wir stehen seit 18 Jahren für queeren und intersektionalen Feminismus in Pop, Kultur und Politik. Die Missy erscheint alle zwei Monate in Print und Online. Unser Online-Angebot umfasst zusätzlich mehr als 4000 feministische Texte zu Pop, Kultur und Politik sowie den Pissy Podcast.

Die Plattformen berichten seit 2010 konstruktiv über gute Ideen und Lösungen. Getragen wird ihre Arbeit aktuell von ca. 6.000 Menschen, die uns durch eine Good Membership und freiwillige Beiträge unterstützen.

Das genossenschaftliche Online-Magazin wird von über 15.000 Mitgliedern getragen. Die Redaktion berichtet seit 2014 ohne Drama und tiefgründig über Bildungspolitik, Klima und weitere aktuelle Themen.

Seit zehn Jahren ist das Team die Instanz für Medienkritik. Getragen wird das Online-Magazin von 7.000 Abonnent:innen.

Surplus ist das Wirtschaftsmagazin, das sich um die Interessen der großen Mehrheit und nicht der Reichsten dreht. Täglich veröffentlicht Surplus Texte, wöchentlich Video- und Podcastformate und zweimonatlich ein digitales sowie gedrucktes Magazin.

Bestehende Abos werden angerechnet Wenn du bereits ein Missy Online-Abo hast (oder auch ein Abo bei einer der anderen Medien), wird dir dieses angerechnet. Das System erkennt nämlich deine e-Mail Adresse wieder. Das heißt: Du musst für Abos, die du schon hast, nicht doppelt zahlen!

Der Medienpass ist kein Abo Die Laufzeit vom Medienpass ist ein Jahr. Es gibt keine automatische Verlängerung. Und wenn du dir noch nicht ganz sicher bist: Mit dem Probe-Pass kannst du 90 Tage lang testen, ob dir der Medienpass taugt.

Erstmal nur für jetzt Das Angebot ist zeitlich befristet und endet am 6. Januar 2027

Faire Verteilung Alle Einnahmen werden gerecht zwischen den fünf Medien aufgeteilt. Jedes Medium bleibt absolut eigenständig.

We <3 Community Statt (vermeintlich) gegeneinander zu konkurrieren, bieten wir euch diesen Pass gemeinsam an. Wir wollen miteinander statt gegeneinander gegen den Rechtsruck kämpfen!

Dein Medienpass unterstützt unseren feministischen und unabhängigen Journalismus und hilft dabei, Missy zu erhalten. Danke für deinen Support, wir wissen ihn sehr zu schätzen! <3

Übrigens: Den Medienpass kann man auch als Geschenk-Pass für jemand anderen kaufen. Stichwort Weihnachten. Just saying ;)

title: Basel: Demonstration 25. November
content:
Eure Gewalt nimmt uns nicht den Mut - notwendig bleibt weiterhin unsere Wut!


Patriarchale Gewalt ist allgegenwärtig. Sie zeigt sich in herablassenden Sprüchen auf der Strasse, in übergriffigen Situationen im Ausgang oder in den eigenen vier Wänden und reicht bis hin zu Feminiziden. Viel zu oft geht diese Gewalt von Personen aus, die uns am nächsten stehen. Aber sie ist kein individuelles Problem, denn die gesellschaftliche Geschlechterordnung mit ihren Rollenbildern wirkt selbst gewaltsam auf unsere blosse Existenz ein.


Jeder dieser Übergriffe ist ein Angriff auf uns alle. Diese Gewalt hat System! Sie geschieht nicht zufällig und die Justiz dieses Systems schafft keine Gerechtigkeit. Die Gewalt an unseren Körpern ist politisch, weil unsere Körper das Ziel der Unterdrückung sind.


Die Uhr scheint sich rückwärts zu drehen, denn weltweit werden hart erkämpfte feministische Errungenschaften wie das Recht auf Selbstbestimmung, Abtreibung und Aufklärung angegriffen. Das Wort „Feminismus“ wird als Schlagwort missbraucht, um Angst zu schüren, Falschinformationen zu verbreiten und trans Menschen ihre Existenz abzusprechen, im Versuch, uns mit ihrer menschenverachtenden Politik zu spalten.


Auch wenn die Marionetten des Kapitalismus ihre Kriegslust und Unterdrückung im Moment auf die Spitze treiben, um unseren ewigen Mut zu brechen, machen wir das, was wir schon immer gemacht haben und immer machen werden:


Wir Frauen und genderqueere Menschen organisieren uns, vernetzen uns und bündeln unsere Wut, gemeinsam mit allen Unterdrückten auf der ganzen Welt, um mit vereinter Kraft weiter gegen die Ordnung der Herrschenden zu kämpfen.


Deshalb tragen wir auch hier in Basel unsere Wut gemeinsam auf die Strasse.


Die Angst muss die Seite wechseln!

author: Zane McNeill
title: The “Blue Tsunami” Can’t Leave Trans People Behind
content:
On this Trans Day of Remembrance, Democrats must recommit to rolling back the anti-trans assault of the past two years.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Many are interpreting the “blue tsunami” that swept the nation earlier this month as a resounding rebuke of the MAGA movement’s fearmongering around transgender rights. But this Trans Day of Remembrance (TDOR), we owe it to ourselves and those we have lost to anti-trans violence to sit with the complicated, nuanced truth and not just comfort ourselves with a convenient, feel-good narrative.

It is true that many candidates who campaigned on explicitly anti-trans messaging and policies lost their elections, in spite of the hundreds of millions of dollars they spent on anti-trans ads. In fact, despite the deluge of anti-transgender messaging, many Democrats who refused to throw trans people under the bus, no matter what anti-trans rhetoric was thrown at them from their opponents, won their races across the country. Ten transgender people were elected into office — in Alabama, Georgia, Delaware, Montana, Florida, Washington, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Michigan. Vermont voters approved a constitutional amendment adding explicit equal protection guarantees for sexual orientation, gender identity, and gender expression.

Polling suggests that voters have grown weary of the weaponization of trans issues by the far right, which they view as an attempt to distract them from the issues that matter most in their lives: inflation and the cost of living; jobs and the economy; and skyrocketing health care bills. Voters who were disenchanted with Donald Trump and the Republicans’ failure to deliver a better life for them mostly ignored the anti-trans messaging and voted blue.

But voting blue doesn’t automatically equate to being pro-trans. Some Democrats who did run on anti-trans policies still won their elections. Further, anti-trans ballot initiatives targeting transgender youth in schools passed in Washington, Arizona, Colorado, and Nebraska, and NBC exit polling showed that 52 percent of people in the U.S. feel that support for transgender rights has “gone too far.”

This sentiment persists despite the fact that at least 25 transgender people have died as a result of violence in the United States over the past year. The actual number of transgender people who have been murdered is certainly higher because the rampant misgendering and deadnaming in news reports and the lack of formal data collection makes accurate tracking and reporting difficult.

The United States has become increasingly untenable for trans people, who now must struggle greatly to survive, let alone thrive. More than half the country has banned medically necessary medication and surgical care for transgender youth and restricted their ability to participate in sports consistent with their gender identity. Across the country, 10 states prohibit people from correcting the gender marker on their birth certificates, eight states ban updates to gender markers on driver’s licenses, and nine states prohibit transgender people from using bathrooms and facilities that align with their gender identity in government-owned buildings and spaces, including K–12 schools and colleges.

Such policies have prompted 9 percent of trans people polled to relocate since 2024, fleeing states with anti-trans laws for supposedly safer havens like Washington and Colorado. But those states, too, have now passed similar anti-trans measures through ballot initiatives (though trans rights advocates have said they will fight to repeal them via legislation and litigation).

Meanwhile, the Trump administration has made attacks on transgender rights a central policy priority, making it increasingly difficult for trans youth to feel safe anywhere in the country. The Trump administration is especially fixated on undermining medical research and standards of care for transgender youth and has challenged states’ sovereign authority to regulate the practice of medicine within their borders. The Trump administration has also issued civil and grand jury subpoenas to hospitals in attempts to obtain transgender youths’ private medical records, targeted the medical associations responsible for researching and developing standards of care for transgender youth through civil investigative subpoenas and litigation, and stopped reimbursing …

author: Freedom Editor
title: Trans remembrance & everyday resistance
content:
The transphobes may have won their draconian legislation, but they have lost the culture war

In July 2017, the Tory Government announced a public consultation on legal gender recognition in the United Kingdom. It aimed to bring in a system based on statutory declaration, and like many European countries, allow trans persons to obtain a Gender Recognition Certificate on the basis of a statutory declaration. This proposed change was supported by the Labour opposition and was not seen as significantly controversial.

Almost immediately, we witnessed a systematic attack on trans children, starting with claims about protecting them from untested medical inteventions and the outright lie that children under 18 were undergoing surgery. In an important case funded by American anti-abortionists, it was argued that young people aged 15 were too young to fully appreciate the consequence of taking puberty blockers. When the lower court ruled that children under 18 should not be able to receive any medical intervention, The Guardian celebrated this in its editorial as a return to common sense.

The Appeals Court judges ruled it was legal nonsense, undermined Gillick competency, and if it upheld could undermine access to contraception for women under 16 (which is why the anti-abortion brigade funded it in the first place). But by now, rebranded ‘gender criticals’ were up in arms and the damage was done to our community. The transphobes were given new life and more foundations to persecute the Tavistock Clinic for Young People and attacking youth services and schools.

Then came the billionaire author J.K Rowldemort, who got involved and began tweeting transphobia to her millions of followers and funding transphobic hate groups. Then came legal intervention by the now Labour (Blue State) government. For Women Scotland, Sex Matters and the LGB Alliance worked as a mesh to split Trans people off from LGB. Freed from the ideological shackles of Sheila Jeffries radical feminist talking points, these new transphobes could move on to fear mongering and hate not seen since the heady days of the persecution of Martina Navratilova in tennis (herself sadly now a terf)

But these culture-war attacks would have gone nowhere without the State. From Boris Johnson to Rishi Sunak to Keir Starmer, a series of deeply transphobic prime ministers have followed complete with transphobic health secretaries, education ministers and home secretaries. One minister made it illegal for teachers to refer to children in school by their preferred name. An employment tribunal agreed that gender critical employees could legally misgender their colleagues at work. Two health secretaries, one from each party, banned all prescription of hormone replacement therapy and puberty blockers for under 18s. One of them (Wes Streeting) had previously worked for leading LGBTIA campaign group Stonewall and appeared on television to defend trans women as women.

So here we are, today on this Trans Day of Remembrance: a new ‘left wing’ Labour prime minister with a gay defence secretary, a Muslim woman home secretary, a Jewish foreign secretary—honestly it sounds like an American Democrat’s fantasy—yet this government will continue to enable and apply a draconian set of transphobic policies that amount to wholesale segregation and apartheid.

Adult trans people cannot use the toilets or changing rooms of their gender identity. They will be housed in prison wards, youth offender wings, immigration hostels and hospital wards of their birth sex. They will be searched by police officers, prison officers and immigration officer on their birth sex/ In Wales, all sex replacement surgery has been cancelled despite people waiting for a decade on waiting lists.

Yet resistance persists. I don’t know a single trans person who uses the toilets of their birth sex. And there has yet to be a single reported incident of a venue or organisation forcing someone to leave. The transphobes may won their legislation, but they have lost the culture war they started. Most people see us as just women, men and nonbinary people who are surviving, just like them, in a toxic authoritarian country ruled by death eaters and bigots.

Personally, I’ve not had one woman in the toilets offer me anything other than acceptance. In those small moments when a woman tells me my dress looks nice in a public toilet, I feel a sense of recognition and solidarity. That gives me hope that out of our remembrance of past …

Ανοιχτη συζητηση για την Pizza Fan – Εργατική  Συμμαχία στα Δυτικά 


ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΣΤΟΥΣ ΕΡΓΑΖΟΜΕΝΟΥΣ ΤΗΣ PIZZA FAN


Το σκάνδαλο μεγατόνων της Pizza Fan δεν αποτελεί απλώς υπόθεση ακραίας φορο – κλοπής. Είναι το πιο κραυγαλέο, έως τώρα, μνημείο της κυβερνητικής απάτης περί «πάταξης της φοροδιαφυγής», περί θαύματος της ελληνικής εστίασης και «προστασίας» των εργαζομένων από την «εθνική κοινωνική συμφωνία» για τις συλλογικές συμβάσεις…


Την ώρα που η κυβέρνηση τσακίζει τα φτωχά νοικοκυριά με ΦΠΑ στο 24% (ενώ καλπάζει ο πληθωρισμός που γεννά το σύστημα και οι πόλεμοι που συμμετέχει το Μητσοτακέικο), εξοντώνει τα μικρομάγαζα της γειτονιάς με τη σύνδεση Ταμειακών Μηχανών – POS και τα ψηφιακά τιμολόγια, έκανε πλάτες και άφηνε στο απυρόβλητο ένα επιχειρηματικό θηρίο να στήνει «πάρτι» εκατομμυρίων προπαντός σε βάρος των εργαζομένων του και των ίδιων των εσόδων του δημοσίου.


Αλλά ακόμα και τώρα που το κράτος αποκάλυψε το σκάνδαλο (προφανώς για να αρπάξουν άλλα επιχειρηματικά μεγα – θήρια το άθαφτο πλέον πτώμα της Pizza Fan), δεν δίνει δεκάρα για τους εργαζομένους – θύματα της εταιρείας.


Πριν το λουκέτο, πίσω από τις βιτρίνες βασίλευε η μαύρη εργασία, οι εικονικές 6ωρες συμβάσεις, «μαύρες» πληρωμές στο χέρι και η πλήρης γελοιοποίηση της ψηφιακής κάρτας εργασίας. Μετά το λουκέτο, βασιλεύει η απειλή της ανεργίας, της μη αποζημίωσης και της ανυπαρξίας κρατικής στήριξης!


Οι συνδικαλιστές «εκπρόσωποι» των εργαζομένων της Pizza Fan, δεν κάνουν τίποτα ουσιαστικά άλλο εκτός από να παρακαλούν την κυβέρνηση και τους εργοδότες να κάνουν το «νομίμως» δυνατό, την ώρα που αυτή μετράει και το παραμικρό σεντς (αν πρόκειται για τους εργαζομένους), ενώ σκάει δις για πολεμικές δαπάνες.


Και γιατί να τηρήσουν το νόμο οι ιδιοκτήτες της Pizza Fan τώρα που έχουν βαρέσει «κανόνι», αφού δεν το έκαναν όταν θησαύριζαν;


Μάς λένε ψέμματα για άλλη μια φορά! Αλλά να μην τους αφήσουμε ξανά να μας τα επιβάλλουν. Παλεύουμε για:


– Καμιά απόλυση στην Pizza Fan! Διασφάλιση όλων των θέσεων εργασίας!


– Άμεση πληρωμή δεδουλευμένων και ενσήμων με ταυτόχρονη κατάσχεση και ρευστοποίηση της κινητής και ακίνητης περιουσίας του απατεώνα ιδιοκτήτη!


– Τοπικές επιτροπές στήριξης των εργαζομένων της Pizza Fan. Στάσεις εργασίας από τοπικά σωματεία.

author: TGEU
title: Joint Statement: Why Portugal’s Self-Determination Act Must Stay
content:
TGEU, IGLYO, OII Europe and ILGA-Europe have submitted joint comments to the Portuguese Parliament on two Bills that would repeal Law 38/2018, the Self-Determination Act, and reinstate the medicalised regime of Law 7/2011: Bill 391/XVII/1, tabled by Chega, and Bill 486/XVII/1, tabled by the PSD. Both parties sit in the ruling government, so together they command the majority needed to pass these Bills into law. We ask Parliament to withdraw both Bills or vote against them in their entirety.


There is no problem to solve.

 The Self-Determination Act works. Between 2018 and 2022, 1,595 people changed their gender marker, more than triple the previous period, and the competent authority, the CIG, reported in 2022 and again in 2026 that it knows of no refusals, no fraud and no misuse. Twelve European countries have self-determination models, some for over a decade; none has repealed them. Where rare problems arose, courts solved them. Legal initiatives that strip people of acquired rights need a demonstrated need, and none exists.


What these Bills would do


Bring back pathologisation and clinical gatekeeping.

 Trans adults would once again have to prove their identity to two multidisciplinary medical teams, undergo years of psychological monitoring and, as drafted, in practice show proof of surgery before the State recognises who they are. The European Court of Human Rights has ruled that no one should have to accept surgery or sterilising treatment to be recognised, and the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe has called for procedures based on self-determination. Worse still, Portugal already struggles with a shortage of professionals in trans-specific healthcare: a procedure requiring two teams, years of monitoring and a surgical pathway would make legal gender recognition effectively inaccessible in practice, squandering scarce medical resources on certifying instead of treating or meeting actual health needs. These Bills would put doctors, not trans people, in charge of trans people’s identities.


Exclude 16 and 17 year olds from legal gender recognition

, despite the existing safeguards (legal representatives, a personal hearing and a capacity report) and no recorded refusals, fraud or abuse. The UN Convention on the Rights of the Child requires capacity-based assessment, not fixed age limits. The reality for those affected: every exam, train ride, job application or school registration becomes a forced outing, in a country where nearly three in four LGBTQI students report bullying or insults at school.


Weaken protection of intersex children.

 Portugal made history in 2018 as the second European country to ban non-consensual medical interventions on intersex children. Bill 391 repeals that ban without an adequate replacement; Bill 486’s weakly defined “health exception” could still permit medically unnecessary “normalising” surgeries. Both Bills regress on Recommendation CM/Rec(2025)7, which Portugal helped adopt only very recently in October 2025.


Roll back healthcare and education rights.

 Bill 391 would ban all gender-affirming care for under-18s by statute, overriding the judgment of doctors, parents and the young people themselves, and restrict teaching on gender diversity in schools, an approach the EU Court of Justice has already rejected in its judgment against Hungary. Bill 486 removes the protected ground of gender expression, restricts sports participation by “biological sex”, risks excluding trans and intersex children from youth and school sport, and deletes the right to a social name, which migrants, minors and non-binary people rely on to live as themselves in schools, workplaces and public services.


Rely on outdated, pathologising and stigmatising terminology

 (“gender identity disorder”, “transsexuality”, “hermaphrodites”) that contradicts ICD-11, which Portugal supported, and the human-rights based language that all 46 Council of Europe member States have adopted with CM/Rec(2025)7. Words matter: law that frames people as disorders invites treating them as such.


Not in line with international human rights law


Restricting fundamental rights requires a pressing social need under Article 8(2) ECHR and the Portuguese Constitution. These Bills offer conceptual or hypothetical worries, thinly sourced on Portuguese practice, not demonstrated problems. Rolling back rights people already hold requires full justification and consideration of all alternatives; these Bills …

author: anred
title: 19N: un grito colectivo contra la violencia sexual hacia las niñeces y adolescencias
content:
En el marco del Día Internacional contra las Violencias Sexuales hacia Niñeces y Adolescencias, organizaciones feministas, transfeministas, sobrevivientes y madres protectoras se movilizarán este jueves 19 de noviembre frente al Congreso de la Nación. Bajo la consigna «Yo sí te creo», denunciarán la impunidad judicial, las revinculaciones forzadas con agresores y el desmantelamiento de las políticas públicas de protección. La jornada combinará denuncia, memoria, organización colectiva y un festival para recuperar el espacio público desde el encuentro y la celebración

. Por ANRed


Este 19 de noviembre, el Congreso de la Nación será escenario de una nueva edición del

Grito Global contra las Violencias Sexuales hacia Niñeces y Adolescencias.

 La convocatoria, impulsada por el Colectivo Yo Sí Te Creo junto a organizaciones sociales, feministas y transfeministas, reunirá a sobrevivientes, madres y familiares protectores, profesionales de la salud, docentes y activistas que desde hace años se organizan para denunciar una de las formas más silenciadas de violencia.


La jornada se inscribe en una trayectoria de trece años de lucha y visibilización, que desde 2020 se articula en distintos territorios del país bajo la iniciativa del Grito Global. Su objetivo es romper el silencio, denunciar las responsabilidades institucionales y construir redes colectivas de acompañamiento y protección.


Según los datos citados por las organizaciones convocantes,

una de cada cinco niñas y uno de cada siete niños atraviesan situaciones de violencia sexual

. En Argentina, señalan que cerca del 80 % de estos hechos ocurren en el ámbito intrafamiliar o en entornos de confianza. Estas cifras, advierten, no alcanzan a reflejar la verdadera magnitud del problema, debido a la enorme cantidad de situaciones que nunca llegan a denunciarse.


La violencia sexual contra las infancias no constituye un problema exclusivamente privado o familiar. Las organizaciones denuncian que se encuentra atravesada por relaciones desiguales de poder, condiciones económicas, estructuras patriarcales y prácticas institucionales que muchas veces terminan garantizando la impunidad de los agresores.


Una justicia que revictimiza y desprotege


Uno de los principales ejes de la convocatoria será la denuncia del funcionamiento del Poder Judicial frente a las situaciones de abuso sexual infantil.


El documento cuestiona la utilización del denominado Síndrome de Alienación Parental (SAP) y de argumentos derivados, como las supuestas falsas memorias o los relatos inducidos, para desacreditar las denuncias de niños, niñas, adolescentes y sus entornos protectores.


Las organizaciones advierten que estas prácticas pueden convertirse en herramientas de revictimización y derivar en decisiones judiciales que obligan a las infancias a mantener contacto con personas denunciadas por abuso sexual.


En ese sentido, rechazan las revinculaciones forzadas y exigen el apartamiento de funcionarios judiciales responsables de vulnerar los derechos de las niñeces. También reclaman el regreso de las niñas Arociris, de La Rioja, y Cielo, de Chaco, a sus respectivos entornos protectores.


La criminalización de las madres que denuncian constituye otro de los puntos centrales. Bajo la consigna «No somos obstructoras, somos protectoras», las organizaciones denuncian la persecución judicial de mujeres que intentan proteger a sus hijos e hijas y reclaman la libertad de Flavia Saganías.


A estas situaciones se suman las dificultades materiales para acceder a la justicia: falta de patrocinio jurídico gratuito, investigaciones que se prolongan durante años, ausencia de acompañamiento especializado y desigualdades económicas que condicionan las posibilidades de sostener una denuncia.


Las organizaciones reclaman presupuesto, equipos interdisciplinarios, atención psicológica especializada, acompañamiento a sobrevivientes y condiciones laborales dignas para quienes trabajan en los dispositivos de protección.


En particular, reivindican la implementación efectiva de la Ley Nacional de Educación Sexual Integral, con formación docente y contenidos científicos en todos los niveles educativos, como una herramienta fundamental para que las infancias puedan reconocer situaciones de violencia, identificar sus derechos y acceder a redes de cuidado.


Asimismo, defienden el acceso a la interrupción legal y voluntaria del embarazo y recuperan la consigna «Son niñas, no madres», frente a las maternidades …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: “Cuba, Ever Committed to Just Causes, Deserves the World’s Support”, by Alice Walker and Salim Lamrani, for Znet
content:
By Alice Walker and Salim Lamrani, for

Znet


Since the triumph of the Revolution in 1959, Cuba has made support for peoples struggling for their emancipation the cornerstone of its foreign policy, consistently assisting nations of the Global South and independence movements worldwide. After breaking the chains of neocolonial domination by overthrowing the dictatorship of Fulgencio Batista, Fidel Castro made internationalism – that is, concrete solidarity with just causes – a national priority. In spite of its modest size and limited resources, and despite the economic siege imposed by Washington beginning in 1960, Cuba has never failed in its duty of solidarity.


Cuba was the first country in the Americas to recognize the People’s Republic of China in 1960, thereby breaking the diplomatic isolation imposed on Beijing by the United States in the Western Hemisphere. That same year, Havana urged the United Nations General Assembly to open its doors to the legitimate representatives of the Chinese people, rejecting the puppet regime of Chiang Kai-shek. Ten years later, beginning in 1970, Canada and Chile, along with other countries in the Americas, would follow the path forged by Cuba, officially recognizing the legitimacy of Mao Zedong’s Revolution. Thus, from the very beginning, despite considerable pressure, the Caribbean nation demonstrated its friendship toward the People’s Republic of China.


Opposed to colonialism on principle, Havana immediately lent its support to the cause of Algerian independence in 1959, expressing its opposition at the United Nations to the subjugation of Africa’s largest country by colonial France. In 1961, Cuba became the first country in the Americas to officially recognize the Provisional Government of the Algerian Republic. That same year, the island sent a substantial shipment of weapons to the mujahideen of the National Liberation Front and welcomed wounded fighters and war orphans onto its soil. In 1963, following Morocco’s invasion of Algeria, Cuba dispatched its finest troops to repel the armed aggression, thereby helping preserve the country’s territorial integrity. Also in 1963, the Cuban Revolution sent its first medical brigade to Algeria to care for a population devastated by 132 years of colonial oppression.


In 1975, when Angola had only just gained its independence, apartheid South Africa invaded the country with the aim of overthrowing the MPLA and installing a regime loyal to Pretoria. Responding to an urgent appeal from Agostinho Neto, Fidel Castro launched Operation Carlota, deploying tens of thousands of seasoned fighters to repel the aggression and inflict the first defeat on white supremacist forces on African soil, irreparably shattering the myth of the white army’s invincibility. In 1988, the decisive Battle of Cuito Cuanavale, fought by Cuban forces, dealt a crushing blow to Pretoria’s racist regime and led to the independence of Southern Africa and the collapse of apartheid, paving the way for the liberation of Nelson Mandela and the South African people.


For decades, Cuba served as a haven for numerous activists fleeing persecution by U.S.-backed military dictatorships in Latin America. The island welcomed thousands of political refugees, particularly from Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, Haiti, and the Dominican Republic. They found protection in revolutionary Cuba, which provided them with housing, employment, and access to education and health care.


Furthermore, since 1959, Cuba has trained tens of thousands of foreign professionals, including doctors, engineers, teachers, and technicians from every continent. It has also provided medical assistance in 165 countries, mobilizing more than 600,000 health care professionals who have treated nearly two billion people and saved millions of lives. Even today, numerous countries in the developing world, as well as developed nations such as Italy, benefit from Cuban medical cooperation, which has proved crucial in preserving health systems and protecting populations. At a time when the drums of war are sounding everywhere, claiming tens of thousands of innocent lives, particularly in Gaza, where a genocide is still underway, Cuba continues to save lives.


Yet, for more than six decades, the Cuban people have endured a ruthless economic siege imposed by the United States, which constitutes the principal cause of their suffering, the foremost …

author: Marianne Dhenin
title: Authors Sue LA Library Over Anti-Palestinian Discrimination After Talk Cancelled
content:
Even institutions meant to be dedicated to free speech and inclusion are censoring Palestinian writers.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Two authors have filed a lawsuit against the City of Los Angeles, alleging that the Los Angeles Public Library engaged in anti-Palestinian discrimination and violated their free speech rights after the library’s leadership canceled an online event last December where the two were slated to speak to teens about their books, which feature Palestinian characters. This lawsuit against one of the largest public library systems in the nation comes at a time when anti-Palestinian racism and censorship are growing more entrenched across the country, now more than three years into the U.S.-backed genocide in Gaza.

“The stakes are really high, and it’s about so much more than the rights of the authors or even the rights of the readers,” Nora Lester Murad, one of the authors and plaintiffs in the case, told Truthout. “If kids and adults can’t be exposed to representation of Palestinians that’s diverse and nuanced and human and complex and multifaceted, [that erasure] converges with the anti-Palestinian and anti-Muslim narratives that are being used to justify genocide.”

Murad and Palestinian American author Jenan Matari filed the lawsuit in the Superior Court of Los Angeles in late September to demand accountability for the Los Angeles Public Library’s cancellation of their event and to draw attention to anti-Palestinian censorship in the arts.

Matari is the author of the picture book Everything Grows in Jiddo’s Garden, about a young Palestinian girl and her grandfather. Murad was slated to discuss Ida in the Middle, her young adult novel about a 13-year-old Palestinian American girl. The two were scheduled to speak at an online event on December 6, 2025, as part of Read Palestine Week, a global weeklong program highlighting Palestinian authors and stories celebrated in late November and early December each year.

The Los Angeles Public Library’s teen council, a youth volunteer group, voted to host a Read Palestine Week event, and the library’s Middle Eastern North African Affinity Group invited Murad and Matari and acted as liaisons between the authors and library administration in the lead-up to the scheduled event, according to the legal complaint.

But just three days before the event was scheduled to take place, the group notified Murad and Matari that the library administration had canceled it. The notice provided no further explanation for the cancellation, according to the legal complaint.

Records obtained by Los Angeles Public Press in a public records request and cited in the legal complaint later revealed that a staff librarian had emailed library leadership in mid-November 2025, accusing Murad and Matari of having “strong terrorist ties and virulently antisemitic views.” The email said it was sent on behalf of a group of Jewish library staffers and referenced an article from the right-wing Washington Free Beacon and profiles of the authors on Canary Mission, a pro-Israel doxxing platform. It also accused the Middle Eastern North African Affinity Group of having “deeply antisemitic views” and showing “racist behavior to me and others in our Heritage group.”

“This attack was not from outside but from inside the library.”

Later in December 2025, City Librarian John Szabo sent an internal email to staff claiming Murad and Matari’s event had been canceled because the library “has a responsibility to remain nonpartisan and apolitical” and that doing so was “necessary to uphold the Library’s commitment to an inclusive environment free of hate, discrimination, and harassment,” according to a copy of that email obtained by The LA Reporter in a public records request.

Szabo did not respond to Truthout’s request for comment before deadline. A member of the library’s public relations team told Truthout that the library cannot comment on pending litigation.

Murad told Truthout the accusations and cancellation follow a familiar pattern in which criticism of Israel is conflated with antisemitism in order to silence Palestinian speakers like Matari, anti-Zionist Jewish speakers like Murad, or others who speak out to criticize Israel or in support of Palestinian liberation. But, she added, the Los Angeles Public Library case is also unique because the pressure to censor Palestine-related speech came not from …

author: Ariel Giagio
title: Mulheres negras na diplomacia: avanços e desafios dentro do Itamaraty
content:
Marise Ribeiro Nogueira foi a primeira mulher negra a ingressar na diplomacia brasileira como bolsista pelo Programa de Ação Afirmativa em 2003. Em entrevista à

Agência Pública

, ela conta que durante uma reunião em Washington D.C, capital dos Estados Unidos, foi abordada por um homem negro, de terno elegante. Era o representante do arquipélago caribenho São Cristóvão e Neves, que ocupava, naquela situação, o cargo de decano dos diplomatas.


“[Ele] me disse que ficava muito satisfeito por ver uma pessoa negra na delegação brasileira, porque era a primeira vez que via uma diplomata negra na delegação do Brasil”, recorda Nogueira que ainda atuava como terceira-secretária, o cargo inicial na carreira diplomática.


A partir deste momento, uma aliança se formou. Nogueira afirma que no fim da reunião conseguiu colocá-lo em contato com o representante alterno da missão brasileira junto à ONU em Nova York “e esse contato colaborou com a parceria entre o Brasil e a OEA na questão negra”, explica.


Hoje, ela é ministra de segunda classe e chefe da Assessoria Especial de Assuntos Internacionais do Ministério da Saúde. “Para mim foi uma honra ter sido a primeira bolsista do programa de ação afirmativa do Instituto Rio Branco a ser aprovada no concurso de admissão à carreira diplomática em 2023. Então lá se vão 23 anos de carreira diplomática”, declara a diplomata que também foi conselheira da embaixada do Panamá e a primeira mulher negra a trabalhar na Embaixada do Brasil nos Estados Unidos.


Marise Nogueira faz parte de um grupo de mulheres negras pouco conhecidas pelos brasileiros, mas que já deixaram seus nomes na diplomacia do país, reconhecida como uma das mais respeitadas do mundo. Entre elas estão Dulce Maria Pereira, Mônica de Menezes Campos e Isabel Heyvaert. São nomes que acabam servindo de referência para profissionais do Ministério das Relações Exteriores (MRE) mais jovens como Flávia Medeiros, ou a

primeira mulher quilombola

 a entrar na carreira diplomática, Helen Borgens.


Em 2026, o Itamaraty conquistou o maior número de mulheres diplomatas aprovadas pelo Concurso de Admissão à Carreira Diplomática (CACD) da história do Instituto Rio Branco e do Itamaraty. A diplomacia, que já foi por lei uma profissão exclusivamente masculina, terá na nova turma de 2026-2028 um grupo 45% feminino.


Se o número de pessoas negras que tomaram posse ainda é baixo, o crescimento já é significativo: 18 diplomatas negros foram aprovados no CACD. Foram 15 aprovados na reserva de vagas para pessoas negras, uma na reserva de vagas para pessoas quilombolas e duas pela ampla concorrência.


“As mudanças que temos hoje são fruto de muita luta coletiva, de movimentos sociais e de políticas de inclusão, como as cotas e bolsas de vocação.

Também carregam o legado de quem veio antes e enfrentou barreiras quando quase ninguém falava sobre isso”, avalia a oficial de Chancelaria e secretária executiva adjunta do Comitê Étnico-Racial do MRE, Flávia Medeiros.


“O papel das primeiras mulheres negras na diplomacia, como Mônica de Menezes Campos, foi muito além de serem pioneiras. Ao ocuparem espaços onde quase nunca se via pessoas como elas, desafiaram padrões e mostraram que mulheres negras também pertenciam àqueles lugares”, complementa.


A diplomata Isabel Heyvaert, , ministra de segunda classe e ex-embaixadora do Brasil na República da Sérvia, em Montenegro e na Etiópia, conheceu Mônica Campos. “Quando ela ingressou na carreira diplomática, eu já integrava o Itamaraty, como Oficial de Chancelaria, carreira distinta da diplomática. O pioneirismo de Mônica demonstrava que mulheres negras também podiam conquistar espaço em uma carreira historicamente marcada por uma representação social bastante restrita”, diz Heyvaert.


As conquistas, entretanto, não garantiram imunidade aos preconceitos raciais e de gênero. Como oficial da Chancelaria, Isabel Heyvaert ouvia que a “casa” era dos diplomatas, e não dos oficiais – assistentes que “não deviam se acomodar”. “Compreendi que, se desejasse ampliar meu campo de atuação e assumir responsabilidades para além das atribuições daquela carreira, precisaria prestar um novo concurso”. Ela foi aprovada em 1982 e oficializada como terceira-secretária em 1984.


Questionada pela

Pública

 sobre os momentos mais marcantes da carreira, Heyvaert relata uma visita ao Sudão em 2011, meses antes da independência do Sudão do Sul, durante graves conflitos que geraram uma dura crise humanitária. Embaixadora do …

author: Rizomatica
title: Juana Paillalef denuncia discriminación racial hacia su familia y la infancia Mapuche en Lavkenmapu
content:
Luego de que la machi Millaray Garrido Paillalef, del territorio Lawen Mapu, Lanalhue, realizara un video denunciando violencia institucional y discriminación en el hospital de Arauco, su madre, Juana Paillalef, quien fue directora del Museo Mapuche de Cañete durante 20 años, junto a Mario Cayupi hacen una reflexión sobre diversas situaciones de discriminación racial hacia su familia.


Juana Paillalef a través de su relato explica cómo han vivido vulneraciones, violencia institucional y discriminación, a través de todas las generaciones de su familia. Ella, su hija y ahora su nieta, ven como se vulneran los derechos de niños, no solo mapuches. Comenta cómo han sido vulnerados en su mogen, en su vida como Mapuche, luego de haber levantado a su hija Machi, quien desde estudiante vivió vulneraciones, en el liceo se le discriminó por el uso de sus chaway y su tukuluwün y en la universidad también existieron educadores que la discriminaron por ser Mapuche. En su primer embarazo también vivió vulneraciones en centros de salud, y ahora en la actualidad denuncian haber vivido discriminación y maltratos por un profesional de la salud del hospital de Arauco en contra de su nieta.


“

Se habla de interculturalidad, cambiando por el racismo, ¿pero qué hemos visto de interculturalida hasta este momento? Seguimos en lo mismo. La colonización ha triturado nuestro pensamiento, nuestras formas de vida, nuestras formas de comportamiento, nuestra forma de exigir nuestros derechos, nos han apagado en vez de abrirnos. Llamo a la población a no dormirse, estar atentos y no dejar de caminar al lado de nuestros niños. Hay muchos niños y jóvenes en colegios que se están levantando como machi, y no hay como atender esas situaciones.”


*Video enviado  a la radio


Esta información se publicó en

Radio Kurruf

author: James Hamill
title: A Disaster Waiting to Happen?  Brent Bozell and the US-South Africa Relationship
content:
President Donald Trump’s appointment of Leo Brent Bozell as the United States ambassador to South Africa in 2025 was a deliberately provocative act on his part. The appointment always seemed purposely designed to further damage a US-South Africa bilateral relationship which was already fraught due to differences over South Africa’s domestic and foreign policy choices. Put bluntly, for decades Bozell has been a conservative activist not a diplomat and he lacks the basic skills set to hold such an important and sensitive position Trump appoints Leo Brent Bozell III, a defender of apartheid in the 1980s, as ambassador to South Africa | U.S. | EL PAÍS English. As his behaviour in South Africa is demonstrating, that is an environment likely to produce partisan ideologues rather than people with the tact, nuance, patience, and knowledge required for high level inter-state diplomacy. Since taking up the role of US ambassador in February 2026, he has consistently abused his position through hostile posturing and ‘megaphone diplomacy.’ He has disrespected South Africa’s independent judiciary, publicly berated the host government, and has persistently interfered in South African domestic politics – in clear violation of Article 41.1 of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, 1961– by aligning himself with Afrikaner nationalist groupings, Afriforum and Solidarity, and amplifying their grievances Between candour and coercion — why SA won’t bend to Washington’s dictates. He has issued a series of ‘asks’ – US demands in effect – on issues such as farm murders and rural crime, Black Economic Empowerment, land expropriation without compensation in exceptional circumstances US to make SA to pay the price of doing nothing. Consequently, he has now been démarched – summoned to receive a diplomatic reprimand – by the South African Department of International Relations and Co-operation on no less than three separate occasions in 2026: in March (after less than one month in position), June and September Dirco summons US ambassador Bozell again over ‘undiplomatic conduct’.

Bozell’s ‘extraordinary experience’ All of this was very predictable. Bozell’s appointment has captured in microcosm the broader failings of the Trump administration’s approach to diplomacy and international relations: it was incendiary and was designed primarily to appease white nationalist opinion within Trump’s MAGA base rather than to help mend US-South African relations. In a reversal of standard diplomatic practice, Bozell was sent to South Africa to exacerbate rather than ease tensions and to promote discord. Although Trump stated that Bozell brought ‘extraordinary experience’ to his role Trump appoints Leo Brent Bozell III, a defender of apartheid in the 1980s, as ambassador to South Africa | U.S. | EL PAÍS English, it is actually his South African ‘experience’ which is the main problem. Bozell has a long history of opposition to the African National Congress (ANC) whom he labelled ‘terrorists’ during the 1980s liberation struggle era. He enlisted his National Conservative Political Action Committee in a so-called ‘Coalition Against ANC Terrorism’, a collection of American conservative groupings supportive of the apartheid regime. He strongly opposed the US’s opening of formal diplomatic contacts with the ANC, initiated by then Secretary of State George Shultz in January 1987, in which the Reagan administration effectively acknowledged that there could be no long term South African settlement without its involvement Trump’s Pick For Ambassador To South Africa Actively Opposed Fight To End Apartheid. Bozell was also hostile to the liberation struggle per se as was demonstrated by his support in the 1980s for the regime of President P W Botha, his opposition to the global anti-apartheid movement, and his opposition to the US sanctions contained in the Comprehensive Anti-Apartheid Act (CAAA) of October 1986. The CAAA proved to be of crucial importance in intensifying pressure on the regime and helping to move South Africa beyond apartheid. Anyone doubting its impact need only look at the striking similarity between the US demands, as set out in the CAAA, and the changes announced by President F W De Klerk in his historic speech of 2nd February 1990, over three years later. Bozell was profoundly wrong on everything South Africa-related in the 1980s: wrong to attempt to shore up a failing Botha regime which was …

author: Michael_1973
title: Socialism or Barbarism? - S'bu Zikode
content:
Keynote address by S'bu Zikode, from Abahlali baseMjondolo, at the Third National Conference of the Aotearoa New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies held in Ōtepoti Dunedin, on Saturday, 14 November 2026.

Comrade Programme director, thank you for welcoming me to Aotearoa once again. May I express my sincere gratitude to the New Zealand Federation of Socialist Societies and Palestine Solidarity Network Aotearoa for inviting me to speak here today, and across the country. I bring greetings from Abahlali baseMjondolo, our movement in South Africa which now has more than 200,000 members.

I want to begin with the words of a song, a song about socialism, that is often sung in the struggles of the left in South Africa.

Yini iSocialism? Umhlaba wonke ezandleni zabantu Akunamuntu, akunamuntu ongaphatha umhlaba ngayedwa Ayayesaba bo, ayesaba amabhujwa, nongxiwa Ngoba bona, ngobabona befuna ukusetshenzelwa ngabantu

The song asks, ‘What is socialism?’ It answers that socialism is the whole world in the hands of the people. It goes on to say that no one person can own the world on their own. It concludes that the bourgeoisie are afraid of socialism, because they want the people to work for them.

Comrades, as you will all know, in 1915, during the mass slaughter of the First World War, Rosa Luxemburg wrote from a prison cell in Germany that humanity stood at a crossroads. Either it would move towards socialism, towards global justice and peace, or it would collapse into further barbarism. She was writing as millions of workers were being sent to kill each other in the trenches for the profits of their rulers. Four years later she was murdered.

In our movement we have our own version of this choice. Lindokuhle Mnguni, the gifted young chairperson of one of our branches, the eKhenana Commune in Durban, introduced the slogan ‘Socialism or Death’ into our movement. For Lindokuhle, socialism was not something that would come one day in the future, after a revolution, or after an election. Socialism had to be lived now, in the way we occupy land, ensure that it is not bought and sold, manage it democratically, grow food together, ensure that nobody goes hungry, care for each other, build and manage social infrastructure like halls, creches and kitchens, and make decisions together.

For us, like urban and rural movements elsewhere in the world, building socialism from below means building communes, connecting them and building wider forms of democratic popular power from these communes. In the same way that the liberated zones were the bases for anti-colonial movements in countries like Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau, communes – from South Africa to Brazil, Venezuela and elsewhere – are the strongest bases for our movements to build socialism. As Ruthie Wilson Gilmore says, ‘Freedom is a place’.

The price for challenging oppression can be very high. Many comrades around the world have given their lives. On 20 August 2022, Lindokuhle was shot dead in his home. He was the third leader of the eKhenana Commune to be assassinated in less than six months.

Frantz Fanon taught that ‘Each generation must, out of relative obscurity, discover its mission, fulfill it, or betray it.’ Comrades like Rosa Luxemburg and Lindokuhle Mnguni understood the mission of their generation, and gave their lives to it. Our generation also has a mission. We are living in a time of genocide, of wealth beyond imagination for a few and hunger for millions, of the far right and fascist forces rising and of the poor being turned against each other. We have to decide whether we will fulfil our mission or betray it. In our movement we have often used Fanon’s words. When people find themselves pushed to the margins of the city and of life, they have the opportunity to discover their mission and to decide whether they want to fulfil it or betray it.

I want to speak today about the barbarism that we see around us, in South Africa and around the world, and about the work of building socialism from below, as we have tried to do it in our movement.

When Luxemburg wrote about barbarism she was thinking of the slaughter of the First World War. Today we are witnessing another mass slaughter of human beings. We have all watched the genocide in Gaza. We have watched children being starved, hospitals and schools being bombed, and whole families being buried under the rubble of their homes. We have watched the most powerful governments in the world supply the weapons …

author: dev
title: Lorenzaccio de David Bobée ou l'insuffisance politique
content:
Acclamée par la critique, l'adaptation de

Lorrenzaccio

 de Musset par le metteur en scène David Bobée nous plonge dans l'impuissance politique de l'Italie du XVI

e

 siècle pour mieux nous renvoyer à notre impuissance contemporaine, c'est ce que raconte France Inter. Adèle Aldokas, y a surtout vu une complaisance narcissique, de l'art institutionnel qui ne critique pas grand chose et un public qui « à la fin, se lève, incapable de se soulever. »


Après le couronnement du bouffon, la lumière tombe et le public se lève pour applaudir généreusement. C'est la preuve que le spectacle a plu et que le public est d'accord : nous n'arrivons pas à nous libérer de la tyrannie, les roitelets se succèdent et la République démocratique reste un idéal.


Mais est-ce vraiment pour cela que le public se lève ?


Une chose est sûre, la performance des acteurs est remarquable. Félix Back est stupéfiant et sa prestation unanimement saluée. Sa présence est délicate, toute en contrastes et de nuances, d'une virtuosité assurée. Et pourtant le début de la pièce est dominé par Mexianu Medenou, dont le charisme et la puissance corporelle fascinent, effraient, révulsent. Les deux acteurs portent la pièce, avec aisance, et on s'émerveille encore de la justesse de Greg Germain (Philippe Strozzi), de Catherine Dewitt (Maria ; Le Cardinal), de Djamil Mohamed (Tebaldeo) ou encore, parmi les autres, d'Yassim Aït Adbelmalek (Maffio ; Capponi). Et c'est sans doute le plus important : ce jeu des acteurs qui fait de la pièce de David Bobée un grand moment de théâtre.


Les fans de Bobée, par ailleurs, ne seront pas déçu-es. Nous retrouvons sa patte et son esprit : une esthétique néo-baroque, par le mélange des techniques, et une approche

woke

 assumée, qui fait la part belle aux acteur-ices noir-es et racisé-es. Un rôle muet est même proposé à Jules Turlet (Pierre Strozzi), et l'homosexualité (auquel invite ce joli mot Valois de Musset : « mignon ») est au rendez-vous.


On aura entendu dire qu'il y avait peut-être un peu trop de son et de lumière, de vidéos, que ça pouvait occulter parfois le jeu virtuose de Félix Back, que ce théâtre regardait un peu trop du côté du cinéma, ou que les beaux chants de Nicolas Moumbounou tranchaient avec son personnage grossier de sire Maurice. On aura entendu dire, au contraire, que cette musique, ces lumières, ces vidéos, ces fumigènes (malgré les crises de toux), rendaient dynamiques et accessibles une pièce que le texte de Musset pouvait parfois alourdir (c'est, on s'en souvient, un « théâtre pour un fauteuil »). L'hémoglobine qui dégouline allégrement plaît ou déplaît, question de goût. La scène de la mort de Louise et même celle de l'assassinat d'Alexandre (adaptée de Sand) ont suscité quelques rires, mais on pourrait invoquer le mélange des genres, en plus du mélange des techniques, un grotesque plus ou moins voulu ou bienvenu. Le tout reste réussi : on ne s'ennuie pas, le public en redemande.


Il faut bien sûr saluer cette présence forte, sans concession, décisive d'acteurices racisé-es et d'un muet. Du reste, on sait, par les quelques portraits d'époque d'Alexandre, qu'il n'était pas blanc. Il est toujours bon de rappeler le métissage profond de l'Italie d'hier et d'aujourd'hui, entre Normands, Lombards, Arabes, Espagnols plus ou moins maures, qui ont envahi violemment Sicile, Calabre, Campanie, loin des migrations du désespoir et des exils pacifiques actuels pourtant stigmatisés. La pièce le clame : le problème n'est pas là, il réside dans la fascisme. C'est le péril d'aujourd'hui.


Pourtant, on peut aussi (et on doit le faire) interroger les limites de ces présences. On aura entendu demander, non sans raison : « cette inclusivité est-elle réelle ? », « Pourquoi n'avoir pas surtitré toute la pièce, si on veut inclure les sourd-es ? » On se flatte de pouvoir mettre en scène des « minorités », mais c'est dans l'écrin d'un théâtre bourgeois. On se flatte d'applaudir à cette « intégration », mais pour qui vote-t-on quand on va voter ? Pour qui travaille-t-on ? Que produit-on et que consomme-t-on ? Que fait-on concrètement, sinon bavarder, comme les Républicains de la pièce ? On est content-e de voir que les Noirs et les Arabes peuvent se produire sur une grande scène, tout comme les Blancs, qu'ils peuvent être homosexuels, qu'ils peuvent bien assimiler les codes de la République, et on oublie finalement que cette République n'en a que le nom, et que ses valeurs, par nature, excluent la vraie diversité …

author: Yasmine Johnson
title: Jillian Segal’s war on the left
content:
Antisemitism Special Envoy Jillian Segal’s “Plan to combat antisemitism” is nothing of the sort. Her latest report, published 30 October, is a stunning piece of Trumpist propaganda. It is riddled with conspiracy theories about malign radical-left and Islamist influence in Australian institutions. It calls for sweeping crackdowns on free speech, political activism and migration, all in the name of protecting Israel’s reputation. It is an indictment of the Labor government that commissioned it.

Labor named Segal “special envoy to combat antisemitism” knowing her record as a right-wing warrior and campaigner for Israel’s murderous wars. Her appointment was part of a multi-faceted offensive against the Palestine solidarity movement. She has consistently used this platform to shield the Israeli government from criticism and attack opponents of the war.

Segal’s new report pays little attention to the growing antisemitic far right. Since her appointment, Nazis have addressed thousands at anti-migrant marches. One Nation, a party

riddled with Hitler fanatics

, has shot up in the polls. But far-right antisemitism is minimised because it isn’t the “primary source of concern or anxiety to members of the Jewish community”.

The real danger is “modern, progressive antisemitism”, which Segal labels “the most pervasive manifestation of antisemitism facing Australia”. 

Segal claims that anti-Israel progressives have simply repackaged an age-old hatred: 

“The language of human rights and its greatest crimes—apartheid, ethnic cleansing, genocide, etc.—has increasingly been appropriated to portray Israel (and, relevantly, members of the Jewish community who support it) as morally evil, often to the point of being equated to Nazis.” 

Segal doesn’t bother disputing the many well-evidenced allegations of apartheid, ethnic cleansing and genocide levelled at Israel. Nor does she consider that comparisons to the Nazis might diminish if Israel dismantled its concentration camps and Israeli politicians stopped quoting Hitler. Her report is remarkably devoid of any facts or engagement with arguments and counter-arguments. It reads like a News Corp opinion piece.

That’s because her primary objective is to dismiss criticism of Israel out of hand on the basis that it inevitably leads to anti-Jewish racism. While she concedes that criticism of Israel is not

inherently

antisemitic, she argues it is “utilised to create an environment where that sentiment can so easily morph into hostility towards Jewish people”. She terms this “ambient antisemitism”, which increases the danger of “conflation”, where “Jews in Australia are treated as collectively responsible for the actions of Israel”. 

There

is

 a danger that people disgusted by Israel’s actions misdirect their anger toward Jewish people as a whole. The Palestine solidarity movement has made every effort to combat this by distinguishing between Jewish people as a politically diverse religious and ethnic group on the one hand, and the state of Israel on the other. 

Segal, for her part, reinforces this conflation. It is laid out explicitly in her report: “Jewish identity is inherently linked to the land of Israel; it is central to the existence of Jewish people, the Jewish religion and culture”. This is echoed by Israeli politicians who cynically claim to represent the

entire Jewish community

 while committing unspeakable crimes. 

So far, these are the predictable arguments of the pro-Israel right. But as you dig deeper into the report, things get weirder. Segal thinks progressive antisemitism is dangerous not only because it legitimises criticism of Israel, but because it can act as a Trojan horse for more sinister ideologies.

Mainstream progressives are guilty, in her eyes, of “effectively laundering far-left antisemitism and Islamic extremism through a progressive lens … giving fundamentally extremist ideologies an apparently acceptable face”. 

Segal’s report makes repeated reference to this supposed intersection of radical-left politics and Islamic extremism, sanitised and promoted by respectable liberals. It is a wild conspiracy theory, one that sounds remarkably similar to Trump’s recent rants blaming rioting in France on an alliance of “migrants, jihadists, and communists”.

The language in her report mirrors that of right-wing intellectuals and government ministers overseas who rail against “Islamo-leftism”. This is the new iteration of the old myth of “Judeo-Bolshevism”, a …

author: Χαρά Καριοφύλη | Chara Kariofyli
title: «Τεχνητή νοημοσύνη» στα προσφυγικά στρατόπεδα (και αλλού;)
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

«Τεχνητή νοημοσύνη» στα προσφυγικά στρατόπεδα (και αλλού;)


Τέσσερα ολόκληρα χρόνια έχουν περάσει από την λειτουργία των συστημάτων

«Κένταυρος»

 και

«Υπερίων»

 στην Κλειστή Ελεγχόμενη Δομή (ΚΕΔ) της Σάμου, πρώην Κέντρο Υποδοχής και Ταυτοποίησης (ΚΥΤ). Το σύστημα «Κένταυρος» μπήκε σε λειτουργία τον Σεπτέμβριο του 2021, και ακολούθησε το σύστημα «Υπερίων», χωρίς το Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Ασύλου (ΥΜΑ) να έχει πραγματοποιήσει τις απαραίτητες διαδικασίες που υποχρεούται, βάσει νόμου, δημιουργώντας μια ζώνη αδιαφάνειας σε ότι αφορά τη συλλογή και την προστασία των προσωπικών δεδομένων σε αυτά.


Δύο

διοικητικά πρόστιμα

 για παραβιάσεις προσωπικών δεδομένων επιβλήθηκαν από την Αρχή Προστασίας Δεδομένων Προσωπικού Χαρακτήρα (ΑΠΔΠΧ), καθώς το Υπουργείο χρησιμοποιούσε λογισμικά τεχνητής «νοημοσύνης» κάτω από άκρα μυστικότητα. Όπως προκύπτει από την έρευνά μας για αυτό το ρεπορτάζ, το Υπουργείο χρησιμοποιεί και άλλες τεχνολογίες τεχνητής «νοημοσύνης» για τις οποίες δεν έχει υπάρξει η απαραίτητη ενημέρωση, συλλέγοντας μια πληθώρα δεδομένων από τους προσφυγικούς πληθυσμούς υπό πλήρη αδιαφάνεια. 


Το χρονικό των συστημάτων «Κένταυρος» και «Υπερίων»


Όπως είναι γνωστό, η οργάνωση για τα ψηφιακά δικαιώματα Homo Digitalis, μαζί με την Ελληνική Ένωση για τα Δικαιώματα του Ανθρώπου (ΕλΕΔΑ), την οργάνωση νομικής βοήθειας HIAS Greece και την ακαδημαϊκό Νιόβη Βάβουλα,

υπέβαλαν αίτημα παροχής πληροφοριών

 τον Φεβρουάριο του 2022, στην Αρχή Προστασίας Δεδομένων Προσωπικού Χαρακτήρα (ΑΠΔΠΧ) για να εξετάσει εάν τα συστήματα «Κένταυρος» και «Υπερίων» συμμορφώνονται με τους κανόνες της ΕΕ σχετικά με την επεξεργασία δεδομένων προσωπικού χαρακτήρα και εάν έχει διενεργηθεί

Εκτίμηση Αντικτύπου σχετικά με την Προστασία Δεδομένων

 (ΕΑΠΔ), μια μελέτη που πρέπει υποχρεωτικά να συνοδεύει εγκαταστάσεις μαζικής συλλογής και επεξεργασίας δεδομένων. 


Η έρευνα της ΑΠΔΠΧ ξεκίνησε τον Μάρτιο του 2022 και αφού διαπιστώθηκαν μια σειρά από παραβάσεις διατάξεων που αφορούν την προστασία δεδομένων, επέβαλε δύο διοικητικά πρόστιμα ύψους 175.000 ευρώ στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Ασύλου, στις 2 Απριλίου 2024.


Ποιες διατάξεις παραβιάζονται και πώς:

Άρθρα του ΓΚΠΔ (GDPR): 5(1)(α), 6(1), 12, 13, 14, 15(ε), 25, 30, 35, 58(1)(ε))

Οι παραβιάσεις του ΓΚΠΔ αφορούν την απουσία νόμιμης, δίκαιης και διαφανούς διαδικασίας συλλογής δεδομένων, την απουσία συγκατάθεσης από τα υποκείμενα των δεδομένων, την απουσία διαφανών πληροφοριών, επικοινωνίας και τρόπων άσκησης των δικαιωμάτων του υποκειμένου των δεδομένων, την απουσία πληροφοριών σχετικά με την ταυτότητα και τα στοιχεία επικοινωνίας του υπεύθυνου επεξεργασίας, τους σκοπούς και τη νομική βάση της επεξεργασίας, τις κατηγορίες δεδομένων, τη διάρκεια αποθήκευσης, την ύπαρξη του δικαιώματος να ζητηθεί πρόσβαση, διόρθωση ή διαγραφή προσωπικών δεδομένων ή περιορισμός της επεξεργασίας προσωπικών δεδομένων, την ύπαρξη του δικαιώματος ανάκλησης της συγκατάθεσης ανά πάσα στιγμή, το δικαίωμα υποβολής καταγγελίας, η πηγή από την οποία προέρχονται τα προσωπικά δεδομένα, η έλλειψη κατάλληλων τεχνικών και οργανωτικών μέτρων που αποσκοπούν στην εφαρμογή των αρχών προστασίας των δεδομένων, η έλλειψη αρχείων καταγραφής των δραστηριοτήτων επεξεργασίας, η έλλειψη ΕΑΠΔ, καθώς και η έλλειψη της δυνατότητας της εποπτικής αρχής να αποκτά, από τον υπεύθυνο επεξεργασίας και τον εκτελούντα την επεξεργασία, πρόσβαση σε όλα τα προσωπικά δεδομένα και σε όλες τις πληροφορίες που είναι απαραίτητες για την εκτέλεση των καθηκόντων της.


Η ΑΠΔΠΧ μέσω της έρευνάς της διαπίστωσε ότι το Υπουργείο δεν είχε πραγματοποιήσει

Εκτίμηση Αντικτύπου σχετικά με την Προστασία Δεδομένων

 (ΕΑΠΔ) η οποία πρέπει να διεξάγεται ήδη από τον σχεδιασμό των συστημάτων και όχι ύστερα από την εφαρμογή τους, ενώ, παράλληλα, δεν διέθετε ούτε

Υπεύθυνο Προστασίας Δεδομένων

 (Data Protection Officer – DPO, όπως προβλέπεται από τον GDPR) κατά την διαδικασία σχεδιασμού αλλά και χρήσης των συστημάτων. 


Επιπλέον, το Υπουργείο, έχοντας τρεις μήνες διορία για να παραδώσει στην ΑΠΔΠΧ τις απαραίτητες πληροφορίες που υποχρεούται για τα δύο συστήματα, παρέδωσε την Εκτίμηση Αντικτύπου σαφώς καθυστερημένα αλλά και γεμάτη ασάφειες, ελλείψεις και αντιφατικές πληροφορίες.

author: Kelly Hayes
title: Here’s How to Secure Your Phone Ahead of Holiday Travel
content:
These steps make it a lot harder for the state to target and repress our movements.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

With the holidays approaching, many of us will soon be navigating airport security. That’s stressful enough, especially given the technical breakdowns we’ve seen lately. For activists and organizers, air travel can bring additional concerns, including the possibility of federal agents attempting to search or confiscate our devices.

After hearing about a recent incident in which border agents demanded access to a friend’s phone, I thought this would be a good time to revisit the subject of device security for activists who are headed to the airport. From the basic precautions everyone should be taking to more extensive measures, like using a secondary phone, I talked through our options with Troy*, an organizer with the Activist Checklist project. Activist Checklist is a website that offers practical checklists and tools to help activists protect their devices, communications, and sensitive information during protests, travel, and other potentially risky situations.

*Troy is a pseudonym used for safety reasons.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Kelly Hayes: We’ve seen a number of disturbing stories about activists and journalists having their phones searched or confiscated at airports. Activist Checklist distinguishes between basic security precautions everyone should take and enhanced protections for people who may face greater risks. How should people assess their own level of risk, particularly when traveling, and determine what kinds of precautions are appropriate for their circumstances?

Troy: It’s definitely the case that not all digital security advice is applicable to everyone. If you’re a US citizen crossing a border or taking a flight, start by asking yourself two questions.

First, how likely am I to be targeted for a device search? Since Trump took office in 2025, we’ve seen an increase in politically motivated device seizures at the border, often targeting people with a public profile in pro-Palestine, anti-ICE, and direct action organizing.

Second, if the cops did break into my phone, how much danger would the data on it expose other people to? We encourage folks to go beyond an individual view of their digital security and focus more on the risk to their communities. The consequences might be relatively low, such as revealing who you organize with in a lower-risk setting. If, on the other hand, you’re doing something like immigrant mutual aid and your Signal chats have the addresses of the undocumented folks you deliver groceries to, that could put them at serious risk, and you should definitely take more precautions. That might include backing up and then wiping your phone, or only traveling with a secondary phone.

Our resources are geared toward US citizens, so if you’re a visa holder or green card holder, you may want to check out the Asian Law Caucus’s resource Know Your Rights at Airports: International and Domestic.

I think people should also think about who they’re communicating with, and whether those people are likely to be targeted by the government. I’ve sat in court and watched prosecutors twist seemingly harmless personal messages into evidence. So if you’re shooting the shit about politics with people doing the kind of work the government seems hyped to criminalize, it’s worth thinking about how much of that conversation history you’re carrying around on your phone. Turning on Signal’s disappearing messages option is a worthwhile precaution, but it’s also important to think about what you’ve already got stored.

Now, let’s talk about what people can do before they leave home. If someone has limited time to prepare for a trip, what are the most important steps they can take to secure their phone or laptop? What difference do things like stronger passcodes, disabling facial recognition, and powering down a device actually make?

Fully power off your phone anytime you’re in a situation where the cops might confiscate it. That includes TSA, customs, immigration, or even higher-risk protests or actions. In addition, make sure to update your phone to the latest operating system version and use a randomly generated passcode that is eight or more digits. As long as you do those three things — updates, a strong passcode, fully powered …

author: Sebastian Lotzer
title: City of Blood [Part V]
content:
“Aber mit den richtigen Augen, die zur richtigen Zeit an die richtigen Stellen schauen, kann man vielleicht den düsteren Schatten der Zukunft sehen, der von Blitzen überirdischen Lichts durchbrochen wird: blendend helle Momente, in denen für einen flüchtigen Augenblick die Perspektive auf Gerechtigkeit erscheint. Das Polizeirevier brennt, die Arbeiter strömen aus der Fabrik, Komitees bilden sich auf den Straßen und in den Dörfern, die Regierung fällt so sanft wie eine Feder, drei Patronenhülsen fallen wie Würfel – in jede ist eine Beschwörungsformel eingraviert, als wolle sie etwas Größeres heraufbeschwören. Vielleicht haben Sie es schon einmal gespürt. Das Herz wird leicht. Engelhaftes Feuer durchströmt das Fleisch, und für diesen einen atemlosen Moment wohnt etwas Unsterbliches in uns. Die Klinge des Meteors schneidet durch den Bauch eines mondlosen Himmels, und dann blinzeln wir, und es ist vorbei: Die Nationalgarde wird gerufen, die Gewerkschaften verhandeln eine Rückkehr zur Arbeit, die Komitees lösen sich auf, der gestürzte Präsident wird durch den Militärrat ersetzt, der tote CEO wird durch einen lebenden ersetzt, und Polizeikugeln fallen wie kalter, harter Regen aus den Glastürmen. Aber das Licht kann nicht ungesehen gemacht werden. Infolgedessen ist gerade diese Niederlage selbst ein Erwachen. Langsam erkennen wir, dass der kollektive, expansive Charakter des Bösen, das uns plagt, eine kollektive, expansive Form der Vergeltung erfordert. Soziale Rache erfordert eine soziale Waffe. Der Name dieser Waffe lautet Kommunistische Partei.”


Phil A. Neel – Theorie der Partei [1]


Nun, das war also ‘Genz Z regelt – Phase 2’ in Berlin. Gut tausend Leute am Savignyplatz, eigentlich nur das übliche etwas jüngere Demopublikum, vorneweg die neuen “Roten Gruppen” mit ihren unauffälligen scharlachroten Sturmhauben, in völliger Abwesenheit des migrantischen Surplus-Proletariats geht es im Wanderkessel der Berliner Bullen über den Kurfürstendamm, am Ende gibt es die übliche Keile durch die Ordnungsmacht. Wann immer die üblichen linken und anarchistischen Verdächtigen von einer neuen “Bewegung” schwadronieren, kann man sich sicher sein, dass alles schon vorbei bzw. erfolgreich in die üblichen Sackgassen manövriert worden ist. Da können dann auch ganz beruhigt selbst die Grünen auf den Zug aufspringen und ihre “volle Solidarität” mit den “Gen Z Protesten” bekunden, was aber wohl nicht einen Solidaritätsfond für die bei den Krawallen an Halloween Festgenommenen inkludiert.


Es ist kein Zufall, dass es in Deutschland nur noch an Tagen knallt, an denen der Exzess diesen normativen Zustandes, der so sehr in den tiefsten Strukturen der Seelen schmerzt, für zumindestens ein paar Stunden durchbricht: wie Silvester 22/23 und jetzt also Halloween 2026. Geister, die kommen und verschwinden, alles liegt in einem dichten Nebel, in diesem Fall aus Pyrotechnik, schemenhaft nur werden die Umrisse des sozialen Antagonismus sichtbar, der dieser Konfliktualität zugrunde liegt. Früher, bevor die Postautonomen und die Trotzkisten den 1. Mai beerbt haben, war auch dieser Tag ein solcher exzessiver Raum, genauso wie ab Anfang der 90er die Walpurgisnacht. Wir sehen, wir werden sie nicht los, die Geister und Fabelwesen… Kein Mensch interessierte sich je für die Programme und Aufrufe zum 1. Mai, die ewig gleichen Redebeiträge, die Szene-Debatten über die Routenführung. Die einzige Frage war ob und wo es knallt. Da wollte man dabei sein. Und auch da schon das migrantische Surplus Proletariat, nur dass das damals noch nicht so hieß. Teile von Antifaşist Gençlik hatten das begriffen, im Gegensatz zu dem überwiegenden Teil der weißen deutschen autonomen Szene. Deshalb die massive staatliche Repression, nachdem bei einer Auseinandersetzung mit Kadern der Faschos in Kreuzberg Gerhard Kaindl tot liegen geblieben war. Mitten im rassistischen Taumel von Hoyerswerda, Rostock-Lichtenhagen und Mölln. Die Entpolitisierung von und Hetze gegen die migrantische Selbstermächtigung, wie man heutzutage sagen würde, zieht sich, wie wir sehen, durch die Jahrzehnte.
