author: Unknown
title: Rudolf Rocker - Nationalisme et culture
content:
Auteur·e

: Rudolf Rocker

Titre

: Nationalisme et culture

Date

: septembre 2008


RUDOLF ROCKER NATIONALISME & CULTURE


 Rudolf Rocker Dessin de son fils Fermin


Présentation


Le 28 février

, les cendres du Reichstag encore fumantes, les Rocker décident que, pour eux aussi, c’est le moment d’abandonner l’Allemagne. Ils pensent aller voir le vieux compagnon Wilhelm Werner pour essayer de résoudre avec lui les nombreux problèmes qui surgissent devant un départ précipité, et Milly sort pour faire quelques courses pendant que Rudolf rassemble les feuilles d’un livre qu’il vient de terminer quelques jours auparavant.


 Mais Milly ne fait pas ses courses. Dans la rue, un marchand ambulant ami l’informe

sotto voce

 qu’Erich Mühsam vient d’être enlevé par la police secrète.


 Mühsam habite le même quartier de Berlin que Rocker, et ils se voient presque quotidiennement dans ces temps agités où les SA, troupes de choc du NSDAP

[1]

, font régner la terreur brune.


 Tous les révolutionnaires, tous les opposants au nazisme, étaient en danger de mort, surtout Erich Mühsam, Juif, anarchiste connu, actif participant avec Gustav Landauer aux événements révolutionnaires de Munich en 1919 (République des conseils de Bavière). Werner et Rocker, deux jours avant l’incendie du Reichstag, avaient convaincu Mühsam, réticent, de sortir du pays sans tarder. Cependant, il voulait laisser les affaires en ordre et retarda son départ. Hésitation qui lui fut fatale. Zensl, sa compagne, racontera qu’il avait le billet pour Prague dans sa poche au moment de son arrestation.

[2]


 Dans la banlieue sud de Berlin, dans ce faubourg de Britz, il y avait très peu de gens dans la rue les jours de travail, et en s’assurant de sa fenêtre qu’il n’y avait pas de mouvements suspects aux alentours, Milly Witkop et Rudolf Rocker, entreprennent la fuite d’une Allemagne livrée maintenant à la furie destructrice du nazisme. Ils ne portent pas de valises pour ne pas éveiller des soupçons, et Rocker prend sous le bras le manuscrit de

Nationalisme et culture

, fruit d’un long travail commencé à l’époque de son premier exil en 1892.


 Les idées qui imprègnent les pages de ce livre se sont formées petit à petit dans l’esprit de l’auteur, au cours de son chemin militant et de l’errance, premièrement à Paris puis à Londres, et elles ont pu s’exprimer par bribes dans des articles et des conférences jusqu’à la brutale interruption imposée par la guerre de 1914 et l’internement pendant quatre ans dans des camps, l’Olympia et l’Alexandra Palace, où il a été jeté par le gouvernement britannique en tant qu’« expatrié ennemi ».


 Expulsé vers l’Allemagne en 1918 avant l’armistice, il arrive, au bout de diverses péripéties, à se réfugier en Hollande. Et, à la fin de l’année, Rocker est à nouveau dans son pays d’origine après vingt-six ans d’absence. L’agitation politique y est fébrile entre les insurrections spartakistes et la révolution de Munich, et elles sont suivies d’une répression sanglante. Ces temps-là n’étaient pas propices au travail intellectuel et d’autres tâches plus urgentes sollicitent Rocker.


 En décembre 1919, se réunissait à Berlin le douzième congrès de la FVDG (

Freie Verinigung deutscher Gewerkschaften

) où Rocker présente les principes de l’organisation révolutionnaire anarcho-syndicaliste. Ce congrès propose aux vieilles associations qui composent la FVDG, dissoute pendant la guerre, de changer de nom et d’agir dorénavant en tant que

Freie Arbeiter Union Deutschland

 (FAUD), comme il avait été décidé à la Conférence de Düsseldorf en septembre de la même année. La force numérique du mouvement se multiplia atteignant le chiffre de 150 000 membres en 1921. Rocker s’engage profondément dans la construction de l’organisation ouvrière, et il parcourt le pays en donnant des conférences, en participant à des meetings publics et à des réunions organisationnelles. « Quelle que soit – écrit-il dans ses Mémoires – la façon dont on juge la situation en Europe après la Première Guerre mondiale, il est indubitable que la conflagration avait créé une situation révolutionnaire qui justifiait des attitudes d’attente porteuses de grands espoirs. »


 À ce moment, Trotsky et Lossovsky cherchent à mettre sur pied l’Internationale syndicale rouge, et invitent à Moscou pour le 1er mai 1921, les syndicalistes et les révolutionnaires, y compris les anarchistes, de tous les pays, mais il est clair que l’ISR resterait soumise à la politique du Kominterm …

author: Indo
title: On “Sultat al-Majalis”
content:
Rather interesting text on the Arab Council Communist group “Sultat al-Majalis” formed by Lafif Lakhdar and Mustapha Khayati. Originally published in "Al-Hewar Al-Mutamadin, Issue 8699, 6th May 2026”. Can be found here.

The Arab Communist Grouping, which published the magazine Sultat al-Majalis (The Power of Workers’ Councils), was a revolutionary organization that adopted the ideas of council communism, drawing inspiration from the experiences of workers’ councils in Europe. The group was active in the early 1970s and consisted of intellectuals and workers of Maghrebi (North African) origin living in France. Its members were influenced by the events of May 1968 in France and by the left-wing critique of the existing socialist regimes of the time.

The group focused on the idea that revolution should be led by workers’ councils elected directly by the workers themselves. It rejected the traditional Leninist party model and centralized bureaucratic authority. It regarded Soviet communism, as well as its Chinese Maoist counterpart, as systems that had nothing to do with socialism. In its view, both were forms of state capitalism, owned and controlled by a new class known as the bureaucracy, which, like the bourgeoisie, was hostile to the working class and its independent movement.

The organization also launched a scathing critique of existing Arab regimes, whether self-proclaimed progressive or conservative, as well as all Palestinian organizations and the very idea of a Palestinian revolution, insofar as it remained detached from an all-encompassing Arab revolution aimed at overthrowing the existing state structures across the various Arab countries.

The first and only issue of Sultat al-Majalis was published in January 1974. Its purpose was to promote awareness of the self-organization of workers and peasants, free from the tutelage of political parties. The magazine included translations of texts by leading international theorists of council communism, articles analyzing the Arab-Israeli conflict from a class-based perspective that rejected nationalism, and studies of Arab labor movements.

Despite its limited organizational base, the group had a notable intellectual influence in independent left-wing circles and helped introduce concepts of workers’ self-management. It remains one of the distinctive experiments in the history of the Arab Left, representing an attempt to offer a third alternative outside the frameworks of Arab nationalism and official communism aligned with Moscow.

The group operated clandestinely, which meant that some of its contributors wrote under pseudonyms while others remained behind the scenes. Its initial core included young university graduates from Beirut who had been influenced by the global New Left movement but chose to work under the umbrella of the group in order to distinguish themselves from the official communist parties and the Organization of Communist Action in Lebanon.

The relationship between Lafif Lakhdar (1934–2013) and Mustapha Khayati was central to the establishment of this tendency. In his writings, Lafif Lakhdar confirmed that he and Mustapha Khayati had overseen the publication of Sultat al-Majalis.

Mustapha Khayati was a Tunisian activist and intellectual, a prominent member of the Situationist International in France, and the author of the famous pamphlet On the Poverty of Student Life. Khayati brought Situationist thought and the critique of the “Society of the Spectacle” into the Arab context, an influence that was reflected in the pages of Sultat al-Majalis.

Lafif Lakhdar was a radical left-wing Tunisian intellectual and one of the most outspoken critics of state capitalism in the Soviet Union and the Arab regimes. He argued that the genuine alternative lay in the “power of workers’ councils,” exercising self-management. This position formed the central ideological identity of the group.

The magazine served as a platform through which Khayati and Lakhdar translated unorthodox Marxist texts and analyzed Arab conflicts from an internationalist perspective.

Regarding the joint activities of three members of the group in early 1970, before its formal establishment, the Palestinian journalist Bilal al-Hassan wrote the following in an article discussing the book Nayef Hawatmeh Speaks, published in Beirut in 1997:

“... After the name of the Democratic Front [for the Liberation of Palestine] became widely known, along with its Marxist orientation, large …

В маленькой редакционной комнате еженедельной пропагандистской газеты мы с наслаждением предавались дружеской беседе между товарищами, как вдруг вошёл рослый парень с ремнём за плечами.

Он весело поздоровался с присутствующими, расстегнул ремни, поставил ящик на пол и сел на него, вытирая пот.

Пока мы ждали, что он заговорит, мы молча рассматривали его. Это был высокий, широкоплечий юноша с чёрными усиками на смуглой, загорелой коже и живыми, искрящимися глазами, как пенистое вино. Одет он был в деревенскую одежду, с некоторыми городскими штрихами или отголосками города.

Наконец, с улыбкой, очень непринуждённо, гость назвал своё имя.

Администратор газеты прекрасно знал его как неутомимого активиста, который очень часто писал ему – то из одного населённого пункта, то из другого – и с дьявольской энергией распространял брошюры. Где бы он ни проходил, люди массами подписывались на газету. Если он не был коммивояжёром, то уж точно был Вечным жидом[1]… – Вечным жидом пропаганды, – сказал парень с ящиком, широко и довольно улыбаясь.

И поскольку на наших лицах откровенно разливалась жадная любопытность, он принялся в общих чертах рассказывать о своей кочевой жизни.

В городе он был механиком и уже зарабатывал хорошую зарплату. Но, будучи человеком читающим и стремящимся к знаниям, завсегдатаем собраний, жадно ловившим каждое слово из дискуссий, которые велись в помещении профсоюза, он вскоре воспламенился нашим прекрасным идеалом человеческого освобождения. И тут же его охватила ненасытная жажда обращать в свою веру, тут же его озаботила великая проблема сельской пропаганды, сеяния за пределами промышленных центров – по этим обширным невозделанным полям провинции, тревожным и полным тайны. Далеко ли может зайти любая попытка городского рабочего, одинокого и встречающего враждебность? Почему бы не последовать прекрасному примеру русских революционеров, которые идут жить и работать среди крестьян?

Молодой и крепкий, без семейных обязательств, в один прекрасный день наш парень отправился по этим землям. Он запасся полезными и дешёвыми предметами, которые продавал с минимальной прибылью. Он изучил основы различных ремёсел и был на селе услужливым умельцем на все руки. В деревенских хижинах не было мебели или утвари, которую он не сумел бы починить или даже изготовить. Он даже чинил грубую обувь, за неимением сапожника, и нередко видели, как он вносил свой изобретательный вклад в ремонт или строительство домов…

При этом он довольствовался малым. Есть и спать – как придётся: иногда лучше, иногда хуже; иногда за несколько грошей, иногда в уплату за работу. В жаркое время он не брезговал спать под открытым небом, на гумнах или под скирдами. Умирать – не умирал. В общем: жил помаленьку – и со здоровьицем…

Таким образом он быстро завоёвывал сердца и доверие людей из деревень и маленьких городков, которые внимательно слушали его беседы и публичные чтения, охотно принимали его брошюры и газеты, задумчиво следили за ясными и светлыми картинами будущего, будущего с большей свободой и большим довольством.

Мы с волнением смотрели на доброго сеятеля, запоминая его облик и черты, словно пытаясь увидеть воплощение той благороднейшей страсти и того животворящего героизма.

— Вот уже пять лет веду эту жизнь, – просто заключил он.

Мы предположили, что он имеет в виду холеру и месть властей. Нет; мы поняли неправильно: речь шла об узах любви. Случаев и соблазнов ему не хватало; и не то чтобы он хвастался, но о многих он знал, что они не сказали бы ему «нет»… Но, честно говоря, решение не казалось ему из самых лёгких, как и не находил он лёгким найти женщину, которая бы ему подошла. Ужасная проблема…

И когда доблестный парень собрался уходить, уже приготовив свой запас печатной …

author: Unknown
title: Agnes Grundel - Novemberminnen
content:
Författare

: Agnes Grundel

Titel

: Novemberminnen

Källa

: Allarm november 1916


 Ett år har förflutit sedan vår kamrat, frihetskämpen Josef Hillström slöt sina av förtryck betyngda ögon, för att aldrig mera skåda den värld som fråntog honom allt - ja till och med rätten att leva. I den värld där han strävade att frigöra människorna, var hans egen frihet osäker. I det samhälle där han agiterade med varje gnista av sin outtröttliga energi, var hans liv icke tryggat.


Varför?

 Jo: Därför att han hade hjältemod nog att trotsa, att opponera sig mot våldets blodtörstige tyranner, som alltid mördat och stympat, bränt och krossat alla dem som försökt vrida makten ur deras järnklor, samt ersätta människornas lidande med lycka.


 Alla dem som i någon mån försökt att förbättra mänsklighetens förhållanden, alla dem som vågat fråga: med vad rätt kunna dessa legaliserade ogärningsmän tvinga mig att arbeta för dem, samt bestjäla mig produkten av mitt arbete, alltid ha de fått falla offer för den s. k. rättvisan. Sådana män äro farliga för förtryckarna, enär de ha förmågan att väcka andra och få dem att göra gemensam aktion mot förtrycket, därför måste de rödjas ur vägen.


 Josef Hillström var en av de oböjlige. Ingenting förfärade honom, in i dödens käftar trotsade han dem alla. De togo hans unga kraftiga, förhoppningsfulla liv, men hans skändligt utgjutna blod ropar på hämd, från alla delar av jorden juder det som av en tordönsstämma:

hämnd

. Så länge här finnes en slav, komma hans brännande odödliga ord och eldiga entusiasm inspirera miljoner till verksamhet.


 Josef Hillström har ej levat förgäves, oaktat han dog i blomman av sitt liv. Det säges han var en drömmare, kanske så, enär hans idé ännu ej hunnit bliva förverkligad, men han drömde ej när han i sina sånger gav slavarna råd huru att bekriga sina svurna dödsfiender. Det var realisten Joe Hill vi minnas och vörda.


 Joe Hill drömde om en bättre värld där arbetaren skördar fulla produkten av sitt arbete, där nyttiga medborgare styra samhället till allas bästa, där list, lögn, våld och bedrägeri ej längre triumferar, där små barn vårdas som praktfulla blommor.


 Att han lärde slavarna att förverkliga detta, däri låg Joe Hills brott. Någon invände hånfullt att han gick i döden för en kvinnas skull. Ja alltid ha frihetshjältar förhånats av den okunniga massan. Vi minnas kanske Robert Emmet, Irlands store frihetskämpe, en Voltaire, Thomas Payne m. fl.


 Samtidigt som Joe Hill mördades i SAlt Lake hade de samhällsbevarande här i staden konferens varvid en av de viktigaste frågorna för dagen var:

hur skola vi kunna fördriva I. W. W. männen ur U. S. A.

 Detta visar att dessa herrar tycka sig redan nu se hur deras makts sista dagar börja randas. De mötas för att uppgöra planer huru att på bästa sätt tillintetgöra denna organisation. En av deras planer är väl känd och praktiseras ofta, den att mörda de aktive ledande männen. För denna metod föll vår präktige Joe Hill, för samma försöka de få de tre kamraterna i norra Minnesota: Joe Smidt, Carlo Tresca och Sam Scharlet. Allt beror på er arbetare om de även i detta fallet skola lyckas. Skola vi låta våldets bödlar döda våra bästa och aktivaste kamrater. Nej. Låt oss visa att vi äro män och kvinnor med ett för rätt och frihet klappande hjärta och med mod att handla.


 Vi kunna ej bättre vörda Joe Hills minne än att följa hans sista uppmaning till världens arbetare:

Organisera.

title: Anarchist Parenting
content:
Author:

An Anarchist FAQ


PDF File Size:

 381 KB


Download PDF


The Anarchist FAQ presents a compelling vision of parenting based on freedom, mutual respect and trust in children’s natural capacity for self-regulation, challenging the authoritarian assumptions embedded in conventional family structures. Its strongest contribution is connecting the personal and political, arguing that raising children without coercion, punishment or imposed moralism is itself a form of anarchist practice. It places freedom, mutual respect and autonomy at the heart of parenting. It challenges us to reject the authoritarian structures of the traditional family and recognise that raising free, confident and independent children is an essential part of building a free society.


Source:

 An Anarchist FAQ found at

https://ananarchistfaq.anarcho-copy.org/


Read more

: Anarchist Parenting


Anarchist Parenting


 An Anarchist FAQ


 


Introduction:

 What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Part 1:

 What are the main obstacles to raising free children?


Part 2:

What are some examples of libertarian child-rearing methods?


Part 3:

 If children have nothing to fear, how can they be good?


Part 4:

 But how will a free child ever learn unselfishness?


Part 5:

 Isn’t “libertarian child-rearing” just another name for spoiling the child?


Part 6:

What is the anarchist position on teenage sexual liberation?


Part 7:

 But isn’t this concern with sexual liberation just a distraction from revolution?


Introduction:

What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Anarchists have long been aware of the importance of child rearing and education. We are aware that child rearing should aim to develop

“a well-rounded individuality”

 and not

“a patient work slave, professional automaton, tax-paying citizen, or righteous moralist.”

 In this section of the FAQ [see

here

] we will discuss anarchist approaches to child rearing bearing in mind

“that it is through the channel of the child that the development of the mature man [or woman] must go, and that the present ideas of . . . educating or training . . . are such as to stifle the natural growth of the child.”

 [Emma Goldman,

Red Emma Speaks

, p. 132 and p. 131]


If one accepts the thesis that the authoritarian family is the breeding ground for both individual psychological problems and political reaction, it follows that anarchists should try to develop ways of raising children that will not psychologically cripple them but instead enable them to accept freedom and responsibility while developing natural self-regulation. We will refer to children raised in such a way as

“free children.”


Work in this field is still in its infancy (no pun intended). Wilhelm Reich was the main pioneer in this field (an excellent, short introduction to his ideas can be found in Maurice Brinton’s

The Irrational in Politics

). In

Children of the Future

, Reich made numerous suggestions, based on his research and clinical experience, for parents, psychologists, and educators striving to develop libertarian methods of child rearing (although he did not use the term “libertarian”).


In this and the following sections we will summarise Reich’s main ideas as well as those of other libertarian psychologists and educators who have been influenced by him, such as A.S. Neill and Alexander Lowen. We will examine the theoretical principles involved in raising free children and will illustrate their practical application with concrete examples. Finally, we will examine the anarchist approach to the problems of adolescence.


Such an approach to child rearing is based upon the insight that children

“do not constitute anyone’s property: they are neither the property of the parents nor even of society. They belong only to their own future freedom.”

 [Michael Bakunin,

The Political Philosophy of Bakunin

, p. 327] As such, what happens to a child when they are growing up

shapes

 the person they become and the society they live in. The key question for people interested in freedom is whether

“the child [is] to be considered as an individuality, or as an object to be moulded according to the whims and fancies of those about it?”

 [Emma Goldman,

Op. Cit.

, p. 131] Libertarian child rearing is the means by which the individuality of the child is respected and developed.


This is in stark contrast to standard capitalist claim that children are the

property

 of their parents …

Anarchie ist ein fortlaufender Prozess zur Demontage von Autorität.

Anarchie ist die unerbittliche Verneinung von Herrschaftsstrukturen, das Bestreben, sich kleine Bereiche des Lebens frei von Ausbeutung und Leid zu schaffen.

Anarchie ist der kompromisslose Vorstoß gegen Unterdrückung und die lautstarke Forderung nach Autonomie und Selbstbestimmung, die Ablehnung aller Klassen, Institutionen und Dogmen, die geschaffen wurden, um Menschen zu beherrschen.

Anarchie ist vor allem eine Praxis, nicht eine Theorie. Es geht darum, aktiv daran zu arbeiten, autoritäre Verhältnisse zu beenden, wo immer sie existieren, und nicht-autoritäre Alternativen aufzubauen. Es geht nicht darum, eine Lebensweise für einen imaginären Ort, eine imaginäre Zeit und imaginäre Menschen vorzuschreiben. Es geht um reale Menschen und die Bewältigung realer Probleme.

Anarchie ist eine lebendige und atmende Praxis, die wir in unser tägliches Leben einbauen. Eine persönliche Haltung gegen die Herrschaft, die alle unsere Entscheidungen beeinflusst und so den Verlauf unserer Existenz prägt.

Es gibt kein Endziel für Anarchie. Sie ist ein fortwährender, nicht enden wollender Kampf gegen hierarchische Strukturen und die Autoritätspersonen, die im Luxus an der Spitze dieser Strukturen sitzen.

Anarchie ist der Wunsch nach Freiheit von Tyrannei. Anarchie sind unzählige Generationen verschiedener Menschen mit dem Drang, freier zu sein als sie es unter den Systemen sind, die sie gewaltsam regieren.

Anarchie ist die Ablehnung der Regierung, der Staaten, der Grenzen, des Kapitals, des Patriarchats, des Gender-Essenzialismus, der Sklaverei, der Ideologie, der Rechten, der Linken, des Klerus, der Demokratie, des Privateigentums, der Technokratie, der Kernfamilie, des Humanismus, des Imperialismus, der Gefängnisse, der Fabriken, der Gründerväter, der Bürokratie, der Ethnokratie, der Heteronormativität, der Idole, der Tradition, der Polizeiarbeit, der Neuronormativität, des Ökozids, der Zivilisation und jeder anderen Form von Autorität.

Anarchie ist Gemeinschaftsgärten, Umsonstläden, Graffiti, 3D-gedruckte Waffen, FKK, vegane Potlucks [1], Hausbesetzungen, Lebensmittelwälder, Sabotage von Pipelines, freie Software, die Befreiung von Kühen, Ladendiebstahl, das Sichern von Saatgut alter Kulturpflanzen, die Bildung autonomer Zonen, Attentate auf Tyrannen, Guerilla-Gärtnern, Zines schreiben, Regenwasser auffangen, Wahlurnen verbrennen, Biodiversität, Abschaffung der Whiteness, Hacken, Aquaponik, Musik machen, Upcycling, Polizeistationen abfackeln und Wildblumen in der ganzen Landschaft säen.

Anarchist*innen sind jene Personen, die sich weigern, von irgendjemandem oder irgendetwas regiert, beherrscht oder dominiert zu werden. Anarchist*innen sind wütende, verbitterte, verlorene, ängstliche, desillusionierte, gewalttätige, friedliche, mutige, idealistische, mitreißende, furchtlose Träumende.

Ein*e Anarchist*in steht allein gegen die riesige Flut der Autorität, die in alle Richtungen ansteigt. Anarchist*innen verbinden sich mit jeder geschundenen, geknechteten Seele im gemeinsamen Angriff gegen die rücksichtslosen Systeme, die uns entmachten und entfremden sollen.

Anarchie ist geprägt von endlosen Widersprüchen, existenzieller Angst und unerträglichen inneren Konflikten, und doch ergibt Anarchie für jede Person, die entsetzt oder wütend ist über die groben Ungerechtigkeiten, die diesen kleinen blauen Planeten verschlingen, einen perfekten Sinn. Anarchie ist für jede Person, die ein Leben in Würde anstrebt.

Anarchie ist ein unmögliches, absonderliches, aber für unser Überleben notwendiges Streben.

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. Dan materi-materi tersebut bisa berupa teks, foto, audio, video, dan lain sebagainya. Semua koleksi arsip digital AAA …

Auteur·e

: Agustín Guillamón

Titre

: Les comités de défense de la CNT à Barcelone (1933-1938)

Date

: 2017


 Tampon du Comité de Défense Local de Barcelone


LES COMITÉS DE DÉFENSE DE LA CNT À BARCELONE (1933-1938)


 Des Cadres de Défense aux Comités révolutionnaires de Quartier, aux Patrouilles de contrôle et aux Milices Populaires


AGUSTÍN GUILLAMÓN


 Première édition en espagnol : avril 2011. Seconde édition en espagnol : septembre 2011. Aldarull edicions. Barcelone.


 Ce livre a été traduit par le Collectif Anarchiste de Traduction et de Scannérisation (CATS) de Caen (et d’ailleurs) en avril et mai 2012, avec le concours précieux de l’auteur. Merci à S. de “La Bataille Socialiste” (

http://bataillesocialiste.wordpress.com/

) pour la mise en relation avec l’auteur. D’autres traductions subversives du CATS sont librement téléchargeables et diffusables sur son site :

http://ablogm.com/cats/


 Un premier brouillon initial (très bref) de ce travail fut publié dans le numéro extraordinaire de Solidaridad Obrera (janvier 2010) dédié au centenaire de la CNT.


 Plus de dirigeants, plus d’État Pour profiter de nos combats.


 — Raoul Vaneigem, La vie s’écoule, la vie s’enfuit


 Vivere militare est.


 — Sénèque. Lettres


 I didn’t say it would be easy, Neo. I just said it would be the truth.


 — Morpheus dans Matrix, Larry et Andy Wachowski.


 « Les révolutions sociales, ces tentatives de réorganisation de la production et de la société sur des nouvelles bases, sont extrêmement rares dans l’Histoire. Au delà des circonstances particulières dans lesquelles elles surgirent, elles nous apportent toujours une expérience irremplaçable, dans leurs succès comme, surtout, dans leurs échecs. Le grand enseignement de la révolution de 1936 a été la nécessité incontournable de la destruction de l’État ».


 Barricade construite le 19 Juillet 1936 sur le Paralelo, face à « El Molino ». Ici les Comités de Défense et le Syndicat du Bois de la CNT mirent en déroute l’armée soulevée.


1. DU RAPPORT DE SHAPIRO À CELUI D’OCTOBRE 1934


 Un rapport confidentiel, à la diffusion réduite, d’Alexandre Shapiro

[1]

, secrétaire de l’AIT, élaboré durant son séjour en Espagne en 1932-33, relatait ce qu’étaient et comment fonctionnaient les Comités de Défense, organisés exclusivement pour des tâches insurrectionnelles de choc, comme celle du 8 janvier 1933, dont il fut témoin. Ce rapport de Shapiro, sur les Comités de Défense, fut réalisé en pleine polémique entre FAIstes et trentistes

[2]

 sur l’opportunité, ou non, de la tactique d’insurrection immédiate, localiste et permanente. Shapiro fit une critique dévastatrice de l’improvisation, du manque d’organisation et de préparation de l’insurrection de janvier. Il dénonça, avec dureté, le fait qu’une même personne puisse détenir des charges aux secrétariats de la CNT et du Comité National de Défense, pour le confusionnisme que cela créait. Il démontra que, dans la pratique, s’était produite une soumission de la CNT aux décisions du Comité National des Comités de Défense (CNDC).


 Le rapport de Shapiro, qui bénéficiait de l’aide inestimable d’Eusebio Carbó, décrivait de cette manière les Cadres de Défense, existants en 1933 : « Ces Comités de Défense, qui existaient déjà depuis un certain temps, avaient comme unique but de préparer les armes nécessaires en cas d’insurrection, d’organiser les groupes de choc dans les différents quartiers populaires, d’organiser la résistance des soldats dans les casernes etc… ».


 Alors même que l’insurrection des Asturies était encore en cours, le CNCD constatait, dans un rapport

[3]

, l’échec de la tactique insurrectionnelle, défendue par le groupe Nosotros, connue populairement sous le nom de « gymnastique révolutionnaire », qu’il accusait précisément d’être responsable du manque de préparation de la CNT pour intervenir, au niveau national, dans l’insurrection d’octobre 1934. Le moment était venu de dépasser cette tactique, parce qu’elle avait démontré le caractère absurde et dangereux d’une insurrection locale à un moment inadéquat, sans une sérieuse préparation préalable, qui soumettait les libertaires à la répression étatique, sans jamais obtenir une extension populaire à tout le pays, ni l’adhésion des autres organisations, nécessaire pour affronter avec succès l’appareil militaire et répressif de l’État. Le pire de tout est que cette répression avait démantelé l’appareil militaire clandestin de la CNT, après les insurrections …

author: rezgar2
title: نحو أممية يسارية رقمية في مواجهة الرأسمالية الرقمية، اليسار الرقمي في زمن الخوارزميات
content:
إن المعركة حول التكنولوجيا هي أيضاً معركة حول الملكية والسلطة والوعي ومستقبل البشرية. ومع اتساع دور الفضاء الرقمي بوصفه إحدى الساحات الرئيسية للصراع الطبقي، يمكن للأممية اليسارية الرقمية أن تصبح نقطة انطلاق لتجديد العمل الأممي عموماً. ويتمثل التحدي اليوم في البناء على التشخيص بأدوات جماعية للمواجهة، وفي تطوير التعاون العملي القائم بين قوى اليسار وتوسيعه، ليكمل المواقف والبيانات التضامنية بعمل مشترك أكثر تنظيماً واستمرارية، وفي التوجه التدريجي من منصات الاحتكارات إلى بدائل مستقلة وديمقراطية. وبذلك يمكن أن تتحول إمكانات الثورة الرقمية من امتياز تستأثر به حفنة من الشركات والدول الكبرى إلى مكسب عام يخدم الإنسان وتحرره.

صدر حديثاً كتاب «نحو أممية يسارية رقمية في مواجهة الرأسمالية الرقمية، اليسار الرقمي في زمن الخوارزميات» نصوص ودراسات وبرنامج عمل حول اليسار الرقمي والأممية اليسارية الرقمية، من إعدادي وتأليفي، وهو متاح إلكترونياً ومجاناً.

يشهد العالم ثورة رقمية متسارعة تعيد تشكيل الاقتصاد والعمل والسياسة والوعي الإنساني. وفي الوقت الذي تفتح فيه هذه الثورة إمكانات هائلة للتقدم والتحرر البشري وتجاوز الفقر والأمراض، تتركز ملكية أدواتها ومواردها الأساسية في أيدي حفنة من الاحتكارات الرأسمالية المدعومة من الدول الكبرى. وفي المقابل، تتسع الاحتجاجات الجماهيرية والشبابية في كثير من بلدان العالم، مستفيدة من الأدوات الرقمية في التنظيم والتعبئة، ومؤكدة أن الظروف الموضوعية لتجاوز الرأسمالية قائمة.

ومن هذا التناقض تنبع الحاجة إلى مسار متكامل يبدأ بفهم الرأسمالية الرقمية، ويمر بإغناء تجربة اليسار فكرياً وتنظيمياً بما يواكب التطورات الراهنة، وصولاً إلى بناء أممية يسارية رقمية قادرة على التأثير.

تتيح الثورة الرقمية تقليص ساعات العمل، وتطوير الخدمات الصحية والتعليمية، وتحرير الإنسان من الأعمال المرهقة والمتكررة. غير أن هذه الإمكانات تتطور في إطار علاقات إنتاج رأسمالية، تستحوذ فيها الاحتكارات على القسم الأكبر من مكاسب التقدم التكنولوجي.

فالخوارزميات والمنصات الرقمية ليست محايدة اجتماعياً أو طبقياً، إذ تتأثر بعلاقات الملكية والتمويل والإدارة. وتتجاوز هذه الهيمنة حدود الاقتصاد إلى تشكيل الوعي وتوسيع المراقبة وتوظيف التكنولوجيا في القتل والحروب، ويزيد تقارب بعض قوى اليمين المتطرف مع الاحتكارات التكنولوجية من مخاطر الفاشية الرقمية.

وأمام هذا الواقع، يبرز السؤال الجوهري: كيف يقاوم اليسار الرأسمالية في طورها الرقمي المتقدم، ويفتح الطريق نحو بديل اشتراكي إنساني أكثر عدلاً، محلياً وعالمياً؟ وكيف يجدد نفسه ويطورها ليكون قادراً على ذلك؟

فقد أصبحت الرأسمالية الرقمية قوة عابرة للحدود، بينما يبقى جزء كبير من العمل اليساري الرقمي محصوراً داخل الأطر الوطنية، ويعاني ضعف التنسيق الرقمي الأممي. وتكشف التجارب الحديثة حجم الخطر الذي يواجهه اليسار في هذا الميدان.

ففي البرازيل، وخلال سباق رئاسي بالغ التقارب عام 2026 بين لولا دا سيلفا ومرشح اليمين المتطرف فلافيو بولسونارو، اتهم لولا وحزبه شركة ميتا بتقليص انتشار منشوراته لمصلحة خصمه. وتدخلت المحكمة الانتخابية العليا وألزمت الشركة بتقديم توضيحات، ونشرت صحيفة «فولها دي ساو باولو» مراسلات داخلية يقر فيها موظفون في الشركة بأن قيود المنصة أضرت بحسابات لولا، فيما تحدثت ميتا عن «أعطال تقنية». ورغم ذلك، حسمت التعبئة الجماهيرية جولة الإعادة لصالح لولا.

وفي ألمانيا، وظّف إيلون ماسك منصته «إكس» لدعم حزب «البديل من أجل ألمانيا» اليميني المتطرف قبيل انتخابات فبراير 2025، عبر مقالات التأييد وبثّ حوار مباشر مع زعيمته أليس فايدل، فيما رصدت دراسات انحياز خوارزميات المنصة لصالح محتوى الحزب. وفي كولومبيا، وبعد جولة إعادة حسمت لمرشح اليمين المتطرف بفارق نحو نقطة مئوية واحدة، اتهم الرئيس غوستافو بيترو شركة سايبر إسرائيلية بنشر نصف مليون حساب آلي زائف للتلاعب بالناخبين، وطعن في سلامة برمجيات الفرز وانحياز المنصات الرقمية لليمين المتطرف. ومهما انتهى إليه التحقيق، فإن انتقال الطعن في انتخابات بلد بأكمله إلى ميدان الخوارزميات والحسابات الآلية يكشف طبيعة المرحلة التي نعيشها.

أما المثال الأوضح فجاء من المحكمة الجنائية الدولية. فبعد أن أصدر قضاتها مذكرات توقيف بحق مسؤولين إسرائيليين بتهم ارتكاب جرائم حرب في غزة، فرضت الإدارة الأمريكية عقوبات على عدد من قضاتها ومسؤوليها، فأغلقت شركات أمريكية حساباتهم المصرفية والرقمية. وإذا كانت الرأسمالية مستعدة لفعل ذلك بمحكمة دولية تضم أكثر من مئة وعشرين دولة عضواً، فماذا ستفعل بمشروع يساري يصبح مؤثراً ويسعى إلى كسر هيمنتها، ويتجاوز الخطوط الحمراء التي رسمتها؟

وتمتد هذه الهيمنة إلى الحياة اليومية للناشطات والناشطين، عبر عقوبات رقمية تفرضها المنصات على من يفضح جرائم الحرب الإسرائيلية وانتهاكات دول أخرى، أو يطرح خطاباً يسارياً جذرياً. وتبدأ هذه العقوبات بالتضييق وتقليص الانتشار والتهميش، وتصل إلى حذف المحتوى وإغلاق الحسابات. وقد وثقت منظمات حقوق الإنسان الدولية هذه الممارسات وأدانتها، ومنها تقرير «هيومن رايتس ووتش» عن الرقابة الممنهجة على المحتوى الفلسطيني في منصات ميتا. ويدفع هذا القمع الرقمي كثيراً من الناشطات والناشطين إلى رقابة ذاتية طوعية، فيعدلون خطابهم ويتجنبون قضايا بعينها خوفاً من الحظر …

author: Esperanza
title: RED ESTUDIANTIL TEMUCO: «Nos interesa generar una alianza social que sea capaz de soportar la arremetida neoriberal que estamos viviendo en este Gobierno».
content:
Tras conocer el proyecto de presupuesto de gobierno para el 2027, se registraron diversas manifestaciones para expresar el descontento social en algunas ciudades del país. Temuco fue una de ellas y en ese contexto conversamos con uno de los representantes de la Red Estudiantil Temuco.


Giordano Leonelli, estudiante Sociología Ufro y parte de la Red Estudiantil Temuco, una alianza entre la Universidad Católica de Temuco, La Universidad de La Frontera y estudiantes secundarios para activar movilizaciones en la ciudad de Temuco.


Hace algunas semanas, se vieron concentraciones y marchas que recorrieron el centro de la ciudad, convocadas por el sector estudiantil. Movilizaciones que surgen principalmente como respuesta tras conocerse los anuncios de recortes en el área de educación para el próximo año. 


«Sabemos las consecuencias que van a tener, van a ser despidos de funcionarios, peores condiciones para estudiar, peor infraestructura. Así como un debilitamiento de la educación pública, lo que nos parece bastante problemático». Giordano Leonelli, Red Estudiantil Temuco.


Como Red, ven la necesidad que el movimiento estudiantil se debe volver a rearticular, tal como en años anteriores. En esa misma línea realizaron un pliego de demandas para presentar un petitorio a nivel Temuco y sumado a ello se levantó un petitorio con alcance a nivel nacional que no solo reúne demandas sobre los recorte a la educación, sino también considera problemáticas asociadas a la salud, el medioambiente, el trabajo, la criminalización a la protesta popular, entre otros puntos.


«Nos interesa generar una alianza social que sea capaz de soportar la arremetida neoriberal que estamos viviendo en este Gobierno». Leonelli describe que trabajan por una articulación social, no partidista,que responda a los intereses de la población.


Se espera que para inicio de 2027 surjan nuevas movilizaciones con la consigna de frenar los recortes, todo en medio de un complejo escenario económico que enfrenta el país, en lo inmediato, la

Red estudiantil Temuco llama sumarse como bloque a la Jornada de Protesta Nacional convocada por profesores y sindicatos de trabajadores para el martes 24 de noviembre, en la Plaza del Hospital en Temuco, desde las 16:30 hrs.

title: Comunicado público de José Melgarejo Calbullanca, Preso Político Mapuche del caso Grollmus
content:
«COMUNICADO PÚBLICO DE JOSÉ MELGAREJO CALBULLANCA, PPM CASO GROLLMUS


Pu Machi, pu Lonko, pu Wuenen, pu Werken, pu Weichave, pu Kona.


Rekuluwaiñ ka yavuluwaiñ ni ta tuvachi weichan.


Inche José Melgarejo Calbullanca, tañi lov Lleu-lleu mapu, comunidad Nicolás Calbullanca, territorio lavkenche, Lago Lleu-lleu.


Doy a conocer mi situación como preso político mapuche, recluído en la cárcel CP Biobío, llevando ya 2 años y medio, de una condena de 7 años y medio y de otra por el llamado Caso del Molino Grollmus, por el cual fui juzgado por el Tribunal de Cañete y condenado a 86 años de prisión, juicio al que actualmente estamos apelando en la Corte Suprema, exigiendo su anulación y del cual me declaro, como lo he hecho anteriormente, inocente de los hechos que se me imputaron y por los que fuí condenado a esta altísima condena.


Por este motivo es que junto a otros ppm, hemos decidido iniciar una Huelga de Hambre de carácter indefinido, exigiendo 3 puntos principales:


Kiñe: Nulidad del juicio viciado y racista que nos condenó.

Epu: La creación de un módulo comuneros mapuche en el Cp Biobío.

Küla: Mi traslado


Por esto hago un llamado a las comunidades, territorios, organizaciones, Hogares Mapuche, Estudiantes y a los demás prisioneros políticos, a que nos apoyen en este proceso. Estaremos eternamente agradecidos de su apoyo fraterno.


También aprovecho de agradecer a todas las personas que me han apoyado, a mi como a los demás ppm, todo este tiempo.


Desde acá me siento con alto newen para seguir luchando por nuestros justos derechos como pueblo nación Mapuche.


Kiñewaiñ weichan mew.

Marichiwew


Concepción. Cárcel CP Biobío.

23 de Noviembre 2026″.

author: Kodao Productions
title: Donald Trump extorts the Philippines
content:
The latest boast of lame duck US President Donald Trump that the Philippines has agreed to source all of its energy and food imports from the US is as credible as his claim that the Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni pleaded for a photo with him, or his insistence with Russian President Vladimir Putin that the Israelis adore him as to name a plaza in his honor, forcing Putin to deliver a snarky riposte: “Donald, Israel should rename their country after you.” Trump didn’t understand the insult, which was not lost in the translation.


Perhaps as worse was the yarn that Mexico had permitted US forces to operate within its territory, which President Caludia Sheinbaum debunked, saying US troops should stick to their US bases, or the brag of years past that Mexico would pay for the thousands of kilometers of durable and impenetrable fence he was building to separate it from the US. Americans paid for the few kilometers of the overpriced fence built by Trump minions.


Trump is a media hog, like the

bangka

 in a drinking spree who conjures stories the way Rodrigo Duterte does, and the usual result is that out of the 10 stories dished out, 11 are false. Trump was battered worldwide for insulting Meloni and Italy and the Mexican people made him the butt of jokes for years for being such a *puerile, reckless and bad storyteller. First of all, he cannot be serious about anything or anybody, save perhaps for his nanny Natalie Harp, and he can hardly understand what he is punishing the media industry with.


As in the case of Fox News before, the defense was that audiences knew that Tucker Carlson was not credible, so it is their call whether to believe him or despise him. Trump is worse that Carlson since the more he talks, the deeper he burrows in his rabbit hole. The guy simply is a congenital liar. Believe him at your peril. So when this clown spewed his latest insult, that the Philippines agreed to buy all its energy and farm imports from the United States otherwise the Mutual Defense Treaty (MDT) cannot be invoked to defend the country from a possible Chinese attack, Malacanang should have taken a forceful response.


The retort to this extortion by Trump was a pablum, with the Palace saying Manila only tackled possible energy imports, noting that the Philippines doesn’t import gas from the US. As the US is saying it would export LNG, it is time for Manila to join the fun. Government is not saying that the US already exports shiploads of farm commodities to the country, from potatoes to specialty rice (with so many hundredweights—59.09 kilos each), as well as wheat, milk, meat and others. The response was **anodyne, not meant to be an underhanded compliment to a court jester and not a double-bladed

beinte nuebe

 from Batangas that could bury deeply into Trump’s carcass.


The administration should have been forthright to tell Trump that a global trading system operates in which the Philippines takes part and that the parity rights ended in 1974, when the Marcos dictatorship that Trump supported to the hilt was in its full bloom. Seventeen years later, the US military bases were kicked out of the Philippines for being precisely the bases of the country’s insecurity. Flashback to the confrontation with Malaysia over the Sabah issue and the US never sided with the Philippines despite the possibility of hostilities. The UK sided with Malaysia and the country was left in the lurch. The ironclad guarantee that US forces would come to fight for the Philippines evaporated.


As the late warmonger Henry Kissinger said being an enemy of the US is dangerous but being a friend of the US is fatal. The French knew it (the US hasn’t paid the money it owed Paris for supporting the US revolution against British colonialism), African countries understood it and Latin American nations had despised the Monroe Doctrine since 1823 and its latest reiteration, the Trump Latrine. By trying to make Trump look good with illogical statements, the Philippine government is massaging his fragile but galactic ego. This is like pulling blood out of stone or pulling hen’s teeth.


It is pretty clear, to most Filipinos anyway but not to Malacanang and the Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), that on a humdrum day at the White House, Trump would always consult his crystal ball of lies and issue statements that have nothing to do with reality, or even with the agreements and side deals that he had cut. title: Başakşehir'in stoperi Emin Bayram sakatlığı nedeniyle sezonu kapattı
content:
Süper Lig'in 12. haftasında Başakşehir'in Çorum FK'yı 4-2 yendiği maçın ardından açıklama yapan Teknik Direktör Nuri Şahin, stoper Emin Bayram'ın sakatlığı sebebiyle sezonu kapattığını duyurdu.

beIN Sports'a konuşan Şahin, "Öncelikle buruk bir sevinç yaşıyoruz. Emin'e büyük ihtimalle... Emin sezonu kapattı, onun burukluğuyla buradayız" ifadelerini kullandı.

Şahin basın toplantısında ise Emin Bayram'ın ameliyat olacağını ve 6-8 ay sahalardan uzak kalacağını söyledi.

Bu sezon Başakşehir'le 14 maçta 2 gol atan 23 yaşındaki Bayram, 18. dakikada yaşadığı sakatlığın ardından sedyeyle oyundan alınmış ve yerine Onur Ergün girmişti.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı Gelir İdaresi Başkanlığı (GİB) tarafından hazırlanan "Vergi Usul Kanunu Genel Tebliği'nde Değişiklik Yapılmasına Dair Tebliğ" Resmi Gazete'de yayımlandı.

"Bilgi Fişi" tanımını yürürlükten kaldıran düzenleme, e-Arşiv Fatura uygulamasına dahil olmayan mükelleflere yeni belge düzenleme seçenekleri sundu. Bu mükellefler, 1 Ocak 2027'den itibaren faturalarını Güvenli Mobil Ödeme ve Elektronik Belge Yönetim Sistemi, Taksi Mali Cihazlar veya izin verilen Yeni Nesil Ödeme Kaydedici Cihazlar (YN ÖKC) üzerinden e-Arşiv Fatura olarak düzenleyebilecek.

Yerli ve yabancı film gösteren sinema işletmeleri, belirlenen usul ve esaslar doğrultusunda e-Bilet uygulamasına geçerek giriş biletlerini elektronik ortamda düzenlemek zorunda olacak.

İlgili bölümün başlığı, sinema işletmelerinin e-Bilet kullanma zorunluluğunu esas alacak şekilde değiştirildi. Yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihazlardan düzenlenen e-Bilet bilgi fişi ve aylık satış raporuna ilişkin ifadeler kaldırıldı.

e-Bilette eğlence vergisine ilişkin bölümde de bilgi fişleri ve aylık satış raporlarına yönelik atıflar çıkarıldı.

Elektronik belge düzenlenmesine izin verilen yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihazların arızalanması veya çalınması, kağıt belge düzenlenebilecek durumlar arasına alındı.

Bu imkânın kullanılabilmesi için arıza veya hırsızlık durumunun ispatlanması ya da belgelendirilmesi gerekecek.

Serbest meslek faaliyeti yürüten hekimlerden, e-Serbest Meslek Makbuzu uygulamasına dahil olan ve 593 sıra numaralı tebliğ kapsamında bu makbuzu düzenleyen yeni nesil ödeme kaydedici cihaz kullananlar, cihazlarını iş yerlerinde bulundurmaları şartıyla POS cihazlarını bulundurmak ve kullanmak zorunda olmayacak.

Tebliğ 1 Ocak 2027 tarihinde yürürlüğe girecek ve hükümlerini Hazine ve Maliye Bakanı yürütecek.

author: Cody Bloomfield
title: New Indictments of Michigan Palestine Activists Are Troubling – and Flimsy
content:
Prosecutors’ use of conspiracy charges resembles the attacks on anti-ICE protesters and Stop Cop City activists.

Prosecutors’ use of conspiracy charges resembles the attacks on anti-ICE protesters and Stop Cop City activists.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In Donald Trump’s National Security Presidential Memorandum 7 (NSPM-7), the president set his sights on uprooting left-wing movements for liberation. What is obvious in the 14 months since the issuance of NSPM-7 is that the Trump administration has thus far failed: People continue to resist ICE, protest police brutality, and hold fast to criticisms of the U.S. national project.

But where the Trump administration has seen its campaign of widescale disruption falter, prosecutors have reached for increasingly attenuated theories of criminal liability to ensnare expanding cross-sections of the movement. On October 30, U.S. Attorneys unsealed a superseding indictment adding four defendants to a prosecution of pro-Palestine activists over the vandalism of University of Michigan campus officials’ homes and businesses with pro-divestment messages.

While the original defendants stand accused of holding the spray paint cans, none of the new defendants are charged with participating directly in the vandalism. Instead, they are charged with playing support roles, including media coordination and logistics planning. By sprawling the indictment into charges against activists accused of no substantive crime — merely conspiracy — federal prosecutors appear to be attempting to instill the type of fear capable of corroding a movement.

The superseding indictment is notable for what it omits: allegations that the new defendants were direct participants in the vandalism. Two defendants are accused of editing a Cryptpad document with a public statement. Federal prosecutors charged another defendant because he discussed locations to meet to plan an action. Still another activist’s alleged participation in the conspiracy is limited to operating a publicly-accessible police scanner. Charging conspiracy allows prosecutors to impose collective liability: Any of the new defendants could be found guilty of conspiracy to transmit interstate threats without ever a need to prove that they personally engaged in any criminal act. (In addition to the conspiracy to transmit interstate threats charges, one defendant also picked up a destruction of property to prevent seizure charge for allegedly removing the target of a search warrant from Signal chats.)

In the opinion of National Lawyers Guild Executive Director Xavier de Janon, the prosecution bears the hallmarks of NSPM-7, adding to the ranks of pending protest cases that include prosecutions of ICE protesters in Minnesota and Stop Cop City activists in Atlanta. In the first NSPM-7 case to secure a conviction, eight Prairieland protesters were convicted at trial of providing material support for terrorism after one protester nonfatally shot a police officer during a noise demonstration at an ICE detention center.

“U.S. Attorney Gorgon said that these alleged threats and attempts to terrorize government officials, businesses, and the Jewish Federation are anti-American. This so-called anti-American ideology is all over the NSPM-7 counterterrorism memorandum, and the topic of the prosecution — a free Palestine — matches its priorities,” said de Janon.

It marks an unusual escalation for federal prosecutors to take an interest in a local protest case. Most of the thousands of people arrested during campus protests against the genocide in Palestine faced minor charges in state court, or no charges at all. One of the defendants added to the indictment, Henry Mackeen-Shapiro, initially faced a state-level felony charge for resisting a police officer and a misdemeanor charge for trespassing. Both charges were dismissed in 2025.

De Janon raised the possibility that the federal charges are retaliatory. Two of the 12 defendants, including one of the newly added defendants, sued University of Michigan officials, alleging that the university violated their First Amendment rights by firing them following their participation in pro-Palestine protests.

“It’s very suspicious that the indictment came after the lawsuit,” said de Janon, noting that the lawsuit survived motions to dismiss.

Another possibility is the connection to Unity of Fields, formerly known as Palestine …

author: Unknown
title: Bakırhan: Silopi's future lies in clean solar energy, not coal
content:
Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), participated in a march against the thermal power plant in Silopi (Silopiya), a district of Şırnak (Şirnex), as part of the “Budget for Bread, Peace and Justice” campaign. Bakırhan said that the plant's operations were causing environmental pollution and health problems and called for its closure.


Bakırhan claimed that 4,000 people had died of cancer in Silopi since the plant began operating in 2009, adding that cases of cancer, asthma, premature births and miscarriages had increased in the region.


Bakırhan said that ash and toxic substances from the plant were contaminating the air, water and agricultural land, while authorities had failed to respond to questions about health data.


Bakırhan demanded the appointment of an independent scientific committee to assess pollution caused by the plant and examine soil, water and agricultural products. He said that the plant's operating licence should not be renewed, and its activities should be terminated.


Criticising tree cutting, mining and energy projects in the region, Bakırhan said that Mount Cudi and the surrounding natural areas must be protected. He also pointed out that young people in Silopi were being forced to migrate because of unemployment and demanded investments that would create jobs instead of a thermal power plant.


Bakırhan said, “Silopi's future does not lie in coal or thermal power plants. It lies in clean solar energy,” and adding that energy policies must prioritise public health and the environment.


Bakırhan said that the destruction of nature was incompatible with the peace process: “Destroying nature, destroying water and issuing licences that lead to people being poisoned are, in fact, another form of war. This must come to an end. Hopefully, Mount Cudi, which protected Noah's Ark from the flood, will once again protect its own people. And its people will protect Cudi, the Hezil River, their rivers, water and plains. We hope that one day we will free our lands from these thermal power plants, geothermal power plants (GPPs), hydroelectric power plants (HPPs), solar power plants (SPPs), and the profit-driven mentality that grants licences over streams and rivers, poisoning our land.”

author: Unknown
title: Dozens of skulls and bones discovered in a three-level cave in Silvan
content:
Numerous human skulls and bones have been discovered in a remote cave in the Silvan district of the Kurdish province of Amed (Diyarbakır). During an investigation, representatives of human rights organizations came across remains in the multi-level cave that may belong to several dozen people. Some of the skulls show damage that could indicate gunshot wounds. The identities of the deceased, the causes of their deaths, and when they died remain unknown.


The cave is located between the villages of Boşat and Çîçika in a forested mountainous area and is known locally as the “Ecnebi Cave.” After the Human Rights Association (IHD) received a report about the discovery of bones, its Amed branch, the Amed Bar Association, and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD) formed a joint delegation. The Mezopotamya News Agency (MA) accompanied the investigation on November 19 and documented the findings at the site.


Hundreds of bones in a multi-level cave system


The entrance to the cave is located on a forested mountaintop, approximately 45 to 50 minutes on foot from the village of Çîçika. It is so narrow that only one person at a time can descend into it using a rope. The cave consists of at least three levels and is estimated to extend 50 meters underground. In the upper section, the team discovered several skulls and bones among the rubble. On the level below, which was completely dark, they encountered a far greater concentration of remains.


According to MA, approximately 15 to 20 skulls and hundreds of other bones were scattered across different locations on this level. Some of the unusually small skulls may belong to children. Several skulls had openings that may have been caused by gunfire, while others were fractured or severely damaged. Numerous remains were also found beneath rocks and in natural crevices.


On the second level, the reporting team also documented blackened stones and bones bearing what appeared to be burn marks. It has not yet been possible to determine whether these were caused by fire or an explosion. According to the journalists, one striking detail was that no clothing was found in any of the areas examined.


A member of the delegation also managed to reach the particularly narrow third level, where further bones were found. It remains unclear whether additional sections of the cave lie beneath this level.


“It was as though we were in a cave of death”


Fırat Akdeniz, a member of the IHD’s Commission on the Disappeared in Amed, was among those who descended into the cave. He described his impressions to MA: “The entrance to the cave is dangerous. We managed to descend only with great difficulty. On the second level, we found even more human bones. It was darker, and the smell was very strong. We saw far more human remains there than we had expected.”


According to Akdeniz, some of the bones may still be buried underground. The delegation was unable to determine either the number of deceased or their identities. “It was a painful and tragic sight. From the first level to the third, it was as though we were in a cave of death. It appeared as if people had been deliberately brought here, from conflict zones or civilian areas, and executed. We could not establish the exact number.”


Whether the cave was actually used as an execution site has yet to be established. A forensic examination of the remains is still pending.


Memories of the crimes of the 1990s


The discovery takes on particular significance against the backdrop of numerous extrajudicial executions and cases of enforced disappearance committed in Silvan and other parts of Kurdistan, particularly during the 1990s. Among those linked to these crimes are JITEM, a clandestine state intelligence and gendarmerie organization, and the Kurdish-Turkish Hezbollah, known as “Hizbulkontra,” which operated as a counterinsurgency force against the Kurdish freedom movement.


Whether the newly discovered remains date back to this period remains unclear. Following their investigation, members of the human rights delegation suggested that the bones might date from a relatively more recent period.


Akdeniz also referred to the Turkish military sieges and curfews imposed on Kurdish cities in 2015 and 2016. Reports of serious human rights violations repeatedly emerged from the areas sealed off at the time. “Our concern is that we will be confronted with more such disturbing findings,” the human rights activist said.

author: Unknown
title: Women from Eastern Kurdistan demand legal equality
content:
In a statement issued on the occasion of November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, the Peace Mothers in Eastern Kurdistan drew attention to the human rights violations faced by women around the world.


Emphasizing women’s rights to freedom, independence, and decision-making, the statement said that crimes and murders committed against women in Iran stem from discriminatory laws, patriarchal attitudes, and the indifference of the authorities.


It noted that, decades after the murder of the Mirabal sisters, gender-based violence continues and perpetrators of crimes committed in the name of “honor” continue to escape punishment.


The statement pointed out that fathers, brothers, and husbands are involved in acts of violence against women, including cases of self-immolation and armed attacks, and identified legal inequality and patriarchal relations as the underlying causes of persistent systemic discrimination.


Criticizing the laws of the Islamic Republic of Iran, the statement pointed out that legal restrictions imposed on women in matters such as family life, marriage, divorce, child custody, and personal independence are among the primary factors perpetuating violence against women.


The statement further highlighted the lack of safe living spaces for women, specialized support centers, independent legal and psychological services, and economic opportunities.


Stressing the need to end femicide, the statement emphasized that the government’s responsibility does not begin only after crimes have been committed and that the necessary preventive measures must be taken.

author: Unknown
title: Guerrillas: Kurdish people recognized their existence with the founding of the PKK
content:
Through 48 years of resistance, the PKK (Kurdistan Workers’ Party) has made significant gains and brought the Kurdish people onto the stage of history. It has brought the Kurdish people’s right to freedom to international attention. Heavy sacrifices have been made in this struggle, and many people regarded as heroes have given their lives. Each of them has become part of the Kurdish people’s legacy of a life in freedom. Thousands of young people headed for the mountains of Kurdistan to embrace the cause and waged a determined struggle despite immense difficulties.


Today, the struggle of the Apoist Movement under the leadership of Abdullah Öcalan has achieved success. On the occasion of the 48th anniversary of the PKK’s founding on November 27, 1978, guerrillas from the HPG (People’s Defense Forces) and YJA Star (Free Women’s Troops) shared their views with ANF.


Bahar Goyî: Millions of people embraced the PKK movement


YJA Star guerrilla Bahar Goyî began by celebrating November 27, saying: “This day is very important to us. When our movement was founded, Kurds, Turks, and Arabs were part of it, and many other peoples also lent their support. The struggle of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] had an impact on all peoples. Comrade Haki Karer is an example of this. He was Leader Apo’s hidden spirit. To honor the memory of Comrade Haki, Leader Apo founded the PKK in the village of Fîs in Amed (tr: Diyarbakır) in 1978. After its founding, the PKK spread throughout Kurdistan and across the world. Millions of people embraced the movement, and thousands of young people headed for the mountains of Kurdistan. Thousands of heroic young people who spearheaded the struggle for freedom embraced martyrdom with great courage. Today, our people are turning out in large numbers to honor the comrades whose martyrdom has recently been announced and to keep their legacy alive. This is deeply meaningful and valuable to us.”


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/54921811_20261119103421_2026-11-21-behdinan-bahar-goyi-gerilaya-yja-star-bi-avabuna-pkk-hebuna-xwe-naskir-1.mp4


The YJA Star guerrilla continued: “Honoring our martyrs means standing by Leader Apo. We are truly happy when we see our people honoring their martyrs. This is a sacred stance. It also demonstrates how deeply committed we are to our Leader. At present, our primary concern is securing Leader Apo’s physical freedom. To achieve this, we must take our martyrs as our example. If we follow in their footsteps, we will make significant gains. When we achieve a free and shared life, we will dedicate it to our people and our Leader. Whether the process moves forward or not, we will continue to stand by our Leader and our martyrs. On this basis, we will carry on our struggle with great enthusiasm.”


Dilgeş Farqîn: The attacks and oppression brought us closer to the PKK movement


HPG guerrilla Dilgeş Farqîn stated that enemy forces had established control over Kurdistan and the Kurdish people had been subjected to genocidal attacks before the founding of the PKK.


Dilgeş Farqîn said: “The occupying forces were attacking the Kurdish people with extreme brutality. Tens of thousands of Kurds were killed in these attacks. All the social and cultural values of the Kurdish people were being destroyed. At that time, many established Kurdish organizations approached the Kurdish people’s cause with fear. However, with the emergence of Leader Apo, the darkness imposed on the Kurdish people was overcome. Leader Apo recognized the need to establish a Kurdish movement. For this reason, he founded the PKK movement in 1978. I consider myself very fortunate to have come to know this movement."


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/d524cddc_20261119154002_2026-11-21-behdinan-dilges-farqin-gerilaye-hpg-bi-avabuna-pkk-hebuna-xwe-naskir-1.mp4


The HPG guerrilla continued: "The attacks and oppression brought us closer to the PKK movement. The acts of heroism we witnessed before our eyes had a profound impact on both me and the society in which I lived. This influence led me to join the PKK Movement. Today, I am proud to be part of such a movement. At its core, the PKK is a movement of revenge. Following the martyrdom of Comrade Haki, the PKK continued its struggle in a spirit of revenge. Leader Apo inspired many heroes who went on to write epic chapters in the PKK’s history. As Leader Apo himself has said, the PKK has fulfilled its historical role. author: Unknown
title: Remains of PKK guerrilla Celal Gök returned to his family after nine years
content:
PKK member Celal Gök (Nom de Guerre: Rüstem Serhed) lost his life in a clash in Dersim in 2017. His body was buried at the time in the Seyrantepe Cemetery for the Nameless in the Tuşba district of Van.


His family, who had traveled to Van and provided DNA samples shortly after receiving news of his death, were informed that a DNA match had been confirmed nine years later.


Following the notification, the family traveled to Van and received their son’s remains together with representatives of the Van branch of MEBYA-DER (Association for Solidarity and Assistance with Families Who Have Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations).


The remains were received with chants of “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal). In a brief speech at the gathering, Gök’s elder brother, Güven Gök, extended his condolences to PKK founder Abdullah Öcalan and the people of Kurdistan.


Celal Gök’s remains were then taken to his home village of Rüstem Gedik (Kopa), in the Korkut district of Muş, for burial.

author: Unknown
title: Doctor tells prisoner with cancer: “Go back to prison and wait to die”
content:
Evin Zapsu, a prisoner diagnosed with stage-four cancer, was reportedly subjected to inhumane treatment by a doctor during a medical examination at Kayseri City Hospital. According to her family, the doctor told her: “Your cancer has spread throughout your body. Go back to prison and wait to die.”


Zapsu is being held at Kayseri-Bünyan Closed Women’s Prison. She was diagnosed with stage-four cancer on November 16. Four days later, on November 20, she was taken to the gynecologic oncology department of Kayseri City Hospital for treatment. A medical report was issued there stating that she was no longer fit to remain in prison.


During her weekly phone call with her family, Zapsu recounted the treating doctor’s remarks. Her husband, Mecit Zapsu, reacted with outrage. He said that a doctor’s duty, particularly when treating a seriously ill patient, was to stand by and support her rather than confront her with such statements. “We do not accept such an attitude,” he said. The family announced that they would file a criminal complaint against the doctor over the incident.


Evin Zapsu was imprisoned in December 2016 amid a political crackdown on the Peoples’ Democratic Party (HDP) in the southern city of Mersin. She was sentenced to 15 years in prison on charges of “membership in a terrorist organization.” The mother of three was initially held at Bakırköy Women’s Prison in Istanbul before being transferred to Kayseri.

author: Unknown
title: Koçyiğit: Prison administrations act as though there is no peace process
content:
Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), criticized the ongoing rights violations in Turkish prisons. At a press conference in parliament in Ankara, she accused the relevant authorities of ignoring developments in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. “Prison administrations are operating entirely independently of this process. It is as though there has been no Peace and Democratic Society Process in this country for the past two years,” Koçyiğit said.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/20f92c94_20261123140019_2026-11-23-ankara-gulistan-kilic-kocgun-cezaevi-idareleri-surecten-bagimsiz-yuryor_1.mp4


Seriously ill prisoners denied adequate treatment


The DEM Party politician drew attention to the cases of Evin Zapsu, Newroz Bozkurt, Devrim Ayık, Fatma Toprak, and Emrah Nebioğlu, whose health conditions are a cause for serious concern. She said that these prisoners continued to face difficulties obtaining adequate medical treatment despite suffering from severe illnesses. Zapsu, who is being held at Kayseri-Bünyan Women’s Prison, was diagnosed with stage-four cancer on November 16. On November 20, a hospital determined that she was unfit to remain in prison.


Koçyiğit also criticized practices such as conducting medical examinations while prisoners are in handcuffs and carrying out searches of their mouths. She noted that the Ministry of Justice and the General Directorate of Prisons and Detention Houses have left inquiries concerning these rights violations unanswered. Referring to Tuncay Sağlam, who recently died in custody, Koçyiğit recalled the state’s obligation to protect the right to life. “Families of seriously ill prisoners are now protesting outside the Ministry of Justice and demanding concrete measures,” the politician said.


Call for implementation of the peace law


Regarding the next political steps, Koçyiğit stated that the DEM Party expected the parliamentary monitoring committee to be established and begin its work soon. At the upcoming meeting of the National Security Council, she said, a decision must be made to officially verify and acknowledge the steps taken by the Kurdish side in the peace process. “We reiterate our expectation that this decision will also pave the way for the implementation of the law adopted on August 10 with overwhelming support. It must be brought into force swiftly, without further delay. The verification and confirmation phase must also be completed promptly.”


Allow journalists to visit Imrali


Responding to questions about possible visits by journalists to Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan on the prison island of Imrali, Koçyiğit stated that no names had yet been finalized. “We expect media professionals to be able to travel to the island as soon as possible. At the same time, the Committee for Peace and Political Participation must be announced without delay. Conditions must be established that allow journalists and other individuals to visit the island. However, no specific names have been determined so far. At least, we have received no information to that effect.”

author: Unknown
title: International conference in Belfast: Ending armed conflict does not constitute peace
content:
An international conference titled “Combating Impunity, Memorialisation, and Transitional Justice Under Threat” has begun in Belfast, the capital of Northern Ireland, bringing together human rights defenders, legal professionals, academics, and representatives of international institutions from around the world.


The two-day conference, held at Riddel Hall at Queen’s University Belfast, is jointly organized by the Northern Ireland-based Committee on the Administration of Justice (CAJ), the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), and Queen’s University Belfast.


The conference addresses conflict and peace processes in various regions, particularly Northern Ireland, South Africa, Argentina, Colombia, Brazil, Ukraine, the Basque Country, and Kurdistan, as well as human rights violations committed by states in the past, policies of impunity, the pursuit of truth, and the preservation of collective memory.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/b2e7a3da_20261123162236_2026-11-23-belfast-baris-ve-adalet-konferansi-catismazlik-tek-basina-baris-degil-1.mp4


UN Special Rapporteur and international human rights defenders also in attendance


The event opened with a speech by Professor Matthew Moran, Director of the Institute for Peace, Security and Justice at Queen’s University Belfast, followed by a presentation on the conference’s objectives by Daniel Holder, Director of the Committee on the Administration of Justice (CAJ) and Vice-President of FIDH. Among the prominent participants is Bernard Duhaime, the United Nations (UN) Special Rapporteur on the promotion of truth, justice, reparation and guarantees of non-recurrence.


Other participants include María José Guembe, President of CELS, from Argentina; Luís Guillermo Pérez Casas, former Secretary-General of FIDH, from Colombia; South African human rights lawyer Kayan Leung; former UN Special Rapporteur Professor Fionnuala Ní Aoláin; Professor Kieran McEvoy, an expert on peace and transitional justice; Chief Constable of the Police Service of Northern Ireland Jon Boutcher; and Kurdish lawyer Reyhan Yalçındağ Baydemir, former Vice-President of the International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH).


The conference, which also brings together representatives of the UK government, addressed the threats to human rights gains posed by the rise of far-right and populist movements, impunity for state crimes, efforts to establish the fate of missing persons, and the pursuit of justice in post-conflict societies.


Human rights violations in Kurdistan and the peace process discussed


Speaking at the session titled “Transitional Justice Processes Under Threat,” moderated by Dr. Brian Dooley, Reyhan Yalçındağ discussed the peace process in Turkey and the historical background of the Kurdish question. Emphasizing that ending armed conflict does not, in itself, constitute peace, Yalçındağ stated that lasting peace could only be achieved by constitutionally guaranteeing fundamental rights and freedoms and confronting serious crimes committed in the past.


Drawing attention to human rights violations committed in Kurdistan during the 1990s, including enforced disappearances, torture, extrajudicial executions, and the burning of villages, Yalçındağ stressed the need to establish mechanisms for truth and justice. She stated that the failure to investigate past crimes perpetuates impunity, adding: “Confronting the past is not an obstacle to peace; on the contrary, it is a fundamental prerequisite for peace.”


‘Peace must be advanced through concrete steps toward democratization’


Reyhan Yalçındağ noted that the steps taken in the peace process were important but insufficient, emphasizing the need to enshrine the fundamental rights of Kurds in the constitution and remove obstacles to participation in democratic politics. Criticizing the continued operations against journalists, the imprisonment of seriously ill prisoners, and the appointment of state trustees to replace elected mayors, Yalçındağ stated that peace must not be limited to political declarations but must be advanced through concrete steps toward democratization.


Drawing attention to the role of women in the peace process, Yalçındağ stated that the Kurdish women’s movement should not merely support the process but should be a direct participant and a driving force in shaping it.
