author: taz
title: Jetzt noch schnell räumen lassen
content:
Alt­mie­te­r*in­nen der Rigaer94 haben schon länger den Widerstand gegen Räumungspläne aufgegeben. Rückt Mitte Dezember der Gerichtsvollzieher an?


„Rigaer94 verteidigen“, diese Parole findet sich seit Jahren auf vielen Plakaten und Transparenten. Doch zuletzt war es um das linke Hausprojekt im Friedrichshainer Nordkiez ruhiger geworden. Das könnte sich in den nächsten Wochen wieder ändern.


Für den 15. Dezember hat sich der Gerichtsvollzieher angekündigt. Er will mehrere Wohnungen im Seitenflügel und Hinterhaus der Rigaer Straße 94 räumen lassen. Die Bewohner*innen, von denen niemand mit Namen in der Zeitung stehen will, hatten damit gerechnet, waren aber trotzdem über den Zeitpunkt der Räumungsankündigung überrascht. Die Wohnungen waren nicht besetzt: Es gab Mietverträge, die noch in den 1990er Jahren abgeschlossen worden waren. Doch die Alt­mie­te­r*in­nen wohnen längst nicht mehr im Haus. Mehrere von ihnen hatten sich schon im Sommer 2024 mit dem Hauseigentümer verständigt, sich nicht weiter gegen Räumungsklagen wehren zu wollen. Dafür gab es unterschiedliche Gründe: Manche von ihnen wollten nicht mehr die juristischen Probleme tragen, zudem gab es politische Differenzen mit den aktuellen Be­woh­ne­r*in­nen der Rigaer 94.


Die Eigentümergesellschaft Lafone Investments hatte ab 2021 schrittweise fast allen bekannten Mie­te­r*in­nen gekündigt und zahlreiche Räumungsklagen wegen unerlaubter Untervermietung oder fehlender Vertragsgrundlage eingereicht. Doch die britische Briefkastenfirma mit Sitz in London ist seit dem EU-Austritt Großbritanniens nicht mehr rechts- und prozessfähig, wie das Berliner Landgericht in den letzten zwei Jahren gleich mehrfach entschieden hat.


Ein Geschenk für die Eigentümerin


Daher war die Ankündigung der Altmieter*innen, gegen die Räumungsklagen nicht mehr juristisch vorgehen, für die Eigentümerin ein Geschenk. Denn jetzt kann sie ohne weitere Klagen räumen lassen. Dass sie fast zwei Jahre verstreichen ließ und nun Mitte Dezember die Räumungen durchsetzen will, erklären sich Be­ob­ach­te­r*in­nen auch damit, dass sie Fakten schaffen will, bevor ein von der Linkspartei geführter Senat regiert.


Ob der Räumungstermin zu halten ist, bleibt offen. Die aktuellen Be­woh­ne­r*in­nen wollen sich informieren, ob es juristische Mittel dagegen gibt. Schließlich war bekannt, dass die Wohnungen auch nach Kündigung der Mietverträge weiterhin bewohnt waren. Somit stellt sich die Frage, ob gegen die Be­woh­ne­r*in­nen eigenständige Räumungsklagen eingereicht werden müssen. Das würde Zeit in Anspruch nehmen, der Räumungstermin im Winter wäre erst einmal vom Tisch.


Sollte es beim angekündigten Termin bleiben, haben die Be­woh­ne­r*in­nen schon angekündigt, die Räume nicht freiwillig aufzugeben. Unterstützung haben sie auch in der Nachbarschaft. Für nicht wenige gilt die Rigaer Straße 94 als Gentrifizierungsbremse, die verhindert, dass im Nordkiez von Friedrichshain die Mieten weiter steigen.

author: Susan Kang
title: Young Leftists and K-Pop Stans Won Brazil for Lula — Now They’re Staying Engaged
content:
In Brazil’s election, Lula didn’t organize the youth. The youth organized Lula.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

There has been much ink spilled since October about the role of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s informal social media supporters, called “Lula’s Army,” in mobilizing for his victory in the second round of presidential votes. Following the first-round victory of Lula’s right-wing rival, Flavio Bolsonaro, on October 4, 2026, some political commentators declared Lula a lame duck, comparing him to President Joe Biden. But Lula defied expectations, pulling off a stunning and historic second-round victory, in a higher-turnout second-round vote that consolidated support for the now fourth-term incumbent.

Multiple media sources have credited Lula’s comeback to André Janones, the “general” of Lula’s Army, the WhatsApp community of more than 10 million that successfully used social media to share and boost support for the left-wing leader. Some commentators have considered how the digital army model could be replicated (with efforts beginning in Argentina, Venezuela, Colombia, and EU countries) in upcoming elections. But less attention in English-language media has been paid to the role of regular grassroots organizers in Brazil, many of whom were engaging in politics for the first time, and how they might continue to engage in their newly activated mobilization infrastructure.

Young Brazilian grassroots organizers, many of them first-time political activists not affiliated with any political party, were more than just loyal soldiers in the WhatsApp-driven campaign for Lula. They did not wait for official directives but instead began mass mobilizations on October 5 in Rio and other cities. Organizers began to mobilize support in their networks: students, K-pop and pop music fandoms, artists, and a generation of young leftists took to the streets and to group chats. When Lula marched down São Paulo’s Avenida Paulista on October 11, 2026, with an estimated 1 million supporters, he benefited from the self-organization of his newly activated support base. This event, called the March for Democracy, was organized by student groups, LGBTQ groups, and fan networks. The event was compared to the 1983 Diretas Já — the mass mobilization that demanded an end to the military dictatorship.

Notably, the grassroots mobilizing moved away from the official campaign’s core legacy message. Rather than provide voters a clear sense of what a fourth term Lula presidency might bring, Lula’s official campaign during the first round relied heavily on his laurels and the accomplishments of his three previous terms, such as the successful Bolsa Família, a direct cash transfer program that lifted millions of families out of poverty. During the election’s first round, Lula did not have a strong social media presence aside from some highly produced official videos, and famously did not have a cell phone. The official campaign did not promote social media posts or many mass public events, and Lula at times drew criticism for talking too much about artificial intelligence and defending Brazil’s rare minerals from Trump’s colonial designs, rather than centering people’s everyday concerns. Furthermore, any criticisms of the official campaign were reportedly not well received.

Recognizing the threat to democracy, independent youth organizers mobilized support for Lula in all kinds of places: at kitchen tables, on family group chats, and on neighbors’ doorsteps. Maria Clara de Oliveira, a 25-year-old photographer in São Paulo, told Truthout, “I flipped a lot of votes, mostly women’s.”

Her biggest success was changing the minds of her girlfriend’s aunts: older evangelical women with conservative views who had skipped the first round altogether. “Talking to those aunts made a big difference,” she said. With voters like them, “what worked was being frank, talking, and understanding that person’s reality.” She borrowed a line that circulated widely among organizers in those weeks: “Fight with all your strength, but never lose your tenderness.”

Others worked their own networks, one contact at a time. Lorrana Freitas, 27, had never organized anything before. She waited three days to get into Janones’s channel, then followed its instructions: hashtags to push up on X, far right content to ignore. She also brought her …

title: İHD, tutuklanan ÇHD'li avukatlar için serbest bırakma çağrısı yaptı
content:
İnsan Hakları Derneği (İHD), İzmir merkezli yürütülen bir soruşturma kapsamında 17 Kasım 2026 tarihinde ev baskınlarıyla gözaltına alınan ve 19 Kasım’da tutuklanan Çağdaş Hukukçular Derneği (ÇHD) üyesi dört avukata ilişkin yazılı bir açıklama yayımladı.


İzmir'de gözaltına alınan 4 avukat tutuklandı


20 Kasım 2026


Açıklamada, dört avukatın derhal serbest bırakılması ve savunmaya yönelik baskıların sona erdirilmesi istendi.


SAVUNMA MAKAMINA YÖNELİK BASKILARA SON VERİLSİN, TUTUKLU AVUKATLAR DERHAL SERBEST BIRAKILSIN! İzmir merkezli soruşturma kapsamında 17 Kasım 2026 tarihinde ev baskınlarıyla gözaltına alınan Çağdaş Hukukçular Derneği üyesi Av. Veysi Çetin, Av. Yemen Cankan, Av. Erdoğan Akdoğdu ve Av. Bahattin Özdemir, 19 Kasım’da tutuklanmıştır. Aralarında derneğimiz üyelerinin de bulunduğu avukatların 24 saati aşkın süre müdafileriyle görüştürülmemesi ve mesleki faaliyetlerinde kullandıkları dijital materyallere el konulması, savunma hakkı ve avukatlık mesleğinin bağımsızlığı açısından ağır hukuki ihlal oluşturmaktadır. Ceza hukukunun temel ilkesi, kişilerin kimlikleri, düşünceleri veya mesleki faaliyetleri üzerinden değil, somut fiilleri ve hukuka uygun deliller temelinde yargılanmasıdır. Günther Jakobs’un kavramsallaştırdığı düşman ceza hukuku anlayışı, bireyin işlediği fiilden ziyade devlet tarafından tehlikeli olarak tanımlanmasını esas alarak hukuki güvencelerin daraltılmasını ifade eder. Avukatların mesleki faaliyetlerinin kriminalize edilmesi, bu anlayışın savunma makamına yönelmesi tehlikesini ortaya koymaktadır. Savunma faaliyetlerinin suçla ilişkilendirilmesi, ceza muhakemesini adaletin gerçekleştirilmesi amacından uzaklaştırarak bir baskı mekanizmasına dönüştürür. İnsan Hakları Derneği olarak, yargı makamlarını Anayasa’nın 19. maddesi ve tutuklamanın istisnailiği ilkesi doğrultusunda dört avukatın derhal serbest bırakılmasını sağlamaya çağırıyoruz. Savunma makamının bağımsızlığını hedef alan her türlü müdahalenin karşısında duracağımızı, Çağdaş Hukukçular Derneği ile tutuklanan avukatlarla ve savunma hakkını koruyan bütün hukukçularla dayanışma içinde olacağımızı kamuoyuna duyuruyoruz. Adalet, yalnızca bugün hakları ihlal edilenlerin değil, herkesin bir gün ihtiyaç duyacağı evrensel bir güvencedir. https://t.co/HDOfHtVibs


— İHD Genel Merkezi (@ihdgenelmerkez)

November 21, 2026


Çalışma materyallerine el konuldu


Açıklamada, avukatların mesleki çalışmalarında kullandıkları dijital materyallere de el konulduğu belirtildi. İHD, bu durumun avukatlık mesleğinin bağımsızlığını zedelediğini belirtti.


İHD, avukatların mesleki faaliyetlerinin suç konusu yapılmasının savunma makamını hedef alan bir baskı anlayışını gösterdiğini söyledi.


Serbest bırakma çağrısı


İHD, tutuklanan avukatlar Veysi Çetin, Yemen Cankan, Erdoğan Akdoğdu ve Bahattin Özdemir'in derhal serbest bırakılmasını istedi. Dernek, bu talebini Anayasa'nın 19. maddesindeki kişi özgürlüğü güvencesine ve tutuklamanın istisnai bir tedbir olduğu ilkesine dayandırdı. Ayrıca Çağdaş Hukukçular Derneği (ÇHD) ve tutuklu avukatlarla dayanışma içinde olacaklarını açıkladı.


Ne olmuştu?


17 Kasım'da İzmir merkezli soruşturma kapsamında ev baskınlarıyla gözaltına alınan avukatlar, 19 Kasım'da tutuklandı. Dört avukat da ÇHD üyesi. İHD, açıklamasında avukatların serbest bırakılmasını istedi.

author: Unknown
title: “I will always have more in common with oppressed group A than with oppressed group B because of…
content:
“I will always have more in common with oppressed group A than with oppressed group B because of these shared oppressed experiences”

… I don’t care?

I thought we were doing solidarity here, not sectarianism?

Like, I know this sentence is used a lot when people are grouped together according to AGAB or some frustratingly pointless shit like that, but we can just challenge the AGAB-grouping thing without making new teams of who is and isn’t in our community.

Like, it’s fine to want to spend time with only people who experience roughly the same oppressive structures as you, but to take that as a guiding principle for your activism is a path to isolated irrelevance.

I don’t need to have any shit in common with my comrades other than ‘let’s smash oppressive structures and build a better world’.

author: Kristopher Drummond
title: Therapy as Rite of Passage Pt. 2: Cultivating Secure Attachment to the Earth
content:
Photo courtesy of the author.


Therapy, in its crazy way, by emphasizing the inner soul and

ignoring the outer soul, supports the decline of the actual world

. Yet therapy goes on blindly believing that it’s curing the outer world by making better people. We’ve had that for years and years: “If everybody went into therapy, we’d have better buildings, we’d have better people, we’d have more consciousness.”

It’s not the case

.


—James Hillman


W

e know—

we know—

that the future our imaginations were promised is not the future that awaits us. This summer, more than any previous, is our evidence. As I write, fires rage across the American west, bombs drop on children, surveillance architecture is daily being constructed outside rural convenience stores. In our hearts, if we look, the knowing of where we really are is clear.


For many in the West, the future has long been a source of secure attachment. It has been our god, a shining destination justifying the sacrifices of generations. All the brutality of history has supposedly made sense through the lens of progress.

We’re going somewhere amazing.

Utopia has been just around the corner with every technological advance, asking for just a bit more patience, a bit more sacrifice, a bit more relinquishment of our humanity—just enough so that when the robots take our jobs, the foretold dawning of endless leisure will arrive as prophecy fulfilled.


For many, this enculturated fantasy of the future has been the bedrock of busy lives, unconsciously justifying cycles of overwork, burnout, and addiction. For a brief window in time, for some, it seemed true that children could build better lives than their parents and that technological advances did indeed improve the quality of life for a majority of the populace. However, here at the logical conclusion of an infinite growth paradigm, driven by technological development that has greatly outpaced our moral or spiritual development, we are left to contend with the starkness of reality.


Anytime you’re gonna grow, you’re gonna lose something. You’re losing what you’re hanging onto to keep safe. You’re losing habits that you’re comfortable with, you’re losing familiarity. That’s a big one, when you begin to move into the unfamiliar. You know, in the organic world when anything begins to grow it’s moving constantly into unfamiliar movements and unfamiliar things.


—James Hillman


As I discussed in

part one of this essay

, we are at a collective threshold that in another cultural context would imply the need for a “rite of passage.” As Peter Kingsley describes in his book

Catafalque: Carl Jung and the End of Humanity,

the mythic energy fueling our collective stories has withdrawn—our society is like a ship at sea, moving forward without propulsion, carried only by its remaining inertia. Soon, the density of the water will have its way.


Rites of passage are about growing up. They are designed to activate our latent soul capacities, allowing us to rise to moments of change and loss, ultimately pointing back to the fundamental uncertainty of existence. These ceremonies intentionally confront us with the facts of life—birth, transformation, and death—with the aim of engendering our surrender to a larger order. True adulthood is marked by the capacity to live in ever deepening levels of complexity, holding nuance, paradox and change with open hands, neither resisting nor clinging to easy answers.


As eco-depth psychologist Bill Plotkin has expressed through his eco-centric developmental model (presented in his book

Nature and the Human Soul

), mainstream western culture is an expression of arrested development at the adolescent level. Look around—the values of ego strength, material accumulation, competition, hubristic certainty, and tribalistic social organization dominate the discourse. It’s all about speed, growth, victory, dominance, knowledge, vitality. The developmental values of healthy adulthood—humility, community, cooperation, surrender, service, death literacy and wisdom—have not yet been embodied on a collective level. As a result, we cling to a future that only exists in the illusory linearity of our underdeveloped psyches. As the promised future and our capacity to attach to it falls away, we face the daunting task of discovering what remains, and where our security actually comes from.

author: Brian Hioe
title: KMT Passes Cash Handouts, Leans into Attacks on Solar Energy Before Elections
content:
THE KMT PASSED a 20,000 NT cash handout to the general public yesterday in the legislature, shortly before elections. This would continue a familiar tactic of the party–to distribute cash handouts to the public in order to affect election outcomes. The TPP, unusually, broke from the KMT when it came to the cash handout at the last minute, but because insufficient DPP legislators were present in the legislature, it still passed.

Indeed, this has proven to be a useful electoral tactic in the past. While President Lai Ching-te called for opposition to the cash hand-outs, one notes that on other occasions the DPP first resisted cash hand-outs and then pivoted toward trying to take credit for the move after seeing that it was popular with the public. At other times, it has been the DPP itself that sought to move for cash hand-outs with the claim that this was distributing the dividends of Taiwan’s AI windfall to the public.

At the same time, one notes that, both last year and this year, the KMT pushed a drastic, far-reaching set of cuts to the government budget. This includes not only the defense budget but social services. While the KMT has claimed that such budgets were necessary for fiscal balance, the cuts it currently calls for would be at the expense of social services.

The KMT has historically leaned into vote buying to win elections, and this is perhaps no different. One notes that practices regarding vote buying continue, especially in rural areas of Taiwan, with young progressive candidates reporting that voters were paid 6,000 NT to vote for anyone but them.

In the meantime, the KMT is also leaning into what has increasingly been a recurrent theme for the party in past years–attacks on solar energy and an attempt to frame it as dangerous. Even as much of the world has sought to boost development in the renewable sector in order to offset the impact of climate change, the KMT has increasingly alleged that solar power is new, untested, and dangerous. By contrast, nuclear power is the only clean and safe alternative, and the DPP only advances solar energy projects because of corruption.

In the past, one has observed the circulation of AI-generated disinformation online claiming that solar panels are radioactive and showing birds seeming to die after drinking water near solar panels damaged by a typhoon–never mind that the species of bird depicted in the video does not exist in Taiwan.

As such, issues regarding solar panels have become contentious in several local races. In Tainan, KMT candidate Hsieh Lung-chieh has hit out at floating photovoltaic solar farms in the Wushantou Reservoir to suggest that chemicals used to clean the panels will be dangerous for the water supply.

Members of the Chiang mayoral administration have also hit out at suggestions to install solar panels on historic buildings such as the National Palace Museum, leading to an unusual spat between the Chiang mayoral administration and the National Palace Museum after Taipei Cultural Affairs division director Tsai Shih-ping published AI-generated images of solar panels being installed on the museum. The museum has since demanded a policy. Such controversies have also led Chiang to be criticized for not knowing his own mayoral administration’s policies, in that it was policies under his mayorship that have led solar panels to be installed on historic buildings such as the Longshan Temple in Wanhua.

Indeed, the KMT’s advocacy for nuclear energy was never rooted in science, but in historic nostalgia for a period in which the KMT was the sole ruling party of Taiwan, the economy was booming, and Taiwan was much more dependent on nuclear energy in its energy mix. The KMT, then, would be suggesting that the restoration of nuclear energy could bring back this period of greater order and economic prosperity. By contrast, any newer form of energy must be framed as potentially a threat to traditionalist reliance on nuclear energy. But it may be a sign of how the KMT has sought to mobilize its voters along traditional party issues to see this recent wave of attacks on the DPP over solar power.

title: Vigil for ill prisoners: The right to life is not negotiable
content:
The protest, launched outside the Ministry of Justice following a call by the Federation of Associations for Legal Solidarity with the Families of Prisoners and Convicts (TUHAD-FED), the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) and the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), will enter its fifth day. 


The indefinite protest will continue every day at 14:00 outside the Ministry of Justice.


On Friday, the relatives of ill prisoners Ömer Güneri, Yakup Akman, Mehmet Ali Taşkın and Selim Çiftçi, Tuncer Sağlam, who died on 7 November in the hospital where he was receiving treatment, attended the protest.


During the demonstration, which was supported by representatives of organisations and members of the public, a banner bearing the names of seriously ill prisoners was unfurled. It read: “We are at the gates of justice; we will open the prison gates through resistance. Freedom for ill prisoners.”


‘Don't stay silent’


Deniz Topkan, a member of the Central Executive Board of the Health and Social Service Workers' Union (SES), called for support for the protest, saying that the vigil outside the Ministry of Justice must not be ignored.


Pointing out that numerous ill prisoners had lost their lives in prison after being denied access to healthcare, Topkan stressed that restricting someone's freedom does not mean their right to health and life can be taken away.


Stating that prisons had become places where illnesses deteriorate and deaths occur, Topkan said that isolation practices in Type S and other high-security prisons negatively affect prisoners' mental health.


Deniz Topkan noted that practices such as delays in hospital transfers, examinations conducted while prisoners are handcuffed, strip searches and intrusive oral cavity searches obstruct prisoners' right to treatment. She called for the release of seriously ill prisoners and guaranteed access to medical care to prevent further deaths.


Ercan Sağlam, a relative of Tuncer Sağlam, who died in the hospital where he was receiving treatment, said that delays in diagnosis and treatment had led to Sağlam's death. Explaining that Sağlam had been transferred from Wan to Ankara Etlik City Hospital and that, despite being unable to meet his own basic needs, there had been attempts to send him back to prison, Ercan Sağlam said:


“We have been experiencing this pain for years. But from now on, we will never accept another one of our comrades dying in prison.”


Noting that while deaths resulting from armed conflict had ceased during the Peace and Democratic Society Process, ill prisoners continued to lose their lives in prisons, Sağlam called for the immediate release of seriously ill prisoners.


‘Responsibility lies with the state’


Nurten Karagöz, co-chair of the Marmara Association for Solidarity and Mutual Assistance with the Families of Prisoners and Convicts (MA-TUHAYDER), emphasised that the right to health and the right to life are fundamental human rights.


Stating that the state is responsible for the lives and healthcare guarantees of all prisoners, Karagöz said: “The deaths of people held in the state's custody should not be this easy. From now on, no ill prisoner should lose their life in prison. The right to life is a sacred right. It cannot be negotiated. Prisoners' lives cannot be used as bargaining chips.”


Karagöz said that while people were speaking about the democratisation of society, it was unacceptable to remain silent as people continued to die in prison. She called for the right to life of ill prisoners to be protected.


‘Prisons must not be turned into places of execution’


Mahfuz Güleryüz, Deputy Co-Chair of the DEM Party, also condemned human rights violations taking place in prisons.


Güleryüz said: “Prisons must not be turned into places of ‘execution’. The state and the Ministry of Justice must immediately abandon these practices. We will continue to oppose this lawlessness, to resist it and to demand justice.”

title: Women artists: No peace or justice without women's freedom
content:
Actors Lale Mansur, Jülide Kural and Merve Asya Özgür spoke to ANF on the occasion of the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on 25 November.


The actors said that male dominance in the arts negatively affects women's creative work and visibility, while also drawing attention to television content that fuels violence. They said that men are emboldened by the failure of the justice system and stressed that there can be no justice, peace or democracy in a society where women are not free.


Lale Mansur: Male perpetrators are emboldened


Lale Mansur stressed that violence against women and femicide should be on the agenda not only on 25 November, but every day, even every moment. She said, "In Turkey, we need to talk about this five times a day. Turkey has become a slaughterhouse for women! We have reached this point because there is impunity. There is no rule of law, the law is not enforced, and there is no justice. Murderers walk among us. They search for the body of one woman and find the bodies of two more women in a well. How much worse can it get?"


Lale Mansur said that murders do not simply result in the loss of one life, but also devastate the lives of mothers, fathers and other relatives. She emphasised that the culture of impunity emboldens perpetrators, adding, "Male murderers are emboldened by impunity."


Lale Mansur also addressed the situation in the media and the shrinking space for opposition, saying that television programmes and series fuel violence: "The absence of any opposition, the disastrous state of television series... Truly disgraceful things are being produced on national television channels, including content that incites violence. They even made a television series about Abdullah Çatlı."


'Male dominance also prevails in television channels'


Lale Mansur said that male-dominated structures also prevail in the arts: "The owners and executives of television channels are mostly men. Male dominance exists there too. As for actors, many people have children to educate and support. With the high cost of living, they are forced to take part in such productions to earn money. Of course, there are very rare cases of people who refuse, saying, 'I'd rather sell lemons.' But when you have children or a family to support, you have little choice."


Lale Mansur said that impunity and the male-dominated mentality lie at the root of violence and femicide. She stressed that the problem cannot be resolved through criminal penalties alone, but requires a fundamental transformation of attitudes across society: "The biggest factor fuelling violence is impunity. They walk among us, and these people are murderers... This language, which targets and objectifies women, confronts us in every aspect of our lives. There is nothing we can tell women. You cannot say something like 'Don't let yourself be killed.' People say, 'Those men were raised by their mothers.' No, they were not raised by their mothers alone; they were raised by society. And society is now morally rotten."


Jülide Kural: There can be no democracy without women's freedom


Jülide Kural said, "25 November is a day of struggle and solidarity for women across the world against all forms of violence, discrimination and inequality. Violence is not directed only at the body. Discrediting a woman's character, disregarding her labour and will, and surrounding her with lies, insinuations and systematic attacks are also forms of violence."


Jülide Kural said that depriving women of their agency over their own lives, defining them through the existence of a man and attempting to confine them to a passive and dependent identity are among the most deeply rooted forms of violence produced by the male-dominated mentality. She emphasised that this violence is not perpetrated exclusively by men, adding, "Anyone who reproduces the male-dominated mentality and its discriminatory language can become part of this violence. Violence does not have a gender; it has a mentality that sustains it."


Jülide Kural stressed that no woman should have to prove her existence, worth or dignity through the judgements of others. She said, "25 November is not merely a day to condemn violence, but a day to confront the social and political order that produces it. In a society where women are not free, there can be no genuine democracy, justice or peace."

title: Alfred de Zayas: Why should Kurds be denied the right to self-determination? - Part One
content:
The right of peoples to self-determination is one of the fundamental principles of international law. However, its implementation remains contested because of the political and economic interests of states. The international representation of the Kurdish people, who are divided among four countries and have no state of their own, and the protection of their political, cultural and linguistic rights remain among the unresolved issues of international law.


Alfred de Zayas, an expert in international law and human rights who served as the United Nations (UN) Independent Expert on the Promotion of a Democratic and Equitable International Order from 2012 to 2018, spoke to ANF about the Kurdish people's right to self-determination and autonomy, the possibilities of obtaining status within the UN, the treatment of stateless peoples and double standards in international law.


De Zayas said that the Kurdish people's right to self-determination has a strong foundation in international law, emphasising that the main obstacle to exercising this right is political rather than legal. He stressed that the UN has failed to fulfil its responsibilities towards the Kurdish people and said that Kurds should bring human rights violations before international mechanisms, explore interstate complaint procedures and build stronger networks of solidarity within the international community.


De Zayas also strongly criticised the European Union's approach to the Kurdish question, arguing that international law must be applied equally to all peoples. He asked, "If the right to self-determination has been granted to other peoples, why should it not be granted to the Kurdish people?"


ANF spoke to international law expert Alfred de Zayas.


Mr. de Zayas, you have worked for many years within the United Nations on international law, human rights and the right of peoples to self-determination. I would like to begin with a fundamental question. What does the right of a people to self-determination mean under international law? Does this right refer only to establishing an independent state, or can it also be exercised in other forms?


Of course, the right to self-determination can also be exercised internally. If there is a federal state and a people enjoys extensive autonomy, that system can work. But what happens when a state oppresses a people who have lived on their own land for thousands of years? The Kurds are not immigrants who recently arrived in the territories of Turkey, Syria, Iran or Iraq.


If we genuinely took the right to self-determination seriously, we would ask which people have the clearest claim to this right. I would say the Kurds. There are between 40 and 45 million Kurds, divided among four states. Yet they have no state of their own.


After the First World War, they could have had their own state if the Treaty of Sèvres had been implemented. However, Mustafa Kemal fought against the French and British forces at that time. Those forces were expelled from the territory of the new Turkey. The Treaty of Sèvres was subsequently replaced by the Treaty of Lausanne, which made no mention of the Kurdish or Armenian peoples.


What, then, are the legal foundations of the right to self-determination?


You can find them in Articles 1 and 55 of the United Nations Charter, as well as Chapters XI and XII. This right is also enshrined in the common Article 1 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights. There is extensive literature on this subject, including my report A/69/272, which I submitted to the UN General Assembly in 2014. In that report, I examine the criteria determining which peoples may claim autonomy or independence.


Before continuing, I would like to mention a book that you may not know about because it has only recently been published. I supervised the doctoral thesis of a young Norwegian researcher, Blerim Mustafa, whose family originates from North Macedonia. He devoted his doctoral research to the right of secession, particularly the concept known in international law as "remedial secession".


His book is entitled Remedial Secession After the Cold War: Self-Determination and the Question of Secession. A substantial part of this work is devoted to the Kurds. The author examines three examples. The first is the people of East Timor, who were previously occupied, colonised and oppressed by Indonesia. The second is Kosovo, which …

author: Isaac Nellist
title: RAFFWU members locked out of work, rally against ‘union-busting’ Book Grocer
content:
Retail and Fast Food Workers’ Union (RAFFWU) members at the Book Grocer in Naarm/Melbourne rallied outside the Northcote store on November 21 to demand it end its lockout of workers.

The Book Grocer notified workers of the lockout at 8pm on November 20, shutting unionised workers out of their workplaces and stopping their pay at Bourke St, Spencer St, Northcote and its Tullamarine warehouse.

RAFFWU said in a media release that members had been bargaining since May for their first enterprise agreement, demanding a right to a safe workplace, protections from unfair treatment and options for permanent jobs. RAFFWU said the Book Grocer “rejected all their claims”.

RAFFWU members notified their employer on November 16 that they would be taking protected industrial action as part of their bargaining campaign, including handing out information flyers and wearing stickers to promote their campaign.

RAFFWU secretary Loukas Kakogiannis said the Book Grover had “crossed a line no retailer in Australian history has crossed”.

“Book Grocer has locked its own workers out in response to workers notifying that they would take action as small as wearing a sticker on their shirt while at work … “t has cut off their pay, just weeks out from Christmas, to starve them into giving up. That is a cowardly, vindictive attack on booksellers whose only crime is asking for fair treatment.”

Kakogiannis said this made The Book Grocer “the worst union-busting employer in the retail sector”.

“The Book Grocer would rather shut their stores and see their workers struggle to put food on the table than give them secure jobs.”

Book Grocer worker and RAFFWU delegate Fen Strangeways said the lockout would be difficult for workers. “Being locked out just weeks before Christmas is going to put real strain on our ability to pay rent and put food on the table.

“We’ve said from the start that we are open to compromise, we just want a safe workplace and to be treated fairly. Some of us have worked as casuals for ten years and just want to be made permanent.”

But workers are “not going to be intimidated”, Strangeways said. “We are sticking together.”

author: Dominic Gutoman
title: ‘Predators-in-chief’ attack ICC
content:
Former United Nations (UN) Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial killing Agnès Callamard visited the Philippines after almost a decade of being barred from entering the country.

“It begins with Duterte, in a few weeks. But it doesn’t end there,” said Callamard, also Amnesty International’s secretary-general in a press conference on November 20. “This is bigger than him. It is about the Philippines. It’s about humanity.”

When she was UN Special Rapporteur, she called for investigations into the thousands of killings under Duterte’s anti-illegal drugs campaign. The immigration ban started in 2017 and Duterte ordered that she and any representatives of the International Criminal Court (ICC) be arrested and deported.

Callamard’s immigration ban was lifted in September 2026 after years of petitioning the Philippine authorities, with the support of Amnesty International Philippines and support from several lawmakers.

“The supposed war on drugs was a slaughter that destroyed lives and families. They have carried their grief with little hope for justice and nowhere else to turn for almost a decade,” Callamard said.

Duterte is charged with three counts of crimes against humanity by the ICC for extrajudicial killings during his term as Davao City mayor and President of the Philippines. His trial is set to begin on November 30.

Human rights organizations reported more than 30,000 extrajudicial killing victims from Duterte’s anti-illegal drugs campaign, significantly higher than the official government records of just over 6,000 victims. Only five cases resulted in conviction and some of them remain on appeal.

“We had conversations with the victims, survivors, and families in the past 48 hours [with Callamard]. It is still depressing. The families have accepted that there will be no justice at home and that they are depending on what will happen in The Hague. It is very ironic,” said Ritz Lee Santos III, section director of Amnesty International Philippines. “We have a justice system here at home. The government is claiming that they are working, but the victims’ families are saying that there is no hope. There is still a culture of impunity and a climate of fear.”

These structures, both of them said, are evident in the continuing drug-related extrajudicial killings, Duterte’s children remaining in power, and the widespread vilification of the victims and their families.

Read: Women human rights defenders face rising tech-assisted violence

The United States has imposed sanctions against the ICC, banning transactions with the court to paralyze its resources and ability to operate. The administration of US President Donald Trump previously sanctioned 13 prosecutors and judges of the ICC, three Palestinian human rights organizations, and the United Nations special rapporteur on human rights in the Occupied Palestinian Territory Francesca Albanese.

Read: US intensifies sanctions vs. ICC

The United States, China, and Russia issued a so-called “peace declaration” in their first trilateral summit on November 29, after Trump’s visit in Manila, Philippines. Particularly, the ICC garnered special attention in their declaration.

“The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction,” the declaration read.

Part of the declaration is to “reform” the United Nations (UN) as permanent members of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC).

“They are the ‘predators-in-chief’ in our current system. This so-called peace treaty is about as worthless as who they are– predators,” said Callamard, highlighting their aggression in Venezuela, Iran, and Palestine. “They are attacking the ICC because international justice for them is a battle ground.”

“We are calling on the rest of the world to stand up to these predatory actions and threats. There are far more governments that ratified the Rome Statute. So in terms of the numbers, we are far more powerful than they are,” Callamard said.

In her international human rights work, Callamard said that there are less powerful governments living in fear of what the US, Russia, and China could do in their economy. “It is about economic characters being fearful of being kept out of the American market, Russian market, or the China market. And for those reasons, humanity is being thrown out. We’re …

title: Evren: Poor children pushed out of education into cheap labour
content:
The Ministry of National Education's (MEB) proposed 2027 budget, approved by the Turkish Parliament's Planning and Budget Committee on 12 November, continues to spark debate ahead of a vote in the General Assembly in December.


The ministry's initial budget for 2026 was set at 1 trillion 943 billion 965 million Turkish lira. The proposed budget for 2027 has been increased by 26.5 percent in nominal terms to 2 trillion 458 billion 762 million lira. Despite this increase, however, the ministry's share of the central government budget and national income continues to decline. Its share of the central government budget fell from 13.38 percent in 2016 to 10.24 percent in 2026 and 9.02 percent in the 2027 proposal. Its share of gross domestic product (GDP) also declined from 2.91 percent to 2.21 percent over the same period.


Of the proposed 2027 budget, 82.1 percent has been allocated to personnel expenses and payments to the Social Security Institution (SGK). Teachers' salaries remaining below the poverty threshold, alongside attempts to address shortages of permanent cleaning and security staff in schools through temporary employment programmes, have once again brought problems in public education to the forefront.


Problems in meeting basic needs at state schools persist, while private schools now account for 20.1 percent of all schools. This means that one in every five schools in the country is privately run. Meanwhile, the proposed budget of 229 billion 64 million lira for the Presidency of Religious Affairs has increased in real terms and exceeds the individual budgets of the ministries of Interior, Foreign Affairs, Trade, Culture and Tourism, and Energy and Natural Resources.


Including the budgets of the Council of Higher Education (YÖK), the Measuring, Selection and Placement Centre (ÖSYM), and universities, the total proposed education budget for 2027 stands at 3 trillion 755 billion 688 million lira.


'The budget cannot be assessed through economic figures alone'


Sami Evren, co-spokesperson of the Education Policies Commission of the Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), spoke to ANF about the budget proposal approved by the committee. Evren said that assessing the budget solely through economic figures would be insufficient. Evren said that problems concerning education, healthcare and justice in the country were directly linked to the question of democracy, adding that the government had closed its budget proposals to criticism from the opposition. Evren also said that the budget deficit of approximately 3.9 trillion lira, within an overall budget exceeding 27 trillion lira, would once again be covered by the public.


Evren said that the approximately 13 percent allocated to the Ministry of National Education was focused on mandatory personnel expenses rather than investment. Evren argued that the government's calculations, based on its own announced inflation figures, reflected a preference for capital interests rather than the public.


Evren said, "This actually means that, in real terms, the political government has prepared the budget according to the priorities of its own financial circles rather than in favour of public education and the people."


'T

he public character of education has been undermined'


Evren said that the future of approximately 17 million students, representing a quarter of Turkey's population, and 75,000 schools would be shaped by this budget. Evren argued that the existence of approximately 15,000 private schools had undermined the public character of education.


Evren said that state schools were increasingly becoming institutions attended primarily by children from poor families, creating a new class hierarchy in education. Evren also stressed that teachers working in private schools were being exploited as cheap labour. Evren argued that expanding private education meant pushing the public sector out of education. He said, "When public education is marginalised, you cannot see students with disabilities or students from poor families. You cannot address the debates about the content of education."


'Peace is impossible without education in the mother tongue'

title: Şadiye Dalkıran: Women should never remain where they are subjected to violence
content:
Dilan Aslan was murdered by a firearm in March last year by Abdulvahap Aslan, the husband she was in the process of divorcing. Following the murder, it emerged that the man had attempted to stage the killing as a suicide and had driven around the city for approximately two hours in an attempt to destroy evidence.


During her marriage in Istanbul, Dilan (nicknamed Tuba) was subjected to systematic violence and repeatedly received death threats. After witnessing her children being subjected to violence as well, Dilan decided to divorce and moved from Istanbul to Amed (Diyarbakır), where her family lived.


After staying with her family for a while, Dilan tried to rebuild her life despite threats from the violent husband, Abdulvahap Aslan. However, following his request for reconciliation and pressure from both families, she agreed to reunite with him.


On the night of 31 March, Abdulvahap Aslan and Dilan arrived in the centre of the Xana Axpar (Çınar) district of Amed and went to the house where they were staying in the Bağlar district. There, Aslan first subjected Dilan to violence and then murdered her using a firearm.


After the murder, the perpetrator attempted to destroy evidence at the scene before leaving the house. Calling a relative, Abdulvahap Aslan claimed, “My wife shot herself in the head,” attempting to make the murder look like a suicide. He then drove around the city, remaining unaccounted for approximately two hours.


Approximately two hours later, Abdulvahap Aslan went to the police station and surrendered. Following police procedures that same day, he was arrested and sent to prison.


Killer sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment


Throughout the trial, the perpetrator, Abdulvahap Aslan, maintained that the incident had been a suicide. However, neither the report prepared by the Council of Forensic Medicine (ATK) nor the indictment supported his claim. Evidence and witness testimonies also disproved his defence of suicide, while statements given by Dilan Aslan’s children during the trial revealed the extent of the violence they had suffered and the circumstances surrounding the murder.


The lawyer representing the family in the case had previously made a statement about the incident, noting that Dilan Aslan still bore signs of physical violence when she arrived in Amed. The lawyer said: “Even when she arrived here, there were marks of physical assault on her face and body. Shortly after she arrived, the defendant followed Dilan to Diyarbakır. With family members intervening, attempts were made to reconcile the two. Following these meetings, Dilan did not return to Istanbul. During conversations that took place from time to time, the same threats continued. All family members witnessed the death threats in question. On the day of the incident, the defendant also sent his three children to different homes, leaving only his five-year-old child at home.”


The case, which was launched following the preparation of the indictment, concluded last month with the final hearing at Diyarbakır's 1st High Criminal Court. The court sentenced Abdulvahap Aslan to aggravated life imprisonment for the crime of “intentional killing of a spouse and a woman”, without granting him any sentence reductions.


She lived under violence and threats for years


Since her daughter's murder, Şadiye Dalkıran has regularly visited her grave. She refused to allow the perpetrator's surname to be inscribed on the gravestone. Instead, she had her daughter's family nickname, Tuba, and her own family surname written on it, and decorated the grave with mint and flowers.


 


Praying at her daughter's grave and commemorating other women who had been murdered alongside her, Şadiye Dalkıran spoke about the violence her daughter endured throughout her marriage, the death threats she received and her struggle to build a new life.


Şadiye Dalkıran said that her daughter had married of her own free will and had four children from the marriage. Despite this, she explained, her daughter had lived under violence and abuse for years.


Şadiye Dalkıran added that her daughter had hidden what she was going through because she did not want to upset her family. She continued: “After my daughter got married, I never once saw her smile. She suffered terribly, endured so much pain and was subjected to torture. She did not tell us what she was going through because she did not want us to worry; she constantly kept it hidden.

title: Kara para aklama suçundan aranan Serdar Altınbaş Çekya’da yakalandı
content:
"Sermaye Piyasası Kanununa Muhalefet" ve "Suçtan Kaynaklanan Mal Varlığı Değerlerini Aklama" suçlarından aranan Serdar Altınbaş, Çekya’da yakalandı. İçişleri Bakanlığı, şüphelinin Türkiye’ye iadesine yönelik işlemlerin başlatıldığını duyurdu.


İade süreci


Emniyet Genel Müdürlüğü Interpol-Europol Daire Başkanlığı, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı ve Adalet Bakanlığı koordinesinde yürütülen ortak çalışmalar sonucunda, hakkında yakalama kararı bulunan Serdar Altınbaş’ın izine Çekya’da ulaşıldı. Çekya INTERPOL birimleriyle kurulan temaslar neticesinde, şüphelinin Prag Vaclav Havel Havalimanı’nın transit bölgesinde bulunduğu tespit edildi.


Bunun üzerine Adalet Bakanlığı ile koordineli biçimde harekete geçilerek 20 Kasım 2026 tarihinde şüpheli hakkında difüzyon mesajı (acil yakalama bildirimi) yayımlandı. Mesajın Çekya makamlarına iletilmesinin ardından Altınbaş havalimanında yakalanarak gözaltına alındı.


Bakanlıktan açıklama


İçişleri Bakanlığı tarafından konuya ilişkin yapılan resmi açıklamada, hukuki sürece ve operasyona dair şu bilgiler paylaşıldı:


"Yapılan incelemelerde, Serdar Altınbaş hakkında İstanbul 8. Sulh Ceza Hâkimliğince 'Sermaye Piyasası Kanununa Muhalefet ve Suçtan Kaynaklanan Mal Varlığı Değerlerini Aklama' suçlarından aranma kaydı bulunduğu, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca da hakkında yurt dışı çıkış yasağı kararı verildiği belirlendi.


ANKA'nın haberine göre, Difüzyon mesajının Çekya makamlarına iletilmesinin ardından Serdar Altınbaş’ın Çekya’da yakalanması sağlandı ve Türkiye’ye iadesine yönelik işlemler başlatıldı. Kahraman Polislerimizi, Interpol Daire Başkanlığımızı, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığımızı ve emeği geçenleri tebrik ediyoruz. Adalet Bakanlığı görevlilerine teşekkür ediyoruz."


Serdar Altınbaş hakkında bilinenler


Resmi kayıtlara ve yargı kararlarına yansıyan bilgilere göre Serdar Altınbaş; sermaye piyasası mevzuatına aykırı işlemler ve suç gelirlerinin aklanması iddiaları kapsamında İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından yürütülen soruşturmanın şüphelisi olarak aranıyordu.


Hakkında İstanbul 8. Sulh Ceza Hâkimliği tarafından çıkarılmış yakalama kararı ve başsavcılıkça konulmuş yurt dışı çıkış yasağı bulunuyordu.


(EMK)

title: Yeni Partili Aşkın Genç'ten Bakan Işıkhan’a: "Emeklinin ihtiyacı hikaye değil, geçinebileceği bir aylık"
content:
Yeni Parti Kayseri Milletvekili Aşkın Genç, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanı Vedat Işıkhan’ın emekli aylıklarına ilişkin yanıtına, açıklamayla tepki gösterdi. Emeklilerin asgari ücret karşısındaki kaybına dikkat çeken Genç, “2002’deki oran korunsaydı bugün emekli 39 bin 150 lira alacaktı” dedi. Bakanlığın 2027 yılı için somut bir aylık tutarı açıklamamasını eleştiren Genç, “Milyonlarca emeklinin hakkı, Sayın Cumhurbaşkanının gönlünden kopacak rakama mı kaldı” diye sordu.

Bakan Işıkhan’ın 2027 bütçesinin görüşüldüğü Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonunda yaptığı açıklamaları hatırlatan Genç, verilen sözlerin karşılığını yazılı cevapta bulamadıklarını ifade ederek, şunları söyledi:

“Sayın Bakan, 3 Kasım’da Plan ve Bütçe Komisyonuna geldiniz. ‘Emeklilerimizin yaşadığı ekonomik koşulların farkındayız’ dediniz. ‘İyileştirme yapacağız’ dediniz. ‘Adalet ve hakkaniyeti sağlayacağız’ dediniz. Dediniz de dediniz… Biz de size çok basit iki soru sorduk. 2027’de en düşük emekli aylığı kaç lira olacak? Milyonlarca emeklimizin aylıkları arasındaki farkları nasıl gidereceksiniz? Yazılı cevabınız geldi. 2019’u anlatmışsınız, 2023’ü anlatmışsınız, dönmüş dolaşmış yine 2002’ye gitmişsiniz. Yüzde 77’den yüzde 663’e varan artışlardan söz etmişsiniz. Sayın Bakan, biz size 2027’yi sorduk, siz 2002’yi anlatmışsınız. Ama emeklinin ihtiyacı hikaye değil, geçinebileceği bir aylık. Takvimi geriye sarınca marketteki fiyatlar geriye doğru gitmiyor.”

Bakanlığın yazılı cevabında 2002 yılından bu yana emekli aylıklarına yapılan artışların öne çıkarılmasına tepki gösteren Genç, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığının verilerini gündeme taşıdı.

2002 ve 2026 yıllarındaki en düşük SSK emekli aylığının net asgari ücret karşısındaki durumunu karşılaştıran Genç, emeklilerin yıllar içinde uğradığı gelir kaybına dikkat çekerek, şöyle konuştu:

“Madem 2002’yi bu kadar seviyorsunuz, gelin bir de o tarihe sizin rakamlarınızla bakalım. Cumhurbaşkanlığı Strateji ve Bütçe Başkanlığının tablosuna göre; 2002’de en düşük SSK emekli aylığı 257 lira, net asgari ücret 184 liraydı. Yani emekli, asgari ücretlinin yüzde 39 üzerinde aylık alıyordu. 2026’da emekli aylığı 24 bin 326 lira, asgari ücret 28 bin 76 lira. Emekli, asgari ücretin yüzde 39 üzerindeyken yüzde 13 geriye düşmüş.”

Emekli aylıklarının asgari ücret karşısındaki eski düzeyini koruması durumunda ortaya çıkacak tutarı da hesaplayan Genç, Cumhurbaşkanlığının kendi verilerinin emeklilerin yaşadığı kaybı gösterdiğini vurgulayarak, “Peki, 2002’deki oran korunsaydı bugün emekli ne kadar alacaktı? Tam 39 bin 150 lira. Aradaki fark yaklaşık 14 bin 825 lira. Bunlar Cumhurbaşkanlığının kendi rakamları. Siz yüzdelerle refah masalı anlatırken emekli her ay, ay sonunu nasıl getireceğinin hesabını yapıyor” dedi.

Emeklilerin yaşadığı geçim sıkıntısını TÜRK-İŞ’in gıda harcamalarına ilişkin verileriyle de ortaya koyan Genç, en düşük emekli aylığının dört kişilik bir ailenin yalnızca mutfak ihtiyacını karşılamaya dahi yetmediğini belirtti.

Genç, “TÜRK-İŞ’e göre dört kişilik bir ailenin yalnızca aylık gıda harcaması 38 bin lirayı aşmış. Sizin en düşük emekli aylığı diye açıkladığınız rakam 23 bin 552 lira. Tek emekli aylığıyla geçinen dört kişilik bir aile, daha mutfak masrafını bile karşılayamıyor” ifadelerini kullandı.

2027 yılı bütçesinde faiz giderleri için ayrılan kaynağı hatırlatan Genç, emekli aylıklarının artırılması konusunda bütçe imkanlarının gerekçe gösterilmesini eleştirdi. Genç, iktidarın bütçe tercihlerine ilişkin şu değerlendirmeyi yaptı:

“2027 bütçesinde faize ayırdığınız para belli, 3 trilyon 975 milyar lira. Faize gelince milyarına kadar hesap yapıyorsunuz. Emekliye gelince ‘bütçe imkanları doğrultusunda’ diyorsunuz.”

Bakan Işıkhan’ın komisyon görüşmeleri sırasında emeklilere yönelik iyileştirmeler için Cumhurbaşkanının talimatını işaret etmesine de tepki gösteren Genç, emekli aylıklarının siyasi tercihlere veya talimatlara bağlı olmaması gerektiğini vurguladı.

Genç, açıklamasını şu sözlerle tamamladı:

“Sayın Bakan komisyonda ‘Cumhurbaşkanımızın talimatıyla’ dediniz. Milyonlarca emeklinin hakkı, Sayın Cumhurbaşkanının gönlünden kopacak rakama mı kaldı? Emekli sadaka istemiyor. Yıllarca çalışmış, primini ödemiş… Emekli bunun karşılığını istiyor. Sizden cevap olarak 2027’de emeklimizin aylığı ne olacak, onun cevabını bekliyoruz.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Sultangazi'de inşaatın bodrum katında erkek cesedi bulundu
content:
İstanbul'un Sultangazi ilçesinde 4 katlı bir inşaatın bodrum katında kimliği henüz tespit edilemeyen bir erkeğin cansız bedeni bulundu. İlk incelemelerde cinayet ihtimali üzerinde durulurken, otopsi sonucunda kişinin yüksekten düşmeye bağlı boyun kırığı nedeniyle hayatını kaybettiği belirlendi.

Olay, 17 Kasım'da Yunus Emre Mahallesi'nde meydana geldi. İnşaatta çalışan bir işçi, bodrum katta yarı çıplak halde hareketsiz yatan bir kişiyi fark ederek durumu firma sahibine bildirdi. İhbar üzerine olay yerine gelen sağlık ekipleri, kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini tespit etti.

Polis ekiplerinin ilk incelemesinde ölümün yaklaşık 3-4 gün önce gerçekleşmiş olabileceği, kişinin başında ise darp izleri bulunduğu değerlendirildi. Bu nedenle başlangıçta cinayet şüphesi üzerinde duruldu. Ancak Adli Tıp Kurumunda yapılan otopside ölümün düşmeye bağlı boyun kırığından kaynaklandığı belirlendi.

Hayatını kaybeden kişinin kimliği henüz tespit edilemezken, olayla ilgili soruşturma sürüyor.

Olay sırasında sokakta bulunduğunu belirten Rüveyda D., "Saat 23.00 sıralarında polis ekipleri geldi. Sorduğumuzda, ceset bulunduğunu ve büyük ihtimalle cinayet olduğunu söyledi. Erkek ve 50 yaşlarında olduğunu da dedi. Başına vurulmuş ve yarı çıplak halde bulunmuş. Sonrasında savcılık ve olay yeri inceleme ekipleri geldi. Saat 01.30 sıralarında nakil aracı cenazeyi alıp götürdü" dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Campagne de soutien à Ali du 22 au 30 novembre
content:
Du 22 au 30 novembre 2024, la campagne pour la libération d'Ali appelle à se mobiliser ne soutien à Ali, refuser son expulsion et exiger sa libération immédiate. Le 30 novembre devait avoir lieu l'audience pour savoir s'il serait expulsé ou non mais elle est reportée.


L'audience du 30 novembre est reportée, à la demande du préfet.


Non à l'expulsion d'Ali


Nous avons été informé-es par M

e

 Kempf, avocat d'Ali, que l'audience devant la commission d'expulsion, prévue le 30 novembre au tribunal judiciaire de Pontoise, a été reportée à la demande du préfet. Aucune nouvelle date n'a été fixée et le motifs de ce report ne nous ont pas été communiqués.


Si ce renvoi retarde la possibilité pour le préfet de prendre une mesure d'expulsion,

Ali reste incarcéré depuis mai 2024 et demeure sous la menace d'une expulsion.


Ce report ne met donc fin ni à la procédure engagée contre lui, ni à l'urgence de la situation.


Notre mobilisation continue jusqu'à la libération d'Ali

 

!


Le report de l'audience ne doit pas affaiblir la mobilisation. Il reste essentiel de faire connaître la situation d'Ali, de renforcer le rapport de force et de maintenir la pression pour obtenir sa libération immédiate, le rétablissement de son statut de réfigué et l'abondon de toutes les charges retenues contre lui.


Nous appelons donc à maintenir et multiplier les initiatives de solidarité tout au long de la semaine du 22 au 30 novembre.

 ___________________________________________________________________________________


Ali est un réfugié palestinien, né dans un camp de réfugié-es en Cisjordanie occupée. À 14 ans, il voit son petit frère de 8 ans être tué par un soldat israélien.

 Deux ans plus tard, Ali est incercéré pour la première fois. Au total, il passera 8 ans de sa vie dans les prisons israéliennes avant d'être contraint à l'exil. Arrivé en France en 2016, Ali obtient le statut de réfugié en 2020 : l'État français reconnaît donc la persécution à laquelle il est exposée de la part des autorités israéliennes. Il reconstruit sa vie en France et y fonde une famille.


Pourtant, en mai 2024, Ali est arrêté lors d'une perquisition violente au domicile familial devant sa femme et ses enfants. Depuis plus de 2 ans et demi, il est incarcéré en France, en détention provisoire, sans jugement ni procès, dans le cadre d'une procédure pénale basée sur des accusations transmises par les services israéliens et son statut de réfugié lui a été retiré

. Depuis son arrestation, quatre demandes de libération ont été refusées, malgré les irrégularités flagrantes présentes dans la procédure, empêchant Ali de retourner auprès de ses enfants et de sa compagne, encore marqué-es par la violence de son arrestation.


Le 28 août 2026,

quatre rapporteur-es spéciaux-les des Nations Unies ont interpellé officiellement la France sur la situation d'Ali, exprimant de graves préoccupations sur les procédures pénales et administratives engagées contre lui et sur son maintien en détention.

 Cette lettre signifie que l'

ONU

 reconnaît officiellement l'injustice subie par Ali.


Le 30 novembre prochain,

 Ali comparaîtra devant une commission d'expulsion au tribunal judiciaire de Pontoise.

Cette commission sera chargée d'émettre un avis

 favorable ou défavorable

quant à une procédure d'expulsion engagée par la préfecture. Mais le préfet gardera la décision finale : même en cas d'avis négatif, Ali peut donc être expulsé

 

!


Du 22 au 30 novembre 2024, la campagne pour la libération d'Ali appelle à se mobiliser ne soutien à Ali, refuser son expulsion et exiger sa libération immédiate. Le 30 novembre, un rassemblement de soutien sera organisé devant le tribunal de Pontoise (3 rue Victor Hugo, 95300 Pontoise). Plus d'infos à venir

 

!

title: Termik santraller su kaynaklarını tüketiyor
content:
Fotoğraf: Özer Akdemir/Evrensel

Greenpeace işbirliğiyle Muğla’nın Milas ve Yatağan ilçeleri ile Maraş Elbistan’da yürüttükleri araştırmaya ilişkin konuşan gazeteci Doğu Eroğlu, kömürlü termik santrallerin sağlık üzerindeki etkilerinin çok sayıda çalışmaya konu olduğunu ancak su kaynakları ve suya erişim üzerindeki etkilerinin daha az incelendiğini belirtti. Araştırma kapsamında bilimsel çalışmaları taradıklarını ve bölgelerde yaşayan, suya erişim güçlüğü çeken çiftçiler ve yerel halkla görüştüklerini ifade eden Eroğlu, her iki havzada yaşanan su sorunlarını belgelemeye çalıştıklarını söyledi.

Elbistan’da termik santrallerin çalışması ve linyit madenciliği için kullanılan su miktarına dikkat çeken Eroğlu, “Elbistan’daki termik santrallere yıllık tahsis edilmiş su miktarı yaklaşık 100 milyon metreküp. Yine aynı havzada yapılan madencilik çalışmaları için havzadan uzaklaştırılması gereken su da yılda 100 milyon metreküp. Yani sadece termik santralin çalışması ve madencilik yapılabilmesi için orada harcanan ve o bölgeden uzaklaştırılan suyun toplamı yıllık 200 milyon metreküp” dedi. Kömür çıkarılabilmesi için maden sahalarının kurutulması gerektiğini belirten Eroğlu, yeraltı sularının drenaj kuyuları açılarak pompalarla dışarı atıldığını söyledi. Bu durumun özellikle maden sahalarının çevresinde tarım yapan çiftçilerin suya erişimini zorlaştırdığını kaydetti.

Yeraltı sularının çekilmesi nedeniyle çiftçilerin daha derin sondajlar açmak zorunda kaldığını kaydeden Eroğlu, “Özellikle o havzaların etrafında çiftçilikle uğraşanların suya erişebilmesi için 200-250 metreye varan derin sondajlar kurması gerekiyor. Bu sondajlardan çıkan suyla çiftçilik yapabilmek için aylık 100 bin lirayı bulan, 200 bin lirayı bulan, çok suya ihtiyaç olan dönemde 300 bin lirayı bulan elektrik faturalarına katlanması gerekiyor” diye konuştu. Bu maliyetlerin tarımsal üretimi ağır biçimde etkilediğini ifade eden Eroğlu, “En ciddi, en artık karşı çıkılamaz bulgulardan bir tanesi bizim rastladığımız tarımın, sulu tarımın bitme noktasına gelmesi, özellikle linyit madenciliği yapılan bu havzalarda. Çünkü çok maliyetli” ifadelerini kullandı.

Termik santrallere su sağlanmasına öncelik verilmesinin bölge halkının yaşamını etkilediğini belirten Eroğlu, birçok köyde insanların kendi ihtiyaçlarını karşılayacak suya erişemediğini söyledi. Eroğlu, "İnsanlar kendi hayvanlarını sulayamıyorlar, yaşamak için gereksinim duydukları bahçelere su veremiyorlar. Hatta bunları geçtim, içecek su bulamadıkları dönemler oluyor. Sular tankerlerle taşınıyor. Başka bölgelerden su satın almak zorunda kalıyorlar” dedi. Kömürlü termik santrallerin sağlık üzerindeki etkilerinin geçmişte de bilindiğini ancak zamanla bu etkilerin daha görünür hale geldiğini hatırlatan Eroğlu, su kaynakları üzerindeki etkilerin de benzer biçimde değerlendirilmesi gerektiğini söyledi. Note for readers: This is a transcript of Zimbabwean-American Zoé Samudzi’s panel titled “On A Black Feminist Anarchism” given at the Orange County Anarchist Bookfair on March 25th, 2017, in Anaheim, California. Despite the rougher audio quality from the video recording of the original panel, the folks associated in the production of “A Black Autonomy Reader” (Seditionist Distribution, 2024), a compilation of Black autonomist and anarchist texts throughout history, were able to transcribe a large amount of Zoé’s panel. While there was a Q&A section where Samudzi answered roughly 3-4 questions from the audience, much of the audience’s questions are garbled compared to Zoé’s clear answers picked up by their microphone. As such, this transcription is solely of what they said as part of her panel, not the answers they gave.

This updated transcription, done by myself, corrects nearly all omissions from the original, restores words that were left out, corrects misspelled names, and includes revisions to grammar and citations. Samudzi’s multiple “and’s” were omitted for readability. Public figures, book titles, and specific events mentioned have been footnoted, recognizing that readers may be unfamiliar with the histories and cultural contexts of what is being discussed. - AnarchoGuac

Hi everyone. I’m really excited to be here. I don’t like — I much prefer to have generative dialogue spaces than to talk at you. So I’m gonna try to keep it on the shorter side, and then we can have some more conversation on what I am trying to talk about.

In her 1983 literary work In Search Of Our Mothers’ Gardens, Alice Walker described a womanist as “a woman who loves another woman, sexually and/or non-sexually. She appreciates and prefers women’s culture, women’s emotional flexibility. She’s committed to the survival and the wholeness of an entire people. She’s not a separatist, except periodically for health. She loves the spirit, she loves struggle, she loves herself, regardless.”[1]

So I have a really complicated relationship with political theory, particularly as someone that studied political science as an undergraduate. My relationship to political theory, especially to the kind of horribly white supremacist enlightenment values of “rationality” and “objectivity” is generally, like, a knee-jerk reaction to the whiteness and the eurocentricity of it and of the canon. With regards to anarchism specifically, I often feel alienated from the theory because of the non-white and non-western globality of the politics of the ideology that have, all of a sudden, been turned into this white politic. Anarchistic values of horizontalism, of mutual aid, of voluntary participation, of non-extra or markably anti-state organization existed prior to Pierre-Joseph Proudhon’s self description of “anarchist” in the mid-1800s, or William Godwin’s framework laying work in the 1790s. title: Lo sciopero Ã¨ sociale: non câ€™Ã¨ governo che tengaÂ
content:
Oggi dalle piazze italiane è passato un messaggio chiaro: lo sciopero è del popolo. L’accordo “sindacati-imprese” sigilla un tradimento non nuovo di chi dovrebbe rappresentare gli interessi dei lavoratori e lavoratrici – perlomeno quelli che hanno un contratto, un salario, delle condizioni minimamente garantite – e invece tutela quelli del padrone. E oggi le piazze in Italia hanno sottolineato questa realtà delle cose con la serenità di chi sa che non ha più niente da perdere ma tutto da prendere. 


foto di Marioluca Barona


L’inimicizia, per usare un eufemismo, nei confronti di un sindacato come la Cgil non ha però dissuaso dal fare sciopero, anzi. Ha fatto sì che il popolo scendesse in piazza, sfruttando l’ultima delle garanzie che sopravvivono a stento in questo Paese, ossia sottrarsi dall’espropriazione del proprio lavoro, per continuare a manifestare con forza la propria contrarietà al riarmo e, quindi, al carovita. Le piazze di oggi non sono state della Cgil, sono state del popolo che dice basta. 


Oltre la metà degli italiani è contrario, secondo un

sondaggio

, all’invio di armi all’Ucraina e al sostegno della guerra. Questo è quanto emerge dai sondaggi ma ad avere occhi per guardare è ciò che viene di fatto richiesto dalle mobilitazioni di questi mesi. In fondo ciò che sta accadendo in Francia, in Italia, in Albania, in Serbia, è la riappropriazione dell’ultimo baluardo di ciò che ci rimane, ossia la possibilità di aggregarsi intorno a un’idea-forza quale il proprio territorio “nazionale” – e le bandiere italiane, la marsigliese cantata dagli studenti di periferia, la bandiera albanese ne sono il simbolo – come elemento di potere per difendere i propri interessi collettivi, di popolo. Un’identificazione che non è da leggersi nei termini “reazionari” del becero sovranismo che i Vannacci di casa nostra vorrebbero rappresentare pur facendosi finanziare dagli Stati Uniti, ma nei termini di una sorta di nuovo patriottismo, o meglio, di nuovo sentimento collettivo che respira aria internazionalista. Questo è possibile oggi grazie alla Palestina, come orizzonte dal quale apprendere il significato di emancipazione. Diventa quindi evidente, anche in queste piazze, ulteriore passaggio di mobilitazione che si iscrive in un ciclo mobilitazione diffusa, che l’unica via per difendere un interesse comune non passa dall’alimentare una guerra come quella Ucraina, tritacarne per giovani ucraini e russi, in funzione degli interessi degli Stati Uniti. Non c’è da difendersi dalla fantomatica guerra della Russia, ma c’è da difendersi da una cricca di mentecatti pronti a tutto solo per salvaguardare la poltrona. C’è da difendersi da una élite europea pronta a tutto pur di far mangiare le proprie lobby di armi e di speculazione e garantirsi il proprio pezzo della torta. Questi sono stati i messaggi di questa giornata di sciopero. 


Lo si vede a partire dal fatto che in tutte le città si sono sviluppati cortei che, o hanno preso le distanze dal principio dalla chiamata della Cgil, o hanno pensato di occupare quello spazio perché era naturale essere in piazza con i temi all’ordine del giorno per il Paese. Così è stato a Torino, dove lo spezzone sociale ha raccolto 20 mila persone che, dopo una prima parte di corteo, hanno deciso di deviare raggiungendo l’ingresso dell’autostrada per poi riconvocarsi la sera stessa per un corteo giovane e vivace che ha tentato di attraversare il centro a più riprese senza arrestarsi a fronte di cariche, lacrimogeni e idranti. Così a Roma, dove 50 mila persone sono scese in piazza e gli studenti universitari hanno sanzionato il Ministero dell’Istruzione e del Merito. Così a Modena, dove un determinato spezzone di giovani (ma non solo) è riuscito a deviare dal corteo sindacale e per poi prendere il palco della Cgil, arrivando prima della testa. Così a Cosenza, dove lo spezzone studentesco e sociale non ha concluso il corteo con la Cgil ma ha proseguito fino all’ufficio scolastico regionale. Così a Bologna, dove un corteo partecipato da decine di migliaia di persone ha raggiunto la sede di Confindustria, difesa dalla polizia che ha risposto al tentativo di avvicinarsi con cariche. Così a Padova, dove il corteo studentesco ha occupato la tangenziale, ma anche a Venezia, Trento e Vicenza dove migliaia di persone sono scese in piazza per contestare le scelte vigliacche del sindacato e contestare i responsabili del carovita. author: Marx-lover
title: Review of "Design of a Worker Cooperatives Society," by Geert Reuten
content:
This is a review of a book published in 2023.

Ancien régimes are always tenacious, but it is clear that society in its present form cannot last. Capitalism itself, as Marx predicted, is evidently unsustainable. The question is, what will come after it? Social thinkers have pondered this question for almost two centuries, and we seem to be no closer to an answer now than in the 1840s. It remains just as difficult now as then to imagine a radically different society than our own oligarchically structured one. Notoriously, it is easier to imagine social chaos or human extinction than an organized post-capitalist world.

Nevertheless, in the (overlapping) anarchist, socialist, and communist traditions, there has been no shortage of visions and sketches of a new society. In some cases, a continued role for government is envisioned; in others, society is to consist of a federation of communes and voluntary associations. Typically, the sketch of the future is not at all detailed, both because it is impossible to predict social evolution and because it is up to people themselves to forge new institutions in their struggles against oppression. Marx famously disdained to write “recipes for the cookshops of the future,” and most socialists and anarchists have been similarly reticent.

Not all have, however. Among the small minority of thinkers who have been bold enough to plan the new world in minute detail, Geert Reuten is probably the boldest. His new book Design of a Worker Cooperatives Society: An Alternative Beyond Capitalism and Socialism, and the Transition Towards It consists of an incredible profusion of detail—420 pages of it—about all the major institutions of a possible new society and what the transition process might look like. Whatever flaws the book has, it is an astonishing imaginative feat, a tour de force of imaginary social reconstruction. A former professor of economics who has previously written from a Marxist viewpoint, Reuten seems to have thought of everything, down to the organization of hospitals, pharmacies, museums, and concert halls. The book is hardly pleasure-reading, but it is so dense with ideas that anyone seriously interested in building a non-capitalist society might want to use it as a kind of reference book.

Before proceeding to the impossible task of summarizing the book, however, it may be worthwhile to express some reservations about Reuten’s project. Specifically, one can’t help sharing Marx’s intuition that writing such an astoundingly detailed recipe for the kitchens of the future is profoundly misguided. The book has plenty of intriguing ideas, but there is approximately zero chance that its grand Design (as Reuten calls it) will ever be enacted. This just isn’t how history works, from the ideal to the material. Rather, new institutions emerge laboriously out of popular economic and political struggles, as new challenges arise and people come up with new ways to meet them. Reuten justifies his book in the following terms (p. 3):

"General accounts or main lines of the organisation of a future society are in my view insufficiently convincing for most people to really see it as an alternative to capitalism... Hence, for the judgement on the possible functioning of a “worker cooperatives society” and the adequacy thereof, one needs a design of its full economic and state organisation that is blueprint-like in its detail. Detailed such that the feasibility and consistency of the design can be fully scrutinised."

But even if the Design is consistent and highly detailed, people can still object that it’s completely unfeasible because of the realities of social conflict and the messiness of society. The latter isn’t pliable enough to be molded into fitting an ideal blueprint. This was one problem with, say, Charles Fourier’s utopianism, and it’s a problem with all utopian blueprints. They’re all more-or-less unfeasible, precisely because they’re blueprints (and thus idealistic, conceived out of thin air far in advance of the era when supposedly they might be realized).

One might object, moreover, that in an age of ecological collapse, it is an oversight for a book outlining a future society not to acknowledge humanity’s grim prospects. Escalating global warming and the ongoing destruction of ecosystems might seem to vitiate any attempt to establish a socialist utopia. (And yes, despite the book’s subtitle, the society Reuten envisions is a type of socialism, in which workers …

Karar, Filistin halkının İsrail işgalinden uzak, kendi topraklarında özgürce yaşama ve bağımsız olma hakkının devredilemez olduğunu teyit ediyor. Ayrıca bu hakkın koşulsuz, vazgeçilemez, müzakere edilemez veya uzlaşmaya konu edilemez olduğunu vurguluyor.
